<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:conditioning-benchmark}
We call $(\mathcal B_n)_{n\ge1}$ a conditioning benchmark for
$(\mathcal C_n)_{n\ge1}$ if the following approximation property holds
for every fixed $p\ge2$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$.
Each state $\rho\in\mathcal C_n$ admits a set $J\subseteq[n]$,
with $|J|\ge(1-\alpha) n$, and a state
$\sigma\in\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal B_n)$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:conditioning-benchmark-asymptotic}
    \frac1{\binom np}
    \sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{n,p}\\
                    \operatorname{supp}(P)\subseteq J}}
    |f_\rho(P)-f_\sigma(P)|^2
    =
    O_{p,\alpha}(n^{-1})
\end{equation}
as $n\to\infty$, uniformly over $\rho\in\mathcal C_n$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}
Let $a_{n,p},b_{n,p}\ge0$ and $B_{n,p}\ge1$ satisfy,
for integers $n\ge p\ge2$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$,
\[
    \log N\left(
        \varepsilon,
        \mathcal F_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n),
        \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \right)
    \le
    a_{n,p}
    +
    b_{n,p}\log\left(\frac{B_{n,p}}{\varepsilon}\right).
\]
Let $\Gamma_{n,p}
    :=
    a_{n,p}
    +
    b_{n,p}\log(eB_{n,p}n)$ denote the effective profile complexity.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
    \item
    \textbf{Quadratic ground-state separation.}
    For every $L<\infty$ and every sufficiently large fixed
    $p$ depending only on $L$, the condition
    \[
        \limsup_{n\to\infty}
        \frac{\Gamma_{n,p}}{n^2}
        \le L
    \]
    implies
    \[
        \mathbb P\left(
            \Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n)
            \ge c_{p,L}\sqrt n
        \right)
        \longrightarrow1
    \]
    for some $c_{p,L}>0$.

    \item
    \textbf{Subquadratic benchmark comparison.}
    Let $\mathcal B_n$ be a conditioning benchmark for $\mathcal C_n$
    in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:conditioning-benchmark}.
    For every fixed $p\ge2$, if $\Gamma_{n,p}=o(n^2)$, then
    \[
        \frac{
            \Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n;\mathcal B_n)
        }{
            \sqrt n
        }
        \longrightarrow0
    \]
    in $L^1$ and in probability as $n\to\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:intro-circuit-size}
For every $L<\infty$, the conclusion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(i)} holds
whenever $G_n\le Ln^2/\log n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.  The
conclusion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(ii)}, with benchmark $\mathcal B_n=\mathsf{prod}_n$, holds
whenever $G_n=o(n^2/\log n)$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:intro-shallow-depth}
For every $L<\infty$, the conclusion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(i)} holds
whenever $D_n{\widehat M}_n\le Ln^2/\log n$ for all sufficiently
large $n$.  The conclusion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(ii)}, with benchmark $\mathcal B_n=\mathsf{prod}_n$, holds
whenever $D_n{\widehat M}_n=o(n^2/\log n)$.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:intro-entanglement-depth}
For every $L<\infty$, the conclusion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(i)} holds for
$b_n$-producible states whenever $2^{b_n}/b_n\le Ln/\log n$ for all
sufficiently large $n$.  The conclusion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(ii)}, with benchmark $\mathcal B_n=\mathsf{prod}_n$, holds
whenever $2^{b_n}\log n/b_n=o(n)$.
Both statements remain valid when each block may use an arbitrary number of
discardable ancillas.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:intro-mps} 
For every $L<\infty$, the conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(i)} holds for $\mathsf{MPS}^{[\chi_n]}_n$ whenever $\chi_n^2\log(n\chi_n)\le Ln$ for all sufficiently large $n$. The conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(ii)}, with benchmark $\mathcal B_n=\mathsf{prod}_n$, holds whenever $\chi_n^2\log(n\chi_n)=o(n)$. The same statements hold for convex mixtures of such MPS and when the ordering of the physical qubits in the MPS is allowed to vary with the state.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{cor:intro-magic}
The following statements hold for every fixed $L<\infty$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
    \item
    For forward magic with total width $M_n=O(n)$, the conclusion of
    Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(i)}
    holds whenever $D_n\le Ln/\log n$.
    With arbitrarily many discardable ancillas, the conclusion of
    part~\textup{(ii)}, with benchmark $\mathcal B_n=\mathsf{prod}_n$,
    holds whenever $D_n\le c\log_2 n$ for any fixed
    $c\in(0,1/2)$.

    \item
    For reverse magic with total width $M_n=O(n)$, the conclusion of
    Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(i)} holds
    whenever $D_n\le Ln/\log n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
    With an arbitrary number of clean ancillas, the same conclusion holds
    for every fixed depth $D$.

    \item
    For every fixed number $k\ge1$ of shallow blocks with total width $M_n=O(n)$, the
    conclusion of
    Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(i)} holds
    for both orientations whenever $D_n\le Ln/\log n$ for all sufficiently
    large $n$.  
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{cor:intro-t-count}
Let $(t_n)_{n\ge1}$ be a sequence of nonnegative integers.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
    \item
    For every $0\le\kappa<\infty$, the conclusion of
    Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(i)}
    holds for $\mathcal C_n=\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,t_n}$ whenever
    $t_n\le\kappa n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

    \item
    If $t_n=o(n)$, then, for every fixed $p\ge2$,
    \[
        \frac{
            M_{n,p}(\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,t_n})
            -
            M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)
        }{\sqrt n}
        \longrightarrow0
    \]
    in $L^1$ and in probability.  In this regime, for every
    $\varepsilon>0$, there exists an integer $p_\varepsilon$ such that for all fixed $p\ge p_\varepsilon$,
    \[
        \mathbb P\left(
            \left|
                \frac{M_{n,p}(\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,t_n})}{\sqrt n}
                -
                \sqrt{2\log6}
            \right|
            \le\varepsilon
        \right)
        \longrightarrow1.
    \]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:pauli-measurement-comparison}
The measurement $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Pauli}}$ satisfies
\eqref{eq:measurement-trace-comparison} with
$\kappa_{\mathcal M}=4$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Let \(Q\) denote the single-qubit subsystem with Hilbert space
\(\mathcal H_Q=\mathbb C^2\), and set
\(\mathcal P:=\{I,X,Y,Z\}\).  The Pauli matrices form an orthogonal basis
of \(\mathsf L(\mathcal H_Q)\), since
\[
    \operatorname{Tr}(ab)=2\delta_{ab},
    \qquad a,b\in\mathcal P.
\]
Hence every Hermitian operator \(\xi\) on \(R\otimes Q\) has a unique
expansion
\[
    \xi
    =
    A_0\otimes I
    +
    \sum_{a\in\{X,Y,Z\}}A_a\otimes a,
\]
where
\[
    A_0=\frac12\operatorname{Tr}_Q(\xi),
    \qquad
    A_a
    =
    \frac12\operatorname{Tr}_Q\left[(I_R\otimes a)\xi\right].
\]
Each coefficient \(A_0,A_X,A_Y,A_Z\) is Hermitian.

For \(a\in\{X,Y,Z\}\) and \(s\in\{\pm1\}\), define the corresponding
output block on \(R\) by $Y_{a,s}
    :=
    \operatorname{Tr}_Q\left[(I_R\otimes E_{a,s})\xi\right]$.
Using
\[
    \operatorname{Tr}(E_{a,s})=\frac13,
    \qquad
    \operatorname{Tr}(E_{a,s}b)=\frac{s}{3}\delta_{ab},
    \qquad b\in\{X,Y,Z\},
\]
we obtain $Y_{a,s}
    =
    \frac13(A_0+sA_a)$.
It follows that
\[
    A_0=\frac12\sum_{a,s}Y_{a,s},
    \qquad
    A_a=\frac32\bigl(Y_{a,+}-Y_{a,-}\bigr).
\]

The measured operator is
\[
    (\operatorname{Id}_R\otimes\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Pauli}})(\xi)
    =
    \sum_{a,s}
    Y_{a,s}\otimes
    |a,s\rangle\langle a,s|_{\mathrm{cl}}.
\]
Since the classical labels are orthonormal, this is the direct sum of
the six operators \(Y_{a,s}\).  Therefore
\[
    \bigl\|
        (\operatorname{Id}_R\otimes
        \mathcal M_{\mathrm{Pauli}})(\xi)
    \bigr\|_1
    =
    \sum_{a,s}\|Y_{a,s}\|_1.
\]

Finally, the trace norm is multiplicative under tensor products and
\(\|P\|_1=2\) for every \(P\in\mathcal P\).  Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
    \|\xi\|_1
    &\le
    2\|A_0\|_1
    +
    2\sum_{a\in\{X,Y,Z\}}\|A_a\|_1                                      \\
    &\le
    \sum_{a,s}\|Y_{a,s}\|_1
    +
    3\sum_{a\in\{X,Y,Z\}}
        \bigl(\|Y_{a,+}\|_1+\|Y_{a,-}\|_1\bigr)                            \\
    &=4\sum_{a,s}\|Y_{a,s}\|_1                                           \\
    &=4\bigl\|
        (\operatorname{Id}_R\otimes
        \mathcal M_{\mathrm{Pauli}})(\xi)
      \bigr\|_1.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:measurement-trace-comparison} with
\(\kappa_{\mathcal M}=4\).
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:measurement-parametrized-definetti}
There is a universal constant \(C<\infty\) such that the following holds.
Fix a finite-outcome one-qubit POVM
\(\{M_u:u\in\mathcal Z\}\) whose measurement map satisfies
\eqref{eq:measurement-trace-comparison} with constant
\(\kappa_{\mathcal M}\).  Let \(\rho\) be an \(n\)-qubit state, let
\(n\ge p\ge2\), and let the integer \(m_\star\) satisfy
\(0\le m_\star\le n-p\).

Then there exists \(J\subseteq[n]\), with
\(|J^c|\le m_\star\), such that applying the prescribed POVM separately
to each qubit in \(J^c\) has the following property.  Denote the joint
outcome by \(z=(z_i)_{i\in J^c}\), and let
\(q(z):=q_{J^c}(z)\) and \(\rho_{J\mid z}\) be defined by
\eqref{eq:conditioning-state-convention}.  

Then
\[
    \eta_J
    :=
    \sum_{z:q(z)>0}q(z)\bigotimes_{i\in J}\rho_{i\mid z},
    \qquad
    \rho_{i\mid z}
    :=
    \operatorname{Tr}_{J\setminus\{i\}}(\rho_{J\mid z}),
\]
is a fully separable state on \(J\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:measurement-conditioned-trace-error}
    \frac1{\binom{|J|}{p}}
    \sum_{\substack{I\subseteq J\\|I|=p}}
    \|\rho_I-(\eta_J)_I\|_1^2
    \le
    C\kappa_{\mathcal M}^2\frac{p^3}{m_\star+1}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
We follow the argument of
\cite[Theorem~2.5]{berta2022semidefinite}, keeping the measurement
constant explicit and truncating the average over conditioning depths.

\medskip
\noindent
\textit{1. retained qubits and conditioning outcomes.}
Let
\[
    \pi=(i_1,\ldots,i_p,j_1,\ldots,j_{n-p})
\]
be a uniformly random permutation of $[n]$.  The first $p$ qubits
are retained for the comparison, and the $j$-qubits are available for
conditioning.  Write $A_t:=i_1\cdots i_t$ for the subsystem of the
first $t$ retained qubits, for $1\le t\le p$, and write $Z_j$ for
the outcome of the prescribed POVM on qubit $j$.  For \(0\le m\le n-p\), let
\[
    S_m:=\{j_1,\ldots,j_m\},
    \qquad
    Z^{(m)}:=(Z_{j_1},\ldots,Z_{j_m})
\]
denote the measured qubits and their outcomes. We use the convention \(S_0=\emptyset\) and \(Z^{(0)}\) is the unique empty
outcome, which has probability one and satisfies
\(\rho_{A_t\mid Z^{(0)}}=\rho_{A_t}\).


For $2\le t\le p$, define
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:revmag-delta-def}
    \Delta_{t,m}
    :=\|
        \rho_{A_t\mid Z^{(m)}}
        -\rho_{A_{t-1}\mid Z^{(m)}}\otimes
         \rho_{i_t\mid Z^{(m)}}
      \|_1.
\end{equation}
This measures the remaining dependence when adjoining the next
retained qubit.  We use $\mathbb E_\pi$ for the average over permutations,
$\mathbb E[\,\cdot\mid\pi]$ for the average over measurement outcomes at
a fixed permutation, and $\mathbb E$ for the joint average.


\medskip
\noindent
\textit{2. a finite information budget.}
Fix \(t\in\{2,\ldots,p\}\).  Imagine also measuring \(i_t\) and
define the classical register $W_t:=(Z_{i_t},Z_{j_1},\ldots,Z_{j_{n-p}})$.

Let $\omega^{\pi,t}_{A_{t-1}W_t}$ be the state obtained by measuring
$i_t,j_1,\ldots,j_{n-p}$ in $\rho$ and keeping only the unmeasured
subsystem $A_{t-1}$ and the classical outcome register $W_t$.

For $0\le m\le n-p$, its marginal on
$A_{t-1}Z_{i_t}Z^{(m)}$ is obtained by discarding the later outcomes
$Z_{j_{m+1}},\ldots,Z_{j_{n-p}}$. Equivalently, we can obtain this
marginal by measuring only $i_t$ and $S_m$, retaining $A_{t-1}$
and those outcomes, and tracing out all other qubits.
These procedures agree because discarding a measurement outcome
means summing over it, which replaces the corresponding POVM
effect by $\sum_z M_z=I$.

All information quantities in this step are computed in
$\omega^{\pi,t}$ or its marginals, with the dependence on $\pi,t$
suppressed from the notation.

For each fixed ordering, the chain rule gives
\begin{align}
\label{eq:revmag-fixed-chain-rule}
    I(A_{t-1}:W_t)
    &=
    I(A_{t-1}:Z_{i_t})
    +
    \sum_{m=1}^{n-p}
    I\left(
        A_{t-1}:Z_{j_m}
        \,\middle|\,
        Z_{i_t},Z_{j_1},\ldots,Z_{j_{m-1}}
    \right).
\end{align}

We now average over the uniformly random ordering.  Fix \(m\ge1\)
and pair each ordering $\pi$ with the ordering obtained by exchanging the entries in positions
\(t\) and \(p+m\).  This pairing is a bijection of the permutation
space and leaves \(i_1,\ldots,i_{t-1}\), and hence \(A_{t-1}\),
unchanged.

For a given ordering \(\pi\), the \(m\)-th chain-rule summand for
the paired ordering, expressed in terms of the physical-site labels
from \(\pi\), is
\[
    I\left(
        A_{t-1}:Z_{i_t}
        \,\middle|\,
        Z_{j_m},Z_{j_1},\ldots,Z_{j_{m-1}}
    \right).
\]
Since the order of the classical conditioning registers is
immaterial, this equals
\[
    I\left(
        A_{t-1}:Z_{i_t}
        \,\middle|\,
        Z_{j_1},\ldots,Z_{j_m}
    \right)
    =
    I(A_{t-1}:Z_{i_t}\mid Z^{(m)}).
\]
Because the uniform average is invariant under this pairing,
\[
    \mathbb E_\pi
    I\left(
        A_{t-1}:Z_{j_m}
        \,\middle|\,
        Z_{i_t},Z_{j_1},\ldots,Z_{j_{m-1}}
    \right)
    =
    \mathbb E_\pi
    I(A_{t-1}:Z_{i_t}\mid Z^{(m)}).
\]
For \(m=0\), the corresponding term in
\eqref{eq:revmag-fixed-chain-rule} is already
\(I(A_{t-1}:Z_{i_t})\).  Averaging
\eqref{eq:revmag-fixed-chain-rule} therefore yields
\[
    \sum_{m=0}^{n-p}
    \mathbb E_\pi I(A_{t-1}:Z_{i_t}\mid Z^{(m)})
    =
    \mathbb E_\pi I(A_{t-1}:W_t).
\]
Note that this is an equality of expectations and the corresponding information
quantities need not be equal for an individual fixed ordering.

Since $W_t$ is classical, for every fixed ordering,
\begin{align*}
    I(A_{t-1}:W_t)
    &=
    S(A_{t-1})+S(W_t)-S(A_{t-1}W_t) \\
    &=
    S(A_{t-1})+H(q_\pi)
    -\left[
        H(q_\pi)
        +\sum_w q_\pi(w)S(\omega_{A_{t-1}\mid w})
    \right] \\
    &=
    S(A_{t-1})
    -\sum_w q_\pi(w)S(\omega_{A_{t-1}\mid w}) \\
    &\le
    S(A_{t-1}) 
    \le
    \log\dim\mathcal H_{A_{t-1}}
    =(t-1)\log 2,
\end{align*}
where $q_\pi$ is the outcome distribution of $W_t$ and
$H(q_\pi):=-\sum_w q_\pi(w)\log q_\pi(w)$ is its classical (Shannon) entropy.
The second equality uses the entropy formula for a
classical--quantum state. The first inequality uses the
nonnegativity of von Neumann entropy, and the second uses
$S(\omega_A)\le\log\dim\mathcal H_A$.
Finally, $A_{t-1}$ consists of $t-1$ qubits, so
$\dim\mathcal H_{A_{t-1}}=2^{t-1}$.  It follows
that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:revmag-mi-budget}
    \sum_{m=0}^{n-p}
    \mathbb E_\pi I(A_{t-1}:Z_{i_t}\mid Z^{(m)})
    \le
    (t-1)\log 2.
\end{equation}

We now transfer this information bound to the original conditional
quantum states.  Fix an ordering and an outcome
\(Z^{(m)}=z\) of positive probability.  Applying
\eqref{eq:measurement-trace-comparison}, with \(\mathcal M\) acting
on \(i_t\), to
\[
    \xi := \rho_{A_t\mid z}
    -
    \rho_{A_{t-1}\mid z}\otimes\rho_{i_t\mid z},
\]
and then Pinsker's inequality gives
\[
    \left\|
        \rho_{A_t\mid z}
        -
        \rho_{A_{t-1}\mid z}\otimes\rho_{i_t\mid z}
    \right\|_1^2
    \le
    C\kappa_{\mathcal M}^2
    I(A_{t-1}:Z_{i_t})_{\omega\mid Z^{(m)}=z}.
\]
Averaging over \(Z^{(m)}\), for the fixed ordering, gives
\[
    \mathbb E[\Delta_{t,m}^2\mid\pi]
    \le
    C\kappa_{\mathcal M}^2
    I(A_{t-1}:Z_{i_t}\mid Z^{(m)}).
\]
Finally, averaging over \(\pi\), summing over \(m\), and applying
\eqref{eq:revmag-mi-budget} yields
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:revmag-df-chain}
    \sum_{m=0}^{n-p}
    \mathbb E\Delta_{t,m}^2
    \le
    C\kappa_{\mathcal M}^2(t-1).
\end{equation}


\medskip
\noindent
\textit{3. truncate the conditioning depth and telescope.}
The summands in \eqref{eq:revmag-df-chain} are nonnegative, and so restricting
to $m\le m_\star$ and summing over $t=2,\ldots,p$ gives
\[
    \frac1{m_\star+1}\sum_{m=0}^{m_\star}
    \mathbb E\sum_{t=2}^p\Delta_{t,m}^2
    \le C\kappa_{\mathcal M}^2\frac{p^2}{m_\star+1}.
\]
Hence, there is a single $m\in\{0,\ldots,m_\star\}$ such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:revmag-df-good-m-step}
    \mathbb E\sum_{t=2}^p\Delta_{t,m}^2
    \le C\kappa_{\mathcal M}^2\frac{p^2}{m_\star+1}.
\end{equation}


For the selected depth \(m\), fix an outcome \(z\) of \(Z^{(m)}\)
having positive probability.  All states below are conditioned on the
same event \(Z^{(m)}=z\).  Tensor telescoping gives
\begin{align*}
&\rho_{A_p\mid Z^{(m)}=z}
-\bigotimes_{\ell=1}^p
 \rho_{i_\ell\mid Z^{(m)}=z}
\\
&\qquad=
\sum_{t=2}^p
\left(
    \rho_{A_t\mid Z^{(m)}=z}
    -
    \rho_{A_{t-1}\mid Z^{(m)}=z}
    \otimes
    \rho_{i_t\mid Z^{(m)}=z}
\right)
\otimes
\bigotimes_{\ell=t+1}^p
\rho_{i_\ell\mid Z^{(m)}=z}.
\end{align*}

Tensoring with a density matrix preserves the trace norm.  The triangle
inequality and Cauchy--Schwarz therefore imply
\[
    \bigg\|\rho_{A_p\mid Z^{(m)}}
       -\bigotimes_{\ell=1}^p\rho_{i_\ell\mid Z^{(m)}}\bigg\|_1^2
    \le(p-1)\sum_{t=2}^p\Delta_{t,m}^2.
\]
Together with \eqref{eq:revmag-df-good-m-step}, this yields
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:revmag-df-good-m}
    \mathbb E\bigg\|\rho_{A_p\mid Z^{(m)}}
       -\bigotimes_{\ell=1}^p\rho_{i_\ell\mid Z^{(m)}}\bigg\|_1^2
    \le C\kappa_{\mathcal M}^2\frac{p^3}{m_\star+1}.
\end{equation}

\medskip
\noindent
\textit{4. fix a measured set and average over its outcomes.}
The conditioning sites in \eqref{eq:revmag-df-good-m} are still random.
Condition first on their ordered list $(j_1,\ldots,j_m)$.  Since the
total average satisfies the displayed bound, some fixed list satisfies
the same bound after averaging only over the retained tuple and the
measurement outcomes.  Fix this list and set
$J^c:=\{j_1,\ldots,j_m\}$, so $|J^c|=m\le m_\star$.
Conditional on the list, the retained tuple is uniform among the ordered
$p$-tuples of distinct sites in $J$.  Every $p$-subset has exactly
$p!$ orderings, and the trace-norm error is unchanged by reordering
its tensor factors.  Thus, writing $q(z)=q_{J^c}(z)$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:conditioning-fixed-set-error}
    \frac1{\binom{|J|}{p}}
    \sum_{\substack{I\subseteq J\\|I|=p}}\sum_zq(z)
    \bigg \|\rho_{I\mid z}
       -\bigotimes_{i\in I}\rho_{i\mid z}\bigg\|_1^2
    \le C\kappa_{\mathcal M}^2\frac{p^3}{m_\star+1}.
\end{equation}
The same measured set is used for every $I$ in this average.

Form $\eta_J$ as in the statement.  Each conditional product is
separable, so $\eta_J$ is fully separable.  By
\eqref{eq:conditioning-average-marginal},
\[
    \rho_I=\sum_zq(z)\rho_{I\mid z},
    \qquad
    (\eta_J)_I=\sum_zq(z)\bigotimes_{i\in I}\rho_{i\mid z}.
\]
The triangle inequality and Jensen's inequality give
\[
    \|\rho_I-(\eta_J)_I\|_1^2
    \le\sum_zq(z)
       \bigg\|\rho_{I\mid z}
          -\bigotimes_{i\in I}\rho_{i\mid z}\bigg \|_1^2.
\]
Average over $I$ and apply \eqref{eq:conditioning-fixed-set-error} to
obtain \eqref{eq:measurement-conditioned-trace-error}.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
\label{cor:conditioning-extensions}
Let $\widehat\rho$ be a state on $[n]\cup E$ and set
$\rho:=\operatorname{Tr}_E\widehat\rho$. Fix $S\subseteq[n]$ and put
$J=[n]\setminus S$.

Measure the qubits in $S$ using the prescribed POVM.
Write $\widehat q(z),\widehat\rho_{JE\mid z}$ for the outcome
probabilities and conditional states when $E$ is kept, and
$q(z),\rho_{J\mid z}$ when $E$ is traced out before measurement.
Then $\widehat q(z)=q(z)$ for every $z$, and
\[
    \operatorname{Tr}_E\widehat\rho_{JE\mid z}=\rho_{J\mid z},
    \qquad q(z)>0.
\]
If $\widehat\rho$ is pure and the POVM effects have rank one,
then $\widehat\rho_{JE\mid z}$ is pure for every outcome
of positive probability.
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Write $K_z=(M_z^{(S)})^{1/2}$, using the measurement operators
on the original $n$ qubits. Since the measurement does not act on $E$,
\[
    \widehat q(z)
    =\operatorname{Tr}\left[(M_z^{(S)}\otimes I_E)\widehat\rho\right]
    =\operatorname{Tr}\left[M_z^{(S)}\operatorname{Tr}_E\widehat\rho\right]
    =q(z).
\]
For $q(z)>0$, the conditioning formula gives
\begin{align*}
    \operatorname{Tr}_E\widehat\rho_{JE\mid z}
    &=
    \frac{\operatorname{Tr}_{SE}\left[
        (K_z\otimes I_E)\widehat\rho(K_z\otimes I_E)
    \right]}{q(z)}\\
    &=
    \frac{\operatorname{Tr}_S\left[K_z(\operatorname{Tr}_E\widehat\rho)K_z\right]}{q(z)}
    =
    \frac{\operatorname{Tr}_S[K_z\rho K_z]}{q(z)}
    =\rho_{J\mid z}.
\end{align*}

Now let $\widehat\rho=|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|$ and order the
qubits as $S,J,E$.
If the effects have rank one, then
$L_z:=\bigotimes_{i\in S}M_{z_i}^{1/2}$ has rank one.
Hence, for some vectors $|v_z\rangle_S$ and
$|\widetilde\phi_z\rangle_{JE}$,
\[
    (L_z\otimes I_{JE})|\Psi\rangle
    =|v_z\rangle_S\otimes|\widetilde\phi_z\rangle_{JE}.
\]
Tracing out $S$ and normalizing gives $\widehat\rho_{JE\mid z}
    =
    |\widetilde\phi_z\rangle\langle\widetilde\phi_z|/
         \|\widetilde\phi_z\|^2$,
which is pure.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- corollary-8: body_md -->
\label{cor:conditioning-canonical}
There is a universal constant \(C_0<\infty\) such that the following
holds.  For every \(n\)-qubit state \(\rho\), integers \(n\ge p\ge2\),
and an integer \(0\le m_\star\le n-p\), there exist a set \(J\subseteq[n]\), with
\(|J^c|\le m_\star\), and a fully separable \(n\)-qubit state \(\sigma\)
such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:definetti-canonical}
    \|\mathsf M_J(f_\rho-f_\sigma)\|_{n,p}
    \le
    r_{p,m_\star}
    :=
    C_0\frac{2^{p/2}p^{3/2}}{\sqrt{m_\star+1}}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-8 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:measurement-parametrized-definetti} with the Pauli
POVM.  By Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-measurement-comparison}, its distortion
constant satisfies \(\kappa_{\mathcal M}=4\).  Let \(J\) and
\(\eta_J\) be the resulting set and separable state, and define $\sigma
    :=
    \eta_J\otimes
    |0\rangle\langle0|^{\otimes J^c}$. Then \(\sigma\) is fully separable and
\(\sigma_I=(\eta_J)_I\) for every \(I\subseteq J\).

For a \(p\)-subset \(I=\{i_1,\ldots,i_p\}\subseteq J\), set $A_I:=\rho_I-\sigma_I$. Pauli orthogonality gives
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{a\in\{X,Y,Z\}^p}
    \left|
        \operatorname{Tr}\left[
            (a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_p)A_I
        \right]
    \right|^2
    \le
    \sum_{P\in\{I,X,Y,Z\}^{\otimes p}}
        |\operatorname{Tr}(PA_I)|^2 
    =
    2^p\operatorname{Tr}(A_I^2)
    \le
    2^p\|A_I\|_1^2.
\end{align*}
The equality follows from Parseval's identity, since the normalized
Pauli strings $2^{-p/2}P$ form an orthonormal basis for the
Hilbert--Schmidt inner product.
Consequently,
\begin{align*}
    \|\mathsf M_J(f_\rho-f_\sigma)\|_{n,p}^2
    &\le
    \frac{2^p}{\binom np}
    \sum_{\substack{I\subseteq J\\|I|=p}}
        \|\rho_I-(\eta_J)_I\|_1^2 \\
    &\le
    C\kappa_{\mathcal M}^2
    \frac{2^pp^3}{m_\star+1}
    \frac{\binom{|J|}{p}}{\binom np} \\
    &\le
    16C\frac{2^pp^3}{m_\star+1},
\end{align*}
where the second inequality uses
\eqref{eq:measurement-conditioned-trace-error}.  Taking square roots
and absorbing the universal factor \(4\sqrt C\) into \(C_0\) proves
\eqref{eq:definetti-canonical}.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:revmag-hit-bound}
There is a universal constant $C<\infty$ such that, for every $n,p\ge2$ and
$0\le m_{\star}\le n-p$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:variable-budget-hit-bound}
    \mathbb E
    \max_{J\in\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}}}
    \|H_{\mathrm{hit}(J^c)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
    \le
    C\,3^{p/2}\sqrt{pm_{\star}}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
For $S\subseteq[n]$, $|S|\le m_{\star}$, write
\[
    H_{\mathrm{hit}(S)}
    =
    \sum_{P\in\mathcal P_{n,p}}g_PA_{P,S},
    \qquad
    A_{P,S}
    :=
    \binom np^{-1/2}
    P\,\mathbf 1_{\{\operatorname{supp}(P)\cap S\ne\emptyset\}}.
\]
Since $P^2=I$,
\begin{align*}
    \bigg\|\sum_{P\in\mathcal P_{n,p}}A_{P,S}^2
    \bigg\|_{\mathrm{op}}
    &=
    3^p
    \frac{
        \#\{I\in\binom{[n]}p:I\cap S\ne\emptyset\}
    }{
        \binom np
    }     
    \le
    3^pp\frac{|S|}{n}
    \le
    3^pp\frac{m_{\star}}{n}.
\end{align*}
To control all admissible sets $J$ simultaneously, we use a
block-diagonal dilation.  Namely, define the block-diagonal Gaussian series
\[
    \mathbf H_{m_{\star}}
    :=
    \bigoplus_{J\in\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}}}
    H_{\mathrm{hit}(J^c)},
\]
which is simply the block-diagonal matrix having one block
$H_{\mathrm{hit}(J^c)}$ for each admissible $J$.  The operator norm
of a block-diagonal matrix is the largest operator norm of its blocks,
so
$\|\mathbf H_{m_{\star}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
=
\max_{J\in\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}}}
\|H_{\mathrm{hit}(J^c)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. Since  $|\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}}|\le2^n$, its dimension is
\[
    d_{m_{\star}}
    =
    2^n|\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}}|
    \le
    2^{2n}.
\]
If
$\mathbf A_P:=\bigoplus_{J\in\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}}}A_{P,J^c}$, then
\[
    \big\|\sum_P\mathbf A_P^2\big\|_{\mathrm{op}}
    \le
    3^pp\frac{m_{\star}}{n}.
\]
The Gaussian matrix-series estimate
\cite[Theorem~4.1 and Eq.~(4.9)]{tropp2012user} then gives
\[
    \mathbb E\|\mathbf H_{m_{\star}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
    \le
    C\sqrt{\log(2d_{m_{\star}})}\,
    3^{p/2}\sqrt{\frac{pm_{\star}}{n}}
    \le
    C\,3^{p/2}\sqrt{pm_{\star}}.
\]
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:profile-entropy-comparison}
Fix $n\ge p\ge2$.  Let $\mathcal C_n$ and $\mathcal B_n$ be classes
of $n$-qubit states, let $0\le m_{\star}\le n-p$ be an integer, and let $r>0$.
Suppose that, for every $\rho\in\mathcal C_n$, there exist
$J\in\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}}$ and
$\sigma\in\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal B_n)$ such that $\|\mathsf M_J(f_\rho-f_\sigma)\|_{n,p}\le r$. Set
\[
    \Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n;\mathcal B_n)
    :=
    \bigl[
        M_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n)-M_{n,p}(\mathcal B_n)
    \bigr]_+.
\]
Then
\begin{align}
\label{eq:profile-entropy-comparison}
    \mathbb E\Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n;\mathcal B_n)
    \le{}&
    C
    \int_0^{2r}
    \sqrt{
        \log\left(
            2|\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}}|
            N\left(
                \varepsilon,
                \mathcal F_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n),
                \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
            \right)
        \right)
    }
    \,d\varepsilon
    +
    C\,3^{p/2}\sqrt{pm_{\star}}.
\end{align}
Moreover, for every $t>0$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:profile-gap-concentration}
    \mathbb P\left(
        \Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n;\mathcal B_n)
        \ge
        \mathbb E\Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n;\mathcal B_n)+t
    \right)
    \le
    \exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{8\cdot3^p}\right).
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
For each $J\in\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}}$, define $\mathcal K_J
    :=
    \left\{
        \mathsf M_Jf_\sigma:
        \sigma\in\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\mathcal B_n)
    \right\}$.
This is a nonempty compact convex set.  The closure is taken in the
finite-dimensional space of density matrices and does not change the
supremum of any linear energy functional.  Let $\Pi_J$ denote metric
projection onto $\mathcal K_J$ in the canonical norm, and set $\mathsf{R}_J(f)
    :=
    \mathsf M_Jf-\Pi_J(\mathsf M_Jf)$.

The dependence of these objects on $\mathcal B_n$ is suppressed in the
notation.  By the approximation hypothesis, every $\rho\in\mathcal C_n$
admits some $J\in\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}}$ for which
\[
    \|\mathsf{R}_J(f_\rho)\|_{n,p}
    =\operatorname{dist}(\mathsf M_Jf_\rho,\mathcal K_J)
    \le r.
\]
Define the class of admissible residuals
\[
    \mathfrak R_{n,p,m_{\star}}(\mathcal C_n)
    :=
    \left\{
        \mathsf{R}_J(f_\rho):
        \rho\in\mathcal C_n,
        \ J\in\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}},
        \ \|\mathsf{R}_J(f_\rho)\|_{n,p}\le r
    \right\} \cup \{0\},
\]
where the zero profile is included to ensure that suprema of the associated Gaussian process are nonnegative, as required to bound \(\Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}\) from above. The benchmark and $r$ are fixed throughout the proof.

Fix $\rho\in\mathcal C_n$ and choose a corresponding set $J$.  Let
\[
    k_J(\rho)
    :=
    \Pi_J(\mathsf M_Jf_\rho),
    \qquad
    r_J(\rho)
    :=
    \mathsf{R}_J(f_\rho).
\]
Then
\[
    \operatorname{Tr}(H_{n,p}\rho)
    =
    X_{k_J(\rho)}
    +
    X_{r_J(\rho)}
    +
    \operatorname{Tr}(H_{\mathrm{hit}(J^c)}\rho).
\]
Because $k_J(\rho)\in\mathcal K_J$, there exists
$\sigma\in\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\mathcal B_n)$ such that
$\mathsf M_Jf_\sigma=k_J(\rho)$.  Hence
\begin{align*}
    X_{k_J(\rho)}
    &=
    \operatorname{Tr}(H_J\sigma)                                                   \\
    &=
    \operatorname{Tr}(H_{n,p}\sigma)
    -
    \operatorname{Tr}(H_{\mathrm{hit}(J^c)}\sigma)                                \\
    &\le
    M_{n,p}(\mathcal B_n)
    +
    \|H_{\mathrm{hit}(J^c)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\end{align*}
Here we used linearity and continuity of the energy on the
closed convex hull of $\mathcal B_n$, together with the operator-norm
bounds
$-\operatorname{Tr}(H_{\mathrm{hit}(J^c)}\sigma)\le
\|H_{\mathrm{hit}(J^c)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ and
$\operatorname{Tr}(H_{\mathrm{hit}(J^c)}\rho)\le
\|H_{\mathrm{hit}(J^c)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}$.
Consequently, pointwise in the Gaussian disorder,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:profile-pointwise-comparison}
    \Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n;\mathcal B_n)
    \le
    \sup_{r'\in\mathfrak R_{n,p,m_{\star}}(\mathcal C_n)}X_{r'}
    +
    2
    \max_{J\in\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}}}
    \|H_{\mathrm{hit}(J^c)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\end{equation}

We next cover the residual class.  Using that metric projections onto a closed convex
subset of a Hilbert space are firmly nonexpansive, we have that $I-\Pi_J$ is nonexpansive. Further, since $\mathsf M_J$ is an orthogonal coordinate projection,
\begin{align}
\label{eq:residual-map-nonexpansive}
    \|\mathsf{R}_J(f)-\mathsf{R}_J(g)\|_{n,p}
    &\le
    \|\mathsf M_Jf-\mathsf M_Jg\|_{n,p}
    \le
    \|f-g\|_{n,p}.
\end{align}
Map an $\varepsilon/2$-cover of the profile class through each residual
map and recenter every ball meeting the admissible residual class at a
point of that class.  It follows that
\[
    N\left(
        \varepsilon,
        \mathfrak R_{n,p,m_{\star}}(\mathcal C_n)\cup\{0\},
        \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \right)
    \le
    1
    +
    |\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}}|
    N\left(
        \varepsilon/2,
        \mathcal F_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n),
        \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \right).
\]
The residual class contains zero and lies in the canonical ball of radius
$r$.  Dudley's entropy inequality therefore implies
\begin{align*}
    \mathbb E
    \sup_{r'\in\mathfrak R_{n,p,m_{\star}}(\mathcal C_n)}X_{r'}
    \le
    C
    \int_0^{2r}
    \sqrt{
        \log\left(
            2|\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}}|
            N\left(
                \varepsilon/2,
                \mathcal F_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n),
                \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
            \right)
        \right)
    }
    \,d\varepsilon.
\end{align*}
Changing variables to $u=\varepsilon/2$ and enlarging the integration
interval from $[0,r]$ to $[0,2r]$ gives the entropy integral in
\eqref{eq:profile-entropy-comparison}, with another universal constant.
Taking expectations in \eqref{eq:profile-pointwise-comparison} and applying
Lemma~\ref{lem:revmag-hit-bound} proves
\eqref{eq:profile-entropy-comparison}.

To show the concentration result, see \cite[Section 3.2]{anschuetz2025bounds} or note that for every state $\rho$, the coefficient
vector of the Gaussian functional $g\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}(H_{n,p}\rho)$ satisfies
\[
    \frac1{\binom np}
    \sum_{P\in\mathcal P_{n,p}}
    |\operatorname{Tr}(P\rho)|^2
    \le
    3^p.
\]
Thus both $M_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n)$ and $M_{n,p}(\mathcal B_n)$ are
$3^{p/2}$-Lipschitz functions of the standard Gaussian coefficient vector.
Their difference is $2\cdot3^{p/2}$-Lipschitz, and taking the positive part
does not increase the Lipschitz constant.
\eqref{eq:profile-gap-concentration} therefore follows by Gaussian concentration.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- corollary-9: body_md -->
\label{cor:quadratic-profile-complexity}
Fix $p\ge2$, and let $\mathcal C_n$ be a class of $n$-qubit states.
Suppose that there exist sequences $a_n,b_n\ge0$ and $B_n\ge1$ such
that, for every $0<\varepsilon\le1$,
\[
    \log
    N\left(
        \varepsilon,
        \mathcal F_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n),
        \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \right)
    \le
    a_n
    +
    b_n\log\left(
        \frac{B_n}{\varepsilon}
    \right),
\]
and that, for some $A<\infty$,
\[
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}
    \frac{
        a_n+b_n\log(eB_nn)
    }{
        n^2
    }
    \le
    A.
\]
Then, for every fixed $0<\alpha<1/2$,
\[
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}
    \frac{
        \mathbb E\Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n;\mathsf{prod}_n)
    }{
        \sqrt n
    }
    \le
    C\left[
        \frac{
            2^{p/2}p^{3/2}\sqrt A
        }{
            \sqrt\alpha
        }
        +
        3^{p/2}\sqrt{p\alpha}
    \right].
\]
Moreover, for every $\varepsilon>0$, with probability tending to one,
\[
    M_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n)
    \le
    M_{n,p}(\mathsf{prod}_n)
    +
    \left\{
        C\left[
            \frac{
                2^{p/2}p^{3/2}\sqrt A
            }{
                \sqrt\alpha
            }
            +
            3^{p/2}\sqrt{p\alpha}
        \right]
        +
        \varepsilon
    \right\}\sqrt n.
\]
<!-- end corollary-9 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Fix $0<\alpha<1/2$ and apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:profile-entropy-comparison} with benchmark
$\mathcal B_n=\mathsf{prod}_n$, budget $m_{\star}:=\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor$, and
radius $r=r_{p,m_{\star}}$.  Then
\[
    r_{p,m_{\star}}
    =
    O_p\left(
        \frac1{\sqrt{\alpha n}}
    \right),
    \qquad
    \log|\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}}|=O_\alpha(n).
\]
Using the assumed entropy bound and the standard entropy-integral
estimate, the residual contribution, after division by $\sqrt n$, is
at most
\[
    C
    \frac{
        2^{p/2}p^{3/2}
    }{
        \sqrt\alpha
    }
    \left[
        \frac{
            \sqrt{
                a_n+b_n\log(eB_nn)
            }
        }{
            n
        }
        +
        o(1)
    \right].
\]
Taking the limsup and using the assumption on $A$ bounds this by
$C 2^{p/2}p^{3/2}\sqrt A/\sqrt\alpha$.

The normalized contribution of interactions intersecting the
conditioned set is at most
$C\,3^{p/2}\sqrt{p\alpha}$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:profile-entropy-comparison} therefore gives the
stated bound on $\mathbb E\Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n;\mathsf{prod}_n)$.
The high-probability statement follows from
\eqref{eq:profile-gap-concentration}.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:profile-product-benchmark}
There is a universal constant $C<\infty$ such that, for every
$n\ge p\ge2$,
\[
    \mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{prod}_n)
    \le
    C\sqrt{n\log(ep)}.
\]
Moreover, for every $t>0$,
\[
    \mathbb P\left(
        M_{n,p}(\mathsf{prod}_n)
        >
        C\sqrt{n\log(ep)}+t
    \right)
    \le
    \exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{2}\right).
\]
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Let $\mathbb S^2:=\{v\in\mathbb R^3:\|v\|_2=1\}$.
Represent a pure product state by
$u=(u_1,\ldots,u_n)\in(\mathbb S^2)^n$, where
$u_i=(u_{i,X},u_{i,Y},u_{i,Z})$, with its $i$th factor equal to
$\frac12(I+u_{i,X}X+u_{i,Y}Y+u_{i,Z}Z)$.
Write $f_u$ for its profile and $X_u:=X_{f_u}$ for its energy.  On a support $I$, the vector
of Pauli expectations is $\bigotimes_{i\in I}u_i$.  Thus $ \|f_u\|_{n,p}^2=\mathbb E X_u^2=1$ and 
\[
    d_{n,p}(f_u,f_v)^2
    =\binom np^{-1}\sum_{|I|=p}
      2\left(1-\prod_{i\in I}(u_i\cdot v_i)\right).
\]
For $c_1,\ldots,c_p\in[-1,1]$, telescoping gives
\[
    1-\prod_{j=1}^p c_j
    =\sum_{j=1}^p(1-c_j)\prod_{\ell<j}c_\ell
    \le\sum_{j=1}^p(1-c_j).
\]
Consequently,
\[
    d_{n,p}(f_u,f_v)^2
    \le\binom np^{-1}\sum_{|I|=p}\sum_{i\in I}\|u_i-v_i\|_2^2
    =\frac pn\sum_{i=1}^n\|u_i-v_i\|_2^2.
\]
A Euclidean $\delta$-net of $\mathbb S^2$ has cardinality at most $(C/\delta)^C$.  Taking the product of
$n$ such nets with $\delta=\varepsilon/\sqrt p$ therefore gives
\[
    \log N\left(
        \varepsilon,\mathcal F_{n,p}(\mathsf{prod}_n),\|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \right)
    \le Cn\log\left(\frac{C\sqrt p}{\varepsilon}\right),
    \qquad 0<\varepsilon\le2.
\]
The canonical diameter is at most two. Dudley's entropy integral gives
\[
    \mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{prod}_n)
    \le C\sqrt n\int_0^2
        \sqrt{\log\left(\frac{C\sqrt p}{\varepsilon}\right)}
        \,d\varepsilon
    \le C\sqrt{n\log(ep)}.
\]
Finally, $\|f_u\|_{n,p}=1$ implies that the energy supremum is
one-Lipschitz in the standard Gaussian coefficient vector.  Gaussian
concentration gives the stated tail bound.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:revmag-ground-benchmark}
There is a universal constant $c_0>0$ such that, for every fixed
$p\ge3$,
\[
    \mathbb P\left(
        \frac{1}{\sqrt n}\lambda_{\max}(H_{n,p})
        \ge
        c_0\frac{3^{p/2}}{p}
    \right)
    \longrightarrow1.
\]
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Fix $L\ge0$ and an integer $p \ge 3$ satisfying
$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\Gamma_{n,p}/n^2\le L$.
We require $p$ to be sufficiently large depending only on $L$.
Corollary~\ref{cor:quadratic-profile-complexity}, together with
$\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n)-\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{prod}_n)
\le\mathbb E\Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n;\mathsf{prod}_n)$, gives, for every
$0<\alpha<1/2$, 
\[
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}
    \frac1{\sqrt n}
    \left[
        \mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n)
        -
        \mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{prod}_n)
    \right]
    \le
    C\left[
        \frac{2^{p/2}p^{3/2}\sqrt L}{\sqrt\alpha}
        +
        3^{p/2}\sqrt{p\alpha}
    \right].
\]
If $L>0$, set $\alpha_p := \sqrt L\,p (2/3)^{p/2}$.  Then, for sufficiently large $p$,
$\alpha_p<1/2$, and the preceding bound becomes
\[
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}
    \frac1{\sqrt n}
    \left[
        \mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n)
        -
        \mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{prod}_n)
    \right]
    \le
    C L^{1/4}p\,6^{p/4}.
\]
For $L=0$, the same bound follows by letting $\alpha\downarrow0$ for
each fixed $p$ in the unoptimized bound.  Together
with Lemma~\ref{lem:profile-product-benchmark}, this gives
\[
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}
    \frac1{\sqrt n}
    \mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n)
    \le
    C\sqrt{\log(ep)}
    +
    C L^{1/4}p\,6^{p/4}.
\]
On the other hand, Lemma~\ref{lem:revmag-ground-benchmark} gives $\lambda_{\max}(H_{n,p})/\sqrt n
    \ge c_0 3^{p/2}/p$ with probability tending to one.  Since
\[
    \frac{
        L^{1/4}p\,6^{p/4}
    }{
        3^{p/2}/p
    }
    =
    L^{1/4}p^2
    \left(\frac23\right)^{p/4}
    \longrightarrow0,
\]
and likewise
\[
    \frac{\sqrt{\log(ep)}}{3^{p/2}/p}
    \longrightarrow0,
\]
the upper bound for $\mathcal C_n$ is a strict fraction of the
ground-state scale for all sufficiently large fixed $p$.

Finally, Gaussian concentration upgrades the expectation bound for
$M_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n)$ to the corresponding high-probability bound. Thus, for every sufficiently large fixed $p$
(depending only on $L$), there is $c_{p,L}>0$ such that
$\mathbb P(
        \Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n)
        \ge
        c_{p,L}\sqrt n ) \to 1$.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Fix $p\ge2$, and let $\mathcal B_n$ be a conditioning
benchmark for $\mathcal C_n$.  Fix $0<\alpha<1/2$.
Definition~\ref{def:conditioning-benchmark} gives a constant
$A_{p,\alpha}$, which we may assume is at least one, and the approximation
hypothesis of Lemma~\ref{lem:profile-entropy-comparison} with $m_{\star}:=\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor$, and $r_n:=A_{p,\alpha}/ \sqrt n$, for all sufficiently large $n$.  In particular, $m_{\star}\le n-p$ and
$2r_n<1$ once $n$ is sufficiently large.

The entropy assumption and $|\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}}|\le2^n$ imply
\begin{align*}
    &\int_0^{2r_n}
    \sqrt{
        \log\left(
            2|\mathcal J_{n,m_{\star}}|
            {N\left(
                \varepsilon,
                \mathcal F_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n),
                \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
            \right)}
        \right)
    }
    \,d\varepsilon
    \\
    &\qquad\le
    C r_n
    \sqrt{
        n+a_{n,p}
        +b_{n,p}\log\left(\frac{eB_{n,p}}{r_n}\right)
    }
    \le
    C\frac{A_{p,\alpha}}{\sqrt n}
    \sqrt{n+\Gamma_{n,p}}.
\end{align*}
For the first inequality, substitute $\varepsilon=2r_nu$ and use
$\int_0^1\sqrt{\log(1/u)}\,du<\infty$.  For the second, use
$A_{p,\alpha}\ge1$ and
$\log(eB_{n,p}/r_n)\le\log(eB_{n,p}n)$.
Consequently,
\[
    \frac{
        \mathbb E\Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n;\mathcal B_n)
    }{\sqrt n}
    \le
    C A_{p,\alpha}\frac{\sqrt{n+\Gamma_{n,p}}}{n}
    +
    C3^{p/2}\sqrt{p\alpha}.
\]
Since $\Gamma_{n,p}=o(n^2)$, the first term tends to zero for each
fixed $p$ and $\alpha$.  It follows that
\[
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}
    \frac{
        \mathbb E\Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n;\mathcal B_n)
    }{\sqrt n}
    \le
    C3^{p/2}\sqrt{p\alpha}.
\]
This holds for every $0<\alpha<1/2$.  Letting $\alpha\downarrow0$
proves convergence of the normalized expectation to zero.  Because
$\Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n;\mathcal B_n)\ge0$, this is convergence in
$L^1$, and convergence in probability follows from Markov's inequality.
No uniform bound on $A_{p,\alpha}$ as $\alpha\downarrow0$ is needed,
since $n\to\infty$ is taken first.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
For integers $M\ge n$ and $G\ge0$, let
$\mathsf{Circ}^{(\le G)}_M$ denote the class of $M$-qubit circuits of
gate count at most $G$, with arbitrary one- and two-qubit gates and no
restriction on their arrangement.  We define
\[
    \mathsf{Gate}^{[G],\mathrm{anc}}_n
    :=
    \bigcup_{M\ge n}
    \left\{
        \operatorname{Tr}_{\{n+1,\ldots,M\}}
        \left(
            Q|0^M\rangle\langle0^M|Q^\dagger
        \right)
        :
        Q\in\mathsf{Circ}^{(\le G)}_M
    \right\}
\]
to be the class of all $n$-qubit states obtainable using at most $G$
one- and two-qubit gates, with an arbitrary number of discardable ancillas.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:gate-count-active-width}
Every state
$\rho\in\mathsf{Gate}^{[G],\mathrm{anc}}_n$ admits a representation
using a circuit of gate count at most $G$ on at most $n+G$ qubits.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
By definition, for some $M\ge n$, there is a circuit
$Q=U_L\cdots U_1$ with $L\le G$ such that
\[
    \rho
    =
    \operatorname{Tr}_{\{n+1,\ldots,M\}}
    \left(
        Q|0^M\rangle\langle0^M|Q^\dagger
    \right).
\]
Let $E_j$ be the support of $U_j$, so $|E_j|\le2$.
Starting from $A_L=[n]$, define recursively, for
$j=L,\ldots,1$,
\[
    A_{j-1}
    :=
    \begin{cases}
        A_j\cup E_j, & E_j\cap A_j\ne\emptyset,\\
        A_j, & E_j\cap A_j=\emptyset.
    \end{cases}
\]
Thus $A_j$ is the set of qubits immediately after gate $j$
in the backward lightcone of the retained outputs.
A gate whose support meets $A_j$ can add at most one new
qubit, so $|A_{j-1}|\le|A_j|+1$ and
\[
    |A_0|\le n+L\le n+G.
\]
Let $\overline{Q}$ be the pruned circuit obtained by retaining
precisely those gates $U_j$ for which
$E_j\cap A_j\ne\emptyset$, in their original order.
Every retained gate is supported in
$A_{j-1}\subseteq A_0$, so we regard $\overline{Q}$ as a circuit
on $A_0$. It has at most $L\le G$ gates.

To verify that this pruning preserves the reduced output,
fix an observable $O$ on the retained qubits and define
recursively
\[
    O_L:=O\otimes I_{\{n+1,\ldots,M\}},
    \qquad
    O_{j-1}:=U_j^\dagger O_jU_j,
    \qquad j=L,\ldots,1.
\]
Backward induction gives
$\operatorname{supp}(O_j)\subseteq A_j$.
Indeed, if $E_j\cap A_j=\emptyset$, then $U_j$ commutes
with $O_j$, and hence $O_{j-1}=O_j$.
Otherwise, conjugation by $U_j$ can enlarge the support
only to $A_j\cup E_j=A_{j-1}$.
In particular, each deleted gate leaves the corresponding
observable unchanged. Therefore,
\[
    Q^\dagger
    (O\otimes I_{\{n+1,\ldots,M\}})
    Q
    =
    \left[
        \overline{Q}^\dagger
        (O\otimes I_{A_0\setminus[n]})
        \overline{Q}
    \right]\otimes I_{A_0^c},
\]
where $A_0^c=[M]\setminus A_0$.

Taking expectations in $|0^M\rangle$ shows that the original
and pruned circuits have the same expectation for every
observable on the retained qubits.
The input on $A_0$ is itself a product of $|0\rangle$-states.
Relabeling the qubits in $A_0$ so that the retained outputs
remain the first $n$ qubits therefore gives
\[
    \rho
    =
    \operatorname{Tr}_{\{n+1,\ldots,|A_0|\}}
    \left(
        \overline{Q}|0^{|A_0|}\rangle
        \langle0^{|A_0|}|\overline{Q}^\dagger
    \right).
\]
Since $|A_0|\le n+G$ and $\overline{Q}$ has at most $G$ gates,
this proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:gate-count-profile-entropy}
There is a universal constant $C<\infty$ such that, for every
$n\ge p\ge2$, $G\ge1$, and $0<\varepsilon<1$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:gate-count-profile-entropy}
    \log
    N\left(
        \varepsilon,
        \mathcal F_{n,p}
        \left(
            \mathsf{Gate}^{[G],\mathrm{anc}}_n
        \right),
        \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \right)
    \le
    CG
    \log\left(
        \frac{
            C\,3^{p/2}G(n+G)
        }{
            \varepsilon
        }
    \right).
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{lem:gate-count-active-width}, after padding with
unused $|0\rangle$-qubits, every state in the class has a
representation
\[
    \rho
    =
    \operatorname{Tr}_{\{n+1,\ldots,n+G\}}(Q\rho_0Q^\dagger),
    \qquad
    \rho_0:=|0^{n+G}\rangle\langle0^{n+G}|,
\]
where $Q$ has at most $G$ gates.
We construct an operator-norm cover of these circuits and
then bound the corresponding error in their output profiles.

\textit{Covering the circuit class: }
By inserting one-qubit identity gates, we may represent
every circuit using exactly $G$ gate locations.
At each location, the gate acts on either one qubit or
an unordered pair of qubits, giving at most
\[
    (n+G)+\binom{n+G}{2}
    \le(n+G)^2
\]
possible supports.
There are therefore at most $(n+G)^{2G}$ support sequences.

As in \cite[proof of Proposition~10]{al2026circuit},
choose operator-norm $\delta$-nets for $\mathsf{U}(2)$
and $\mathsf{U}(4)$, with centers in the respective unitary
groups and cardinalities at most $(C/\delta)^C$.
For each support sequence, choosing a gate from the
appropriate net at every location gives at most
$(C/\delta)^{CG}$ circuits.
Taking the union over all support sequences produces
a finite set $\mathcal Q$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:gate-count-circuit-cover-size}
    |\mathcal Q|
    \le
    (n+G)^{2G}(C/\delta)^{CG}.
\end{equation}

For every circuit $Q=U_G\cdots U_1$, the set $\mathcal Q$
contains a circuit
$\widetilde Q=\widetilde U_G\cdots\widetilde U_1$
with the same gate supports and
$\|U_j-\widetilde U_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta$.
Here each gate acts as the identity outside its support.
The telescoping identity
\[
    Q-\widetilde Q
    =
    \sum_{j=1}^G
        \widetilde U_G\cdots\widetilde U_{j+1}
        (U_j-\widetilde U_j)
        U_{j-1}\cdots U_1
\]
and the unitarity of the surrounding factors give
\[
    \|Q-\widetilde Q\|_{\mathrm{op}}
    \le
    \sum_{j=1}^G
        \|U_j-\widetilde U_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}
    \le G\delta.
\]
Thus $\mathcal Q$ is an operator-norm $G\delta$-cover
of the circuit class.

\textit{Transferring the circuit approximation to profiles: }
Let $\rho$ and $\widetilde\rho$ be the reduced outputs of
$Q$ and $\widetilde Q$ applied to $\rho_0$.
Using contractivity under partial trace and $\|\rho_0\|_1=1$,
we obtain
\begin{align*}
    \|\rho-\widetilde\rho\|_1
    &\le
    \|Q\rho_0Q^\dagger
        -\widetilde Q\rho_0\widetilde Q^\dagger\|_1\\
    &\le
    \|(Q-\widetilde Q)\rho_0Q^\dagger\|_1
    +
    \|\widetilde Q\rho_0(Q^\dagger-\widetilde Q^\dagger)\|_1\\
    &\le
    2\|Q-\widetilde Q\|_{\mathrm{op}}
    \le2G\delta.
\end{align*}
Since every Pauli has operator norm one and
$|\mathcal P_{n,p}|=3^p\binom np$,
\[
    \|f_\rho-f_{\widetilde\rho}\|_{n,p}^2
    =
    \frac1{\binom np}
    \sum_{P\in\mathcal P_{n,p}}
        |\operatorname{Tr}(P(\rho-\widetilde\rho))|^2
    \le
    3^p\|\rho-\widetilde\rho\|_1^2.
\]
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:gate-count-profile-approximation}
    \|f_\rho-f_{\widetilde\rho}\|_{n,p}
    \le
    3^{p/2}\|\rho-\widetilde\rho\|_1
    \le
    2\cdot3^{p/2}G\delta.
\end{equation}

\textit{Combining the estimates: }
Choose $\delta=\varepsilon/(2\cdot3^{p/2}G).$ By \eqref{eq:gate-count-profile-approximation}, the output
profiles of the circuits in $\mathcal Q$ form an
$\varepsilon$-cover of
$\mathcal F_{n,p}(\mathsf{Gate}^{[G],\mathrm{anc}}_n)$.
Its cardinality is at most $|\mathcal Q|$, so
\eqref{eq:gate-count-circuit-cover-size} gives
\begin{align*}
    \log N\left(
        \varepsilon,
        \mathcal F_{n,p}
        \left(\mathsf{Gate}^{[G],\mathrm{anc}}_n\right),
        \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \right)
    &\le
    \log|\mathcal Q|\\
    &\le
    2G\log(n+G)
    +
    CG\log\left(
        \frac{C3^{p/2}G}{\varepsilon}
    \right)\\
    &\le
    CG\log\left(
        \frac{C3^{p/2}G(n+G)}{\varepsilon}
    \right),
\end{align*}

after increasing $C$.
This proves \eqref{eq:gate-count-profile-entropy}.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:gate-count-main}
Let $(G_n)_{n\ge1}$ be a fixed deterministic sequence of nonnegative integers.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Suppose $G_n\le Ln^2/\log n$ for all sufficiently large $n$,
for some fixed $L<\infty$. Then, for every sufficiently large fixed $p$, with the lower threshold depending only on $L$, there is
$c_{p,L}>0$ such that
\[
    \mathbb P\left(
        \Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n,p}
        \left(\mathsf{Gate}^{[G_n],\mathrm{anc}}_n\right)
        \ge c_{p,L}\sqrt n
    \right)
    \longrightarrow1.
\]

\item For every fixed $p\ge2$, if $G_n=o(n^2/\log n)$, then
\[
    \frac{
        \Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}
        \left(\mathsf{Gate}^{[G_n],\mathrm{anc}}_n;\mathsf{prod}_n\right)
    }{\sqrt n}
    \longrightarrow0
\]
in $L^1$ and in probability.
\end{enumerate}
Both conclusions are uniform over the number of discardable ancillas.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Set $\widehat G_n:=\max\{G_n,1\}$.  Since
$\mathsf{Gate}^{[G_n],\mathrm{anc}}_n\subseteq
\mathsf{Gate}^{[\widehat G_n],\mathrm{anc}}_n$, Lemma~\ref{lem:gate-count-profile-entropy}, after enlarging the universal constant $C$ if necessary, allows us to take
\[
    a_{n,p}=0,
    \qquad
    b_{n,p}=C\widehat G_n,
    \qquad
    B_{n,p}=C3^{p/2}\widehat G_n(n+\widehat G_n)
\]
in Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}.  Hence $\Gamma_{n,p}
    \le
    C\widehat G_n
    \log (
        eC3^{p/2}n\widehat G_n(n+\widehat G_n)
    )$.
Under the hypothesis of part~\textup{(i)}, for every fixed $p$,
$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\Gamma_{n,p}/n^2\le CL$, with a constant on the
right independent of $p$.  Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(i)}
therefore gives the first conclusion.  Under the hypothesis of
part~\textup{(ii)}, $\Gamma_{n,p}=o(n^2)$ for every fixed $p$.
Because $\mathsf{prod}_n$ is a conditioning benchmark for every state class,
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(ii)} gives the
second conclusion.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
The two conclusions follow from
Proposition~\ref{prop:gate-count-main}\textup{(i)} and~\textup{(ii)},
respectively, applied to $\mathsf{Gate}^{[G_n],\mathrm{anc}}_n$.
That proposition permits arbitrary circuit depth and geometry and is uniform
over the number of discardable ancillas.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
For integers $M\ge n$ and $D\ge0$, let
$\mathsf{Circ}^{[D]}_M$ denote the class of $M$-qubit circuits of depth at
most $D$, where every layer consists of one- and two-qubit gates with
pairwise disjoint supports.  Define
\[
    \mathsf{shallow}^{[D]}_{n,M}
    :=
    \left\{
        \operatorname{Tr}_{\{n+1,\ldots,M\}}
        \left(
            Q|0^M\rangle\langle0^M|Q^\dagger
        \right):
        Q\in\mathsf{Circ}^{[D]}_M
    \right\}.
\]
We write
$\mathsf{shallow}^{[D]}_n:=\mathsf{shallow}^{[D]}_{n,n}$ for the
ancilla-free class, and set
\[
    \mathsf{shallow}^{[D],\mathrm{anc}}_n
    :=
    \bigcup_{M\ge n}
    \mathsf{shallow}^{[D]}_{n,M}.
\]
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:plain-shallow-width-depth-tradeoff}
Let $(M_n)_{n\ge1}$ and $(D_n)_{n\ge1}$ be fixed deterministic integer
sequences with $M_n\ge n$ and $D_n\ge0$, and set
${\widehat M}_n:=\min\{M_n,n2^{D_n}\}$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Suppose $D_n{\widehat M}_n\le Ln^2/\log n$ for all
sufficiently large $n$, for some fixed $L<\infty$. Then, for every
sufficiently large fixed $p$, with the lower threshold depending
only on $L$, there is $c_{p,L}>0$ such that
\[
    \mathbb P\left(
        \Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n,p}
        \left(\mathsf{shallow}^{[D_n]}_{n,M_n}\right)
        \ge c_{p,L}\sqrt n
    \right)
    \longrightarrow1.
\]

\item For every fixed $p\ge2$, if
$D_n{\widehat M}_n=o(n^2/\log n)$, then
\[
    \frac{
        \Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}
        \left(\mathsf{shallow}^{[D_n]}_{n,M_n};\mathsf{prod}_n\right)
    }{\sqrt n}
    \longrightarrow0
\]
in $L^1$ and in probability.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Fix $n$ and a state
$\rho\in\mathsf{shallow}^{[D_n]}_{n,M_n}$,
prepared by a circuit $Q=Q_{D_n}\cdots Q_1$.
Let $E_{t,j}$ denote the gate supports in layer $Q_t$.
Starting from the retained qubits $A_{D_n}=[n]$, define recursively
\[
    A_{t-1}
    :=
    A_t\cup
    \bigcup_{j:E_{t,j}\cap A_t\ne\emptyset}E_{t,j},
    \qquad t=D_n,\ldots,1,
\]
so that $A_t$ collects the qubits that can affect the $n$ retained qubits through the remaining layers $Q_{t+1},\ldots, Q_{D_n}.$ The gate supports in each layer are disjoint and have size at most two. Thus at most $|A_t|$ gates meet $A_t$,
and each adds at most one qubit outside $A_t$, giving $|A_{t-1}|\le2|A_t|$. Since $A_0\subseteq[M_n]$, it follows that
\[
    |A_0|
    \le
    \min\{M_n,2^{D_n}|A_{D_n}|\}
    =
    \min\{M_n,n2^{D_n}\}
    =
    \widehat{M}_n.
\]

Retain precisely those gates in layer $t$ whose supports
meet $A_t$.
By the observable argument in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:gate-count-active-width}, deleting the other
gates preserves the reduced state on the retained outputs.
After relabeling the active qubits, the resulting circuit
$\overline{Q}$ acts on $|A_0|$ qubits, starts from
$|0^{|A_0|}\rangle$, and prepares $\rho$ on its first $n$
output qubits.

The retained gates still have disjoint supports within each
layer, so each layer contains at most $|A_0|$ gates.
Consequently, $\overline{Q}$ has at most $D_n|A_0| \le D_n\widehat{M}_n$ gates. Setting $G_n:=D_n\widehat{M}_n$, we obtain
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:shallow-gate-count-inclusion}
    \mathsf{shallow}^{[D_n]}_{n,M_n}
    \subseteq
    \mathsf{Gate}^{[G_n],\mathrm{anc}}_n.
\end{equation}
This also holds when $D_n=0$, in which case $A_0=[n]$
and the pruned circuit has no gates.

By \eqref{eq:shallow-gate-count-inclusion} and monotonicity
with respect to the state class,
\[
    \Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n,p}
    \left(\mathsf{shallow}^{[D_n]}_{n,M_n}\right)
    \ge
    \Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n,p}
    \left(\mathsf{Gate}^{[G_n],\mathrm{anc}}_n\right),
\]
and
\[
    0
    \le
    \Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}
    \left(\mathsf{shallow}^{[D_n]}_{n,M_n};\mathsf{prod}_n\right)
    \le
    \Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}
    \left(\mathsf{Gate}^{[G_n],\mathrm{anc}}_n;\mathsf{prod}_n\right).
\]
Under the hypothesis of part~\textup{(i)},
$G_n\le Ln^2/\log n$ eventually.
Proposition~\ref{prop:gate-count-main}\textup{(i)}
and the first inequality therefore give part~\textup{(i)}. Under the hypothesis of part~\textup{(ii)},
$G_n=o(n^2/\log n)$.
Proposition~\ref{prop:gate-count-main}\textup{(ii)}
and the second inequality give the claimed convergence
in $L^1$ and in probability.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:plain-shallow-width-depth-tradeoff} with the
same sequences $D_n,M_n$ and effective width
${\widehat M}_n=\min\{M_n,n2^{D_n}\}$.
Its parts~\textup{(i)} and~\textup{(ii)} give the ground-state
separation and product-state comparison, respectively, at the stated
thresholds.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
The proposition proves Corollary~\ref{cor:intro-shallow-depth} and
interpolates between the linear-width and unrestricted-workspace regimes.
If $M_n=O(n)$, it gives ground-state separation for
$D_n=O(n/\log n)$ and product-state comparison for
$D_n=o(n/\log n)$.  More generally, if $M_n=O(n^\gamma)$ for fixed
$1\le\gamma<2$, the corresponding depth scales are
$O(n^{2-\gamma}/\log n)$ and $o(n^{2-\gamma}/\log n)$, respectively.
With unrestricted ambient width, ${\widehat M}_n\le n2^{D_n}$;
more precisely, the same pruning argument gives $\mathsf{shallow}^{[D_n],\mathrm{anc}}_n
    \subseteq
    \mathsf{Gate}^{[D_nn2^{D_n}],\mathrm{anc}}_n$.
Hence the product-state conclusion holds for the union over every ambient
width whenever $D_n\le c\log_2 n$ for any fixed $c\in(0,1)$.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\cite[Theorem~13]{al2026circuit} proves a comparison with product states,
uniformly over an arbitrary number of ancillas, under the condition
$4^{D_n}D_n(\log n+D_n)=o(n)$.  The present argument gives the same
product-state comparison under the weaker depth restriction $D_n2^{D_n}
    \log(e n(D_n+1)2^{D_n})
    =
    o(n)$, which in particular permits
$D_n\le c\log_2n$ for every fixed $c\in(0,1)$.

The improvement in the accessible depth range does not come from a
stronger backward-lightcone reduction, since we use the same pruning
mechanism developed in \cite{al2026circuit}.  The difference is how the
reduction is used.  The argument in \cite{al2026circuit} controls a
lightcone-localized residual process, whose variance introduces an
additional $2^D$ cost.  Here pruning is used only to bound the
effective gate count, after which the local-profile complexity principle
gives both the product-state comparison and ground-state separation.

For circuits of linear width, pruning is unnecessary altogether, and
the gate-count theorem yields the much larger depth range
$D_n=o(n/\log n)$, with ground-state separation continuing to the
critical scale $D_n=O(n/\log n)$ for sufficiently large $p$.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
For integers $1\le b\le n$, let $\mathfrak B_{n,b}$ be the set of partitions
$\pi$ of $[n]$ into nonempty blocks $B$ with $|B|\le b$.  Define
\[
    \mathsf{blockprod}^{[b]}_n
    :=
    \bigcup_{\pi\in\mathfrak B_{n,b}}
    \left\{
        \bigotimes_{B\in\pi}
        |\psi_B\rangle\langle\psi_B|
        :
        |\psi_B\rangle\in(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes |B|},
        \ \|\psi_B\|_2=1
        \ \text{for all } B\in\pi
    \right\}.
\]
Thus $\mathsf{blockprod}^{[b]}_n$ consists of pure states whose entanglement is
confined to blocks of at most $b$ qubits.  The convex hull of
$\mathsf{blockprod}^{[b]}_n$ is the usual class of mixed $b$-producible
states.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:block-product-ancillas}
Suppose a joint state of the $n$ physical qubits and an arbitrary
number of ancillas factors across blocks, each containing at most $b$
physical qubits.  After discarding the ancillas, the resulting state on
the physical qubits belongs to
$\operatorname{conv}(\mathsf{blockprod}_n^{[b]})$.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Tracing out the ancillas preserves the tensor-product decomposition
between blocks.  Each remaining factor is a mixed state on at most $b$
physical qubits.  Decomposing these factors into pure states expresses
the resulting physical state as a convex combination of elements of
$\mathsf{blockprod}_n^{[b]}$.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:block-product-profile-entropy}
There is a universal constant $C<\infty$ such that, for every
$n\ge p\ge2$, integer $1\le b\le n$, and $0<\varepsilon<1$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:block-product-profile-entropy}
    \log
    N\left(
        \varepsilon,
        \mathcal F_{n,p}\left(\mathsf{blockprod}^{[b]}_n\right),
        \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \right)
    \le
    n\log n
    +
    \frac{Cn2^b}{b}
    \log\left(
        \frac{C\,3^{p/2}n}{\varepsilon}
    \right).
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Fix $\pi\in\mathfrak B_{n,b}$.  For each $B\in\pi$, the unit sphere
of $(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes |B|}$ has a $\delta$-net of cardinality
at most $(C/\delta)^{C2^{|B|}}$.  For unit vectors
$\ket{\psi},\ket{\phi}$, $\|
        |\psi\rangle\langle\psi|
        -
        |\phi\rangle\langle\phi|
    \|_1
    \le
    2\|\psi-\phi\|_2$. Therefore, a Euclidean $\delta/2$-net of the unit sphere induces a
trace-norm $\delta$-net of the pure states, so
\[
    N\left(
        \delta,
        \{\text{pure states on }B\},
        \|\cdot\|_1
    \right)
    \le
    \left(\frac{C}{\delta}\right)^{C2^{|B|}}.
\]

For
$\rho=\bigotimes_{B\in\pi}\rho_B$ and
$\widetilde\rho=\bigotimes_{B\in\pi}\widetilde\rho_B$, tensor
telescoping gives
\[
    \|\rho-\widetilde\rho\|_1
    \le
    \sum_{B\in\pi}
    \|\rho_B-\widetilde\rho_B\|_1.
\]
Moreover, $\|f_\rho-f_{\widetilde\rho}\|_{n,p}
    \le
    3^{p/2}\|\rho-\widetilde\rho\|_1$. Since $|\pi|\le n$, choosing
$\delta=\varepsilon/(3^{p/2}n)$ on each block gives an
$\varepsilon$-net in the canonical metric.  For positive integers $j$,
$2^j/j$ is nondecreasing.  Since $1\le |B|\le b$ and
$\sum_{B\in\pi}|B|=n$, we have
\[
    \sum_{B\in\pi}2^{|B|}
    \le\frac{2^b}{b}\sum_{B\in\pi}|B|
    =\frac{n2^b}{b}.
\]
For the fixed partition, the logarithmic cardinality is therefore at most
\[
    C
    \sum_{B\in\pi}2^{|B|}
    \log\left(
        \frac{C\,3^{p/2}n}{\varepsilon}
    \right)
    \le
    \frac{Cn2^b}{b}
    \log\left(
        \frac{C\,3^{p/2}n}{\varepsilon}
    \right).
\]

Finally,
$|\mathfrak B_{n,b}|\le n^n$, since assigning one of $n$ block
labels to each site only enlarges the number of admissible partitions.
Taking the union over $\pi\in\mathfrak B_{n,b}$ proves
\eqref{eq:block-product-profile-entropy}.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:block-product-main}
Let $(b_n)_{n\ge1}$ be a fixed deterministic sequence of integers with
$1\le b_n\le n$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Suppose $2^{b_n}/b_n\le Ln/\log n$ for all sufficiently
large $n$, for some fixed $L<\infty$. Then, for every sufficiently
large fixed $p$, with the lower threshold depending only on $L$,
there is $c_{p,L}>0$ such that
\[
    \mathbb P\left(
        \Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n,p}
        \left(\operatorname{conv}(\mathsf{blockprod}^{[b_n]}_n)\right)
        \ge c_{p,L}\sqrt n
    \right)
    \longrightarrow1.
\]

\item For every fixed $p\ge2$, if $2^{b_n}\log n/b_n=o(n)$, then
\[
    \frac{
        \Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}
        \left(\operatorname{conv}(\mathsf{blockprod}^{[b_n]}_n);\mathsf{prod}_n\right)
    }{\sqrt n}
    \longrightarrow0
\]
in $L^1$ and in probability.
\end{enumerate}
Both conclusions remain valid when each block may use an arbitrary number
of discardable ancillas.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Lemma~\ref{lem:block-product-profile-entropy} allows us to take
\[
    a_{n,p}=n\log n,
    \qquad
    b_{n,p}=Cn2^{b_n}/b_n,
    \qquad
    B_{n,p}=C3^{p/2}n
\]
for the pure block-product class in
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}.  Hence
\[
    \Gamma_{n,p}
    \le
    n\log n
    +
    \frac{Cn2^{b_n}}{b_n}
    \log\left(eC3^{p/2}n^2\right).
\]
Under the hypothesis of part~\textup{(i)},
$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\Gamma_{n,p}/n^2\le CL$ for every fixed $p$,
with a constant independent of $p$.  Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(i)}
therefore gives ground-state separation.  Under the hypothesis of
part~\textup{(ii)}, $\Gamma_{n,p}=o(n^2)$ for every fixed $p$, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(ii)}, with
benchmark $\mathcal B_n=\mathsf{prod}_n$, gives the product-state comparison.

Passing to the convex hull does not change the maximal energy, since the objective is linear.  Finally, the extension to arbitrary
discardable ancillas follows from
Lemma~\ref{lem:block-product-ancillas}.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
The class of $b_n$-producible states is
$\operatorname{conv}(\mathsf{blockprod}^{[b_n]}_n)$.
Both conclusions therefore follow from
Proposition~\ref{prop:block-product-main}.
The extension to arbitrary discardable ancillas within each block is
included there by Lemma~\ref{lem:block-product-ancillas}.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:mps-profile-entropy}
There is a universal constant $C<\infty$ such that, for every
$n\ge p\ge2$, $\chi\ge1$, and $0<\varepsilon<1$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:mps-profile-entropy}
\log N\left(
    \varepsilon,
    \mathcal F_{n,p}\left(\mathsf{MPS}^{[\chi]}_n\right),
    \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
\right)
\le
C n\chi^2
\log\left(
    \frac{C\,3^{p/2}n\chi}{\varepsilon}
\right).
\end{equation}
The same estimate holds with an added $O(n\log n)$ term if the ordering of
the physical qubits is also allowed to vary.
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Assume first a fixed ordering of the qubits and a sequence of bond dimensions $\chi_1, \dots, \chi_n$ where $\chi_0=\chi_n=1$ and $\chi_j\le\chi$.
The Schmidt rank across a cut at site $j$ is at most $\chi_j$.

Every state in $\mathsf{MPS}^{[\chi]}_n$ can be put into a canonical form where the state is generated by a sequence of isometries (see \cite[Theorem~1 and Section~5.1]{perez2006matrix})
\[
    V_j:\mathbb C^{\chi_{j-1}}
    \longrightarrow
    \mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^{\chi_j},
    \qquad
    \chi_0=\chi_n=1,
    \quad
    \chi_j\le\chi.
\]
More specifically, in this canonical form, matrices may be chosen so that $\sum_{x=0}^1 A_x^{[j]}A_x^{[j]\dagger} = I_{\chi_{j-1}}$.

We now construct a $\delta$-net in operator norm for the possible isometries at each site.  The matrix $V_j$ is a $(2\chi_j)\times\chi_{j-1}$ matrix, and therefore belongs to a real vector space of dimension $d_j\le 4\chi^2$. Furthermore, $\|V_j\|_F \le  \sqrt\chi$ since columns of $V_j$ are orthonormal.
Let $\mathcal I_j$ denote the set of admissible isometries at site $j$,
viewed as a subset of this real Euclidean space.  Choose a maximal
$\delta$-separated subset $\mathcal N_j\subseteq\mathcal I_j$ in
Frobenius norm so that $\mathcal N_j$ is a $\delta$-net.
Using the standard packing and covering bounds from~\cite[Lemma~4.2.8 and Proposition~4.2.12]{vershynin2018high}, for $0<\delta<1$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
    |\mathcal N_j| &\le \left(1+\frac{2\sqrt\chi}{\delta}\right)^{d_j} \le \left( \frac{C\sqrt\chi}{\delta}\right)^{4\chi^2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since $\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|A\|_F$, this is also a
$\delta$-net in operator norm.

If two sequential representations satisfy
$\|V_j-\widetilde V_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta$ at every site, telescoping
through the isometries gives
\[
    \bigl\||\psi\rangle-|\widetilde\psi\rangle\bigr\|_2
    \le n\delta,
    \qquad
    \bigl\|
      |\psi\rangle\langle\psi|
      -|\widetilde\psi\rangle\langle\widetilde\psi|
    \bigr\|_1
    \le2n\delta.
\]
Since $\|f_\rho-f_\sigma\|_{n,p}
    \le3^{p/2}\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$, we choose $\delta=\varepsilon/(2\,3^{p/2}n)$.  Multiplying the tensor nets over
all sites gives logarithmic cardinality
$Cn\chi^2\log(C3^{p/2}n\chi/\varepsilon)$.  Finally, there are at most
$\chi^{n-1}$ choices of dimension in the sequences, and at most $n!$ possible site orderings if these are included.  Absorbing these additional terms proves the result.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:mps-energy}
Let $(\chi_n)_{n\ge1}$ be a fixed deterministic sequence of bond dimensions.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Suppose $\chi_n^2\log(n\chi_n)\le Ln$ for all sufficiently
large $n$, for some fixed $L<\infty$. Then there exists $p_0=p_0(L)$ such that, for every fixed $p\ge p_0$, there is $c_{p,L}>0$ for which
\[
    \mathbb P\left(
        \Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n,p}
        \left(\mathsf{MPS}^{[\chi_n]}_n\right)
        \ge c_{p,L}\sqrt n
    \right)
    \longrightarrow1.
\]

\item For every fixed $p\ge2$, if $\chi_n^2\log(n\chi_n)=o(n)$,
then
\[
    \frac{
        \Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}
        \left(\mathsf{MPS}^{[\chi_n]}_n;\mathsf{prod}_n\right)
    }{\sqrt n}
    \longrightarrow0
\]
in $L^1$ and in probability.
\end{enumerate}
The same conclusions hold for the convex hull of the MPS class and for the
union over all one-dimensional orderings.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Lemma~\ref{lem:mps-profile-entropy} gives $\Gamma_{n,p}
    \le
    Cn\chi_n^2
    \log\left(eC3^{p/2}n^2\chi_n\right)$. If $\chi_n^2\log(n\chi_n)\le Ln$, then, for every fixed $p$,
$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\Gamma_{n,p}/n^2\le CL$, where the constant is
independent of $p$; the fixed factor $3^{p/2}$ contributes only an additive
constant inside the logarithm.  This proves part~\textup{(i)} by
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(i)}.  If
$\chi_n^2\log(n\chi_n)=o(n)$, then $\Gamma_{n,p}=o(n^2)$ for every
fixed $p$, and Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(ii)},
with benchmark $\mathcal B_n=\mathsf{prod}_n$, proves part~\textup{(ii)}.
Optimizing over the convex hull does not change the optimum of the
Hamiltonian objective, and the additional $O(n\log n)$ entropy from varying the ordering of sites is negligible in both regimes.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Both conclusions follow from Proposition~\ref{prop:mps-energy}.
Its final assertion also includes convex mixtures of the MPS class and
the union over all orderings of the physical qubits, so the ordering may
vary with the state.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
The same telescoping argument applies to other
tensor networks with fixed architectures.  A binary one-dimensional MERA of bond dimension $\chi$ has
$O(n)$ tensors, while each disentangler or isometry lies in an ambient matrix
space of real dimension at most $O(\chi^4)$ \cite{vidal2008class}.
Write $\mathsf{MERA}^{[\chi]}_n$ for the class of normalized states
represented by such networks with a fixed architecture and bond
dimension at most $\chi$.  Consequently,
\[
\log N\left(
    \varepsilon,
    \mathcal F_{n,p}\left(\mathsf{MERA}^{[\chi]}_n\right),
    \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
\right)
\le
C n\chi^4
\log\left(
    \frac{C\,3^{p/2}n\chi}{\varepsilon}
\right).
\]
Thus fixed bond dimension MERA also have no asymptotic advantage
over product states, and the preceding corollary extends with $\chi_n^2$
replaced by $\chi_n^4$.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
\label{def:forward-reverse-magic}
For integers $M\ge1$ and $D\ge1$, define
\[
    \mathsf{mag}^{[D]}_M
    :=
    \left\{
        QC|0^M\rangle\langle0^M|C^\dagger Q^\dagger:
        C\in\mathsf{cliff}_M,\;
        Q\in\mathsf{Circ}^{[D]}_M
    \right\}
\]
and
\[
    \mathsf{revmag}^{[D]}_M
    :=
    \left\{
        CQ|0^M\rangle\langle0^M|Q^\dagger C^\dagger:
        C\in\mathsf{cliff}_M,\;
        Q\in\mathsf{Circ}^{[D]}_M
    \right\}.
\]
For $M\ge n$, define their reduced-output classes by
\[
    \begin{aligned}
        \mathsf{mag}^{[D]}_{n,M-n}
        &:=
        \left\{
            \operatorname{Tr}_{\{n+1,\ldots,M\}}(\rho):
            \rho\in\mathsf{mag}^{[D]}_M
        \right\},\\
        \mathsf{revmag}^{[D]}_{n,M-n}
        &:=
        \left\{
            \operatorname{Tr}_{\{n+1,\ldots,M\}}(\rho):
            \rho\in\mathsf{revmag}^{[D]}_M
        \right\}.
    \end{aligned}
\]
Here $M$ is the total width, and the $M-n$ ancillary qubits may be
discarded.  Taking $M=n$ recovers the classes without ancillas.
We also set
\[
    \mathsf{mag}^{[D],\mathrm{anc}}_n
    :=
    \bigcup_{M\ge n}\mathsf{mag}^{[D]}_{n,M-n}.
\]
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
\label{def:higher-magic-levels}
For integers $M,k,D\ge1$, define
\[
    \mathsf{mag}^{[D,k]}_M
    :=
    \left\{
        U\ket{0^M}\bra{0^M}U^\dagger:
        U=Q_kC_{k-1}\cdots Q_1C_0,\;
        C_0,\ldots,C_{k-1}\in\mathsf{cliff}_M,\;
        Q_1,\ldots,Q_k\in\mathsf{Circ}^{[D]}_M
    \right\}
\]
and
\[
    \mathsf{revmag}^{[D,k]}_M
    :=
    \left\{
        U\ket{0^M}\bra{0^M}U^\dagger:
        U=C_kQ_k\cdots C_1Q_1,\;
        C_1,\ldots,C_k\in\mathsf{cliff}_M,\;
        Q_1,\ldots,Q_k\in\mathsf{Circ}^{[D]}_M
    \right\}.
\]
For $n\ge1$ and $r\ge0$, define the reduced-output classes by
\[
    \begin{aligned}
        \mathsf{mag}^{[D]}_{n,k,r}
        &:=
        \left\{
            \operatorname{Tr}_{\{n+1,\ldots,n+r\}}(\rho):
            \rho\in\mathsf{mag}^{[D,k]}_{n+r}
        \right\},\\
        \mathsf{revmag}^{[D]}_{n,k,r}
        &:=
        \left\{
            \operatorname{Tr}_{\{n+1,\ldots,n+r\}}(\rho):
            \rho\in\mathsf{revmag}^{[D,k]}_{n+r}
        \right\}.
    \end{aligned}
\]
Thus $k$ counts the shallow blocks, the total width is $M=n+r$,
and all $r$ ancillas may be discarded. For $k=1$, these agree
with $\mathsf{mag}^{[D]}_{n,r}$ and $\mathsf{revmag}^{[D]}_{n,r}$,
respectively.
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
\label{rem:higher-parham-notation}
With depth at most $D$ imposed on each shallow block,
$\mathsf{mag}^{[D,k]}_M$ and $\mathsf{revmag}^{[D,k]}_M$
are the output density-matrix classes corresponding to
$\mathcal A_{CQ}^{2k-1}$ and $\mathcal A_{QC}^{2k-1}$
in \cite{parham2026quantum}, respectively.

At even level $2k$, suppose again that every shallow
block has depth at most $D$.
A circuit in the $CQ$ orientation begins and ends with
a Clifford block. Appending an identity shallow block
therefore places its output density matrix in
$\mathsf{mag}^{[D,k+1]}_M$.
Similarly, a circuit in the $QC$ orientation begins and
ends with a shallow block. Appending an identity Clifford
block places its output density matrix in
$\mathsf{revmag}^{[D,k+1]}_M$.
For $M=n+r$, discarding the last $r$ qubits gives states
in $\mathsf{mag}^{[D]}_{n,k+1,r}$ and
$\mathsf{revmag}^{[D]}_{n,k+1,r}$, respectively.

Parham's hierarchy is defined for circuit families
admitting some constant shallow-depth bound, independent
of the number of qubits. Each such family therefore
satisfies the depth restriction above for a suitable
fixed $D$. Consequently, our bounds for every fixed
number of rounds apply to both orientations at every
fixed level, under the stated restrictions on circuit
width.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:higher-magic-entropy}
There is a universal constant $C<\infty$ such that, for all integers
$M\ge n\ge p\ge2$, $k,D\ge1$, and all $0<\varepsilon<1$,
\[
    \log N\left(
        \varepsilon,
        \mathcal F_{n,p}
        \left(
            \mathsf{mag}^{[D]}_{n,k,M-n}
            \cup
            \mathsf{revmag}^{[D]}_{n,k,M-n}
        \right),
        \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \right)
    \le
    CkM^2
    +
    CkDM
    \log\left(
        \frac{C3^{p/2}kDM}{\varepsilon}
    \right).
\]
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
In either orientation, the preparation circuit contains $k$
Clifford blocks and $k$ shallow blocks. We construct a finite
cover of these circuits and then show that their reduced-output
profiles form the required cover.

We first count the possible choices of Clifford blocks. Identifying unitaries that differ only by a global phase,
the number of $M$-qubit Clifford operations is
\[
    |\mathsf{cliff}_M|
    =
    2^{M^2+2M}\prod_{j=1}^M(4^j-1)
    \le
    \exp(CM^2);
\]
see \cite[Equation~(1)]{koenig2014efficiently}. Choosing one Clifford operation for each of the $k$ blocks
therefore gives at most
$|\mathsf{cliff}_M|^k\le\exp(CkM^2)$ possibilities.
For each operation, we fix a representative unitary matrix.
The choice of global phase does not affect the output density
matrix.

An architecture specifies the gate locations in each layer.
For each qubit, there are three possibilities: it participates
in a two-qubit gate, in which case there are $M-1$ choices
for the other qubit; it has a one-qubit gate; or it has no gate.
Thus there are
\[
    (M-1)+1+1=M+1
\]
possible labels per qubit.
Every valid layer determines such a labeling, so there are
at most $(M+1)^M$ layer architectures.
Padding each shallow block with identity layers gives $kD$
layers in total, and hence at most $(M+1)^{kDM}$ choices
of their architectures.
Finally, disjointness of the gate supports implies that
each layer has at most $M$ gates, giving at most $kDM$
local gate locations in total.

We now construct an operator-norm cover of the preparation
circuits. Fix $0<\delta<1$.
As in Lemma~\ref{lem:gate-count-profile-entropy}, choose
operator-norm $\delta$-nets for $\mathsf U(2)$ and
$\mathsf U(4)$, with centers in the respective unitary groups
and cardinalities at most $(C/\delta)^C$.
For each choice of Clifford blocks and matching architectures,
approximate every local gate by a point in the corresponding
net, keeping the Clifford blocks unchanged.
Since there are at most $kDM$ local gates, this gives at most
$(C/\delta)^{CkDM}$ approximating circuits for each such choice.
Taking the union over all Clifford blocks, architectures,
and both orientations gives a finite set $\mathcal U$
of circuits satisfying
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:higher-magic-circuit-cover-size}
    |\mathcal U|
    \le
    2\exp(CkM^2)
    (M+1)^{kDM}
    (C/\delta)^{CkDM}.
\end{equation}
For every preparation circuit $U$, the set $\mathcal U$
contains a circuit $\widetilde U$ with the same Clifford
blocks and matching architectures, and with corresponding
local gates differing by at most $\delta$.

To bound the covering radius, let $Q_i$ and $\widetilde Q_i$
be the corresponding shallow blocks of $U$ and $\widetilde U$.
Each contains at most $DM$ local gates.
The telescoping estimate in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:gate-count-profile-entropy} therefore gives
\[
    \|Q_i-\widetilde Q_i\|_{\mathrm{op}}
    \le DM\delta,
    \qquad i=1,\ldots,k.
\]
Replacing the shallow blocks one at a time in the full
preparation circuit, all surrounding factors are unitary
and the Clifford blocks remain unchanged. Hence
\[
    \|U-\widetilde U\|_{\mathrm{op}}
    \le
    \sum_{i=1}^k
        \|Q_i-\widetilde Q_i\|_{\mathrm{op}}
    \le
    kDM\delta.
\]
Thus $\mathcal U$ is an operator-norm $kDM\delta$-cover
of the preparation circuits with the chosen Clifford
representatives.

We now transfer this circuit approximation to the output
profiles. Let $\rho$ and $\widetilde\rho$ be the reduced
