outputs on the first $n$ qubits obtained by applying
$U$ and $\widetilde U$ to the same input $|0^M\rangle$.
The trace-distance and profile estimates in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:gate-count-profile-entropy} give
\[
    \|\rho-\widetilde\rho\|_1
    \le
    2\|U-\widetilde U\|_{\mathrm{op}}
    \le
    2kDM\delta
\]
and consequently
\[
    \|f_\rho-f_{\widetilde\rho}\|_{n,p}
    \le
    3^{p/2}\|\rho-\widetilde\rho\|_1
    \le
    2\cdot3^{p/2}kDM\delta.
\]
Taking $\delta = \varepsilon/(2\cdot3^{p/2}kDM)$ therefore ensures that every target profile is within
$\varepsilon$ of the reduced-output profile of a circuit
in $\mathcal U$.
These profiles form an $\varepsilon$-cover of the target
class with cardinality at most $|\mathcal U|$.

Substituting the chosen value of $\delta$ into
\eqref{eq:higher-magic-circuit-cover-size} gives
\begin{align*}
    &\log N\left(
        \varepsilon,
        \mathcal F_{n,p}\left(
            \mathsf{mag}^{[D]}_{n,k,M-n}
            \cup
            \mathsf{revmag}^{[D]}_{n,k,M-n}
        \right),
        \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \right)
    \le
    \log|\mathcal U|\\
    &\qquad\le
    \log2+CkM^2+kDM\log(M+1)
    +CkDM\log\left(
        \frac{C3^{p/2}kDM}{\varepsilon}
    \right)\\
    &\qquad\le
    CkM^2
    +CkDM\log\left(
        \frac{C3^{p/2}kDM}{\varepsilon}
    \right).
\end{align*}
The last inequality absorbs the architecture term and
$\log2$ by increasing $C$, using $k,D\ge1$ and
$0<\varepsilon<1$.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:higher-magic-ground-gap}
Fix an integer $k\ge1$ and constants $K\ge1$ and $0<L<\infty$.
Let $M_n\ge n$ and $D_n\ge1$ be deterministic integer sequences
satisfying
\[
    M_n\le Kn,
    \qquad
    D_n\le\frac{Ln}{\log n}
\]
for all sufficiently large $n$.  There is
$p_0=p_0(k,K,L)<\infty$ such that, for every fixed $p\ge p_0$,
there is $c_{p,k,K,L}>0$ for which
\[
    \mathbb P\left(
        \Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n,p}
        \left(
            \mathsf{mag}^{[D_n]}_{n,k,M_n-n}
            \cup
            \mathsf{revmag}^{[D_n]}_{n,k,M_n-n}
        \right)
        \ge
        c_{p,k,K,L}\sqrt n
    \right)
    \longrightarrow1.
\]
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Lemma~\ref{lem:higher-magic-entropy} gives
\[
    \Gamma_{n,p}
    \le
    CkM_n^2+CkD_nM_n
    \log\left(eC3^{p/2}kD_nM_n n\right).
\]
For each fixed $k$ and $p$, the width and depth assumptions bound the
logarithm by $3\log n+O_{p,k,K,L}(1)$.  Hence
\[
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{\Gamma_{n,p}}{n^2}
    \le Ck(K^2+KL).
\]
The right-hand side is independent of $p$, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(i)} gives
the conclusion with a threshold depending only on $k$, $K$, and $L$.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
\label{def:mixed-stabilizer}
Let $\mathsf{mixstab}_M$ be the class of $M$-qubit states obtained as
reductions of pure stabilizer states:
\[
    \mathsf{mixstab}_M
    :=
    \left\{
        \operatorname{Tr}_{\{M+1,\ldots,M+s\}}
        |\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|:
        |\Psi\rangle\in\mathsf{stab}_{M+s},\;
        s\ge0
    \right\}.
\]
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:fixed-depth-active-cone-pruning}
Every $\rho\in\mathsf{mag}^{[D],\mathrm{anc}}_n$ has a representation
\[
    \rho
    =
    \operatorname{Tr}_{\{n+1,\ldots,n2^D\}}
    \left(
        \widehat Q\widehat\tau\widehat Q^\dagger
    \right),
    \qquad
    \widehat\tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_{n2^D},
\]
for some depth-$D$ circuit $\widehat Q$ on $n2^D$ qubits,
independently of the number of ancillas used in the original
preparation. For a fixed total width $M\ge n$, every
$\rho\in\mathsf{mag}^{[D]}_{n,M-n}$ admits the same representation
with $n2^D$ replaced by $\widehat{M}:=\min\{M,n2^D\}$.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
By definition, for some $r\ge0$, there is a Clifford
unitary $C$ and a depth-$D$ circuit $Q=Q_D\cdots Q_1$
on $M:=n+r$ qubits such that
\[
    \rho
    =
    \operatorname{Tr}_{\{n+1,\ldots,M\}}
    (Q\rho_0Q^\dagger),
    \qquad
    \rho_0
    :=
    C|0^M\rangle\langle0^M|C^\dagger.
\]
Write each layer of the circuit as a product of its one- or two-qubit gates,
\[
    Q_t=\prod_{j=1}^{\ell_t}U_{t,j},
    \qquad
    E_{t,j}:=\operatorname{supp}(U_{t,j}).
\]
The sets $E_{t,j}$ are pairwise disjoint and have
size at most two.
Let $A_D=[n]$ be the set of retained output qubits at layer $D$, and for
$t=D,\ldots,1$, define recursively
\[
    J_t
    :=
    \{j\in[\ell_t]:E_{t,j}\cap A_t\ne\emptyset\},
    \qquad
    A_{t-1}
    :=
    A_t\cup\bigcup_{j\in J_t}E_{t,j}.
\]
In words, $A_t$ collects the qubits in layer $t$ that can affect the retained output qubits through the remaining layers $Q_{t+1},\dots, Q_D$, and $J_t$ indexes the gates in layer $t$ whose supports intersect the current set $A_t$. Because the gate supports are disjoint, $|J_t|\le|A_t|$.
Each gate indexed by $J_t$ adds at most one qubit outside
$A_t$, so
\[
    |A_{t-1}|
    =
    |A_t|+\sum_{j\in J_t}|E_{t,j}\setminus A_t|
    \le
    |A_t|+|J_t|
    \le
    2|A_t|.
\]
Consequently, $|A_0|\le2^D|A_D|=n2^D$. Since $A_0\subseteq[M]$, we also have $|A_0|\le M$,
and hence $|A_0|\le\widehat{M}$.

We now construct a pruned circuit $\overline{Q}$ by retaining only
the gates in the backward lightcone of the retained outputs.
In layer $t$, these are the gates indexed by $J_t$. Define
\[
    V_t:=\prod_{j\in J_t}U_{t,j},
    \qquad
    \overline{Q}:=V_D\cdots V_1.
\]
For every $j\in J_t$, we have
$E_{t,j}\subseteq A_{t-1}\subseteq A_0$, so all retained
gates act on qubits in $A_0$.
We therefore regard $\overline{Q}$ as a circuit on $A_0$.
Since each $V_t$ consists of gates with disjoint supports,
$\overline{Q}$ has depth at most $D$.


To see that this circuit preserves the reduced output, fix an observable $O$ on the retained $n$ qubits and define recursively on the full workspace, for $t=D,\ldots,1$,
\[
    O_D:=O\otimes I_{\{n+1,\ldots,M\}},
    \qquad
    O_{t-1}:=Q_t^\dagger O_tQ_t.
\]
We claim that
\[
    \operatorname{supp}(O_t)\subseteq A_t,
    \qquad
    O_{t-1}
    =
    (V_t\otimes I_{A_0^c})^\dagger
    O_t
    (V_t\otimes I_{A_0^c}),
\]
where $A_0^c$ is the complement of $A_0$ in $[M]$.
The support inclusion holds initially for $t=D$.
Suppose it holds at layer $t$.
For $j\notin J_t$, the support $E_{t,j}$ is disjoint
from $A_t$, so $U_{t,j}$ commutes with $O_t$.
It also commutes with all other gates in that layer,
and therefore cancels with its adjoint in
$Q_t^\dagger O_tQ_t$.
The remaining gates are supported in $A_{t-1}$, proving
both the displayed identity and
$\operatorname{supp}(O_{t-1})\subseteq A_{t-1}$.

Iterating the identity gives
\[
    Q^\dagger
    (O\otimes I_{\{n+1,\ldots,M\}})
    Q
    =
    \left[
        \overline{Q}^\dagger
        (O\otimes I_{A_0\setminus[n]})
        \overline{Q}
    \right]\otimes I_{A_0^c}.
\]
Set $\tau:=\operatorname{Tr}_{A_0^c}(\rho_0)$.
Taking expectations and using the defining property of
partial trace yields
\[
    \begin{aligned}
    \operatorname{Tr}(O\rho)
    &=
    \operatorname{Tr}\left(
        Q^\dagger
        (O\otimes I_{\{n+1,\ldots,M\}})
        Q\rho_0
    \right)\\
    &=
    \operatorname{Tr}\left(
        \overline{Q}^\dagger
        (O\otimes I_{A_0\setminus[n]})
        \overline{Q}\tau
    \right)\\
    &=
    \operatorname{Tr}\left(
        O\,\operatorname{Tr}_{A_0\setminus[n]}
        (\overline{Q}\tau \overline{Q}^\dagger)
    \right).
    \end{aligned}
\]
Since this holds for every observable $O$,
\[
    \rho
    =
    \operatorname{Tr}_{A_0\setminus[n]}
    \left(
        \overline{Q}\tau \overline{Q}^\dagger
    \right).
\]

Since $\rho_0$ is a pure stabilizer state,
$\tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_{|A_0|}$.
Relabel the qubits in $A_0$ so that the retained outputs
are the first $n$ qubits.
If $|A_0|<\widehat{M}$, append $\widehat{M}-|A_0|$ qubits in the
state $|0\rangle$ and extend $\overline{Q}$ by the identity.
Appending these qubits preserves the mixed-stabilizer class since tensoring $\rho_0$ with the appended $|0\rangle$-states produces another pure stabilizer state, whose partial trace
over $A_0^c$ is the padded state. Thus we obtain $\widehat\tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_{\widehat{M}}$
and a depth-$D$ circuit $\widehat Q$ on $\widehat{M}$ qubits
such that
\[
    \rho
    =
    \operatorname{Tr}_{\{n+1,\ldots,\widehat{M}\}}
    \left(
        \widehat Q\widehat\tau\widehat Q^\dagger
    \right).
\]
This proves the representation for fixed total width $M$.
Since $\widehat{M}\le n2^D$, further padding with $|0\rangle$-states
and extending the circuit by the identity gives a representation
on exactly $n2^D$ qubits, independent of the original number
$r$ of ancillas.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:forward-profile-entropy}
There is a universal constant $C<\infty$ such that, for every
$M\ge n\ge p\ge2$, $D\ge1$, and $0<\varepsilon<1$, setting
${\widehat M}:=\min\{M,n2^D\}$ gives
\[
    \log N\left(
        \varepsilon,
        \mathcal F_{n,p}\left(\mathsf{mag}^{[D]}_{n,M-n}\right),
        \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \right)
    \le
    C{\widehat M}\left[
        \min\{p2^D,{\widehat M}\}
        +D\log\left(\frac{C3^{p/2}D{\widehat M}}{\varepsilon}\right)
    \right].
\]
The same bound holds for $\mathsf{mag}^{[D],\mathrm{anc}}_n$ upon setting
${\widehat M}:=n2^D$.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:dense-magic}
Let $(M_n)_{n\ge1}$ and $(D_n)_{n\ge1}$ be fixed deterministic
integer sequences with $M_n\ge n$ and $D_n\ge1$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
    \item Suppose $M_n\le Kn$ and $D_n\le Ln/\log n$ for all
    sufficiently large $n$, for some fixed constants $K\ge1$ and
    $0<L<\infty$. Then, for every fixed $p$ sufficiently large in terms of $K$
and $L$, there is $c_{p,K,L}>0$ for which
\[
    \mathbb P\left(
        \Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n,p}
        \left(\mathsf{mag}^{[D_n]}_{n,M_n-n}\right)
        \ge c_{p,K,L}\sqrt n
    \right)
    \longrightarrow1.
\]

    \item For every fixed $p\ge2$, if $M_n=O(n)$ and $2^{D_n}=o(n)$,
    then
    \[
        \frac{
            \Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}
            \left(\mathsf{mag}^{[D_n]}_{n,M_n-n};\mathsf{prod}_n\right)
        }{\sqrt n}
        \longrightarrow0
    \]
    in $L^1$ and in probability.
\end{enumerate}
With arbitrarily many discardable ancillas, assume that
$4^{D_n}=o(n)$.  Then the convergence in
part~\textup{(ii)} holds for
$\mathsf{mag}^{[D_n],\mathrm{anc}}_n$ for every fixed
$p\ge2$.  Moreover, there is a universal $p_0$ such
that, for every fixed $p\ge p_0$,
\[
    \mathbb P\left(
        \Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n,p}
        \left(\mathsf{mag}^{[D_n],\mathrm{anc}}_n\right)
        \ge c_p\sqrt n
    \right)
    \longrightarrow1,
\]
where $c_p>0$ depends only on $p$.
Both conclusions are uniform over the number of
discardable ancillas.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Set ${\widehat M}_n:=\min\{M_n,n2^{D_n}\}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:forward-profile-entropy} allows us to take
\[
    a_{n,p}=C{\widehat M}_n\min\{p2^{D_n},{\widehat M}_n\},
    \qquad
    b_{n,p}=CD_n{\widehat M}_n,
    \qquad
    B_{n,p}=C3^{p/2}D_n{\widehat M}_n
\]
in Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}.  Hence
\[
    \Gamma_{n,p}
    \le
    C{\widehat M}_n\min\{p2^{D_n},{\widehat M}_n\}
    +CD_n{\widehat M}_n\log\left(eC3^{p/2}D_n{\widehat M}_n n\right).
\]
Under the hypotheses of part~\textup{(i)}, using
${\widehat M}_n\le M_n$ gives
\[
    \Gamma_{n,p}
    \le
    CM_n^2+CD_nM_n\log\left(eC3^{p/2}D_nM_n n\right).
\]
For fixed $p,K,L$, the logarithm is at most
$3\log n+O_{p,K,L}(1)$, so
\[
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{\Gamma_{n,p}}{n^2}
    \le C(K^2+KL).
\]
The right-hand side is independent of $p$.
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(i)}
therefore gives the result.

For part~\textup{(ii)}, choose a fixed
$K$ such that $M_n\le Kn$ eventually.  Using
$\min\{p2^{D_n},{\widehat M}_n\}\le p2^{D_n}$ instead gives
\[
    \Gamma_{n,p}
    \le
    C_{p,K}n\left[
        2^{D_n}+D_n\log\left(en^2D_n\right)
    \right]
    =o(n^2),
\]
since $2^{D_n}=o(n)$ implies $D_n=O(\log n)$. Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(ii)},
with benchmark $\mathcal B_n=\mathsf{prod}_n$, gives the result.

For the arbitrary-ancilla class, the entropy bound gives
\[
    \frac{\Gamma_{n,p}}{n^2}
    \le
    C_p\left[
        \frac{4^{D_n}}{n}
        +
        \frac{
            D_n2^{D_n}
            \log(en^2D_n2^{D_n})
        }{n}
    \right].
\]
If $4^{D_n}=o(n)$, then eventually
$2^{D_n}\le\sqrt n$ and $D_n=O(\log n)$, so
\[
    \frac{\Gamma_{n,p}}{n^2}
    \le
    C_p\left[
        \frac{4^{D_n}}{n}
        +\frac{(\log n)^2}{\sqrt n}
    \right]
    \longrightarrow0.
\]
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}
\textup{(ii)} gives the product-state comparison.
Part~\textup{(i)}, applied with $L=0$, gives the
ground-state separation with a universal lower
threshold for $p$ and a gap constant depending only
on $p$.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:fixed-depth-mixed-stabilizer-growth}
For every $\tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_M$ and every $P\in\mathcal P_M$,
$f_\tau(P) = \operatorname{Tr}(P\tau)\in\{-1,0,1\}$.  Moreover, each of the set classes
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal A_+ &:=
    \bigl\{\{P\in\mathcal P_M:f_\tau(P)=1\}:
    \tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_M\bigr\},\\
    \mathcal A_- &:=
    \bigl\{\{P\in\mathcal P_M:f_\tau(P)=-1\}:
    \tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_M\bigr\}
\end{align*}
has VC dimension at most $M$.  Consequently, for arbitrary
$P_1,\ldots,P_q\in\mathcal P_M$,
\[
    \#\left\{
        \bigl(f_\tau(P_1),\ldots,f_\tau(P_q)\bigr):
        \tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_M
    \right\}
    \le
    \bigg(\sum_{j=0}^M\binom qj\bigg)^2.
\]
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
By Definition~\ref{def:mixed-stabilizer}, every
$\tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_M$ can be written as
$\tau=\operatorname{Tr}_A(|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|)$, where
$|\Psi\rangle\in\mathsf{stab}_{M+s}$ for some $s\ge0$ and $A$ denotes the
$s$ discarded qubits.  Any $(M+s)$-qubit stabilizer state $|\Psi\rangle$ has a corresponding
stabilizer group $\mathcal G_\Psi$, consisting of all signed Pauli
operators $G$ that stabilize it, meaning
$G|\Psi\rangle=|\Psi\rangle$.
This group has $M+s$ independent generators $g_1,\ldots,g_{M+s}$,
which give the representation
\[
    |\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|
    =
    \prod_{j=1}^{M+s}\frac{I+g_j}{2}
    =
    2^{-(M+s)}\sum_{G\in\mathcal G_\Psi}G;
\]
see Appendix~\ref{app:IsotropicSubspaces}.
The group contains $I$ but not $-I$, since
$(-I)|\Psi\rangle=-|\Psi\rangle\ne|\Psi\rangle$.

Write each $G\in\mathcal G_\Psi$ as $G=S\otimes R$, where $S$ is
a signed Pauli operator on the retained qubits and $R\in\mathcal P_s$
acts on $A$. Then
\[
    \operatorname{Tr}_A(G)
    =
    S\operatorname{Tr}(R)
    =
        2^sS \mathbf 1 \{R=I_A\}.
\]
Define
\[
    \mathcal S_\tau
    :=
    \left\{
        S\in\{\pm P:P\in\mathcal P_M\}:
        S\otimes I_A\in\mathcal G_\Psi
    \right\}.
\]
The stabilizer expansion therefore gives
\[
    \tau
    =
    2^{-(M+s)}
    \sum_{G\in\mathcal G_\Psi}\operatorname{Tr}_A(G)
    =
    2^{-M}\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_\tau}S.
\]
The set $\mathcal S_\tau$ inherits the group structure and
commutation relations of $\mathcal G_\Psi$: for every
$S,S'\in\mathcal S_\tau$,
\[
    SS'=S'S\in\mathcal S_\tau,
    \qquad S^{-1}=S.
\]
Moreover, $I\in\mathcal S_\tau$ and $-I\notin\mathcal S_\tau$.  Pauli orthogonality gives for $P \in \mathcal P_M$
\begin{align} \label{eq:pauli-profile-in-proof}
    f_\tau(P)
    =
    2^{-M}\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_\tau}\operatorname{Tr}(PS)
    =
    \begin{cases}
        +1,  & P\in\mathcal S_\tau,\\
        -1, & -P\in\mathcal S_\tau,\\
        ~0,  & \text{otherwise}.
    \end{cases}
\end{align}
Next, suppose that $P_1,\ldots,P_k$ are \emph{shattered} by $\mathcal A_+$, meaning that for every $B\subseteq[k]$, there exists
$\tau_B\in\mathsf{mixstab}_M$ such that
\[
    f_{\tau_B}(P_i)=1
    \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
    i\in B.
\]
First apply shattering with $B=[k]$, and denote the resulting state
by $\tau_{\mathrm{all}}$.
By \eqref{eq:pauli-profile-in-proof}, all the $P_i$ belong to
$\mathcal S_{\tau_{\mathrm{all}}}$, whose elements commute, so the $P_i$ commute.

We next show that $[P_1],\ldots,[P_k]$ are linearly independent
over $\mathbb F_2$. Suppose for the sake of contradiction that there are coefficients
$c_1,\ldots,c_k\in\{0,1\}$, not all zero, such that $\sum_{i=1}^k c_i[P_i]=0$. Setting $T:=\{i:c_i=1\}$, this becomes
\[
    \sum_{i\in T}[P_i]=0,
    \qquad T\ne\emptyset.
\]
Multiplication of Pauli operators corresponds to addition of their
binary labels, with phases ignored. Hence
\[
    \left[\prod_{i\in T}P_i\right]
    =
    \sum_{i\in T}[P_i]
    =
    0.
\]
Since the zero label corresponds to the identity, the product equals
$I$ up to a phase. Moreover, the $P_i$ commute and satisfy $P_i^2=I$,
so
\[
    \bigg(\prod_{i\in T}P_i\bigg)^2
    =
    \prod_{i\in T}P_i^2
    =
    I.
\]
The phase must therefore be $+1$ or $-1$, giving $\prod_{i\in T}P_i=\pm I$. Since the product belongs to $\mathcal S_{\tau_{\mathrm{all}}}$, which does not
contain $-I$, it must equal $I$. Now fix $j\in T$ and apply
shattering again, this time to the subset $[k]\setminus\{j\}$.
Denote the resulting state by $\tau_{-j}$, so that
\[
    P_i\in\mathcal S_{\tau_{-j}}\quad\text{for every }i\ne j,
    \qquad
    P_j\notin\mathcal S_{\tau_{-j}}.
\]
The identity $\prod_{i\in T}P_i=I$ is an identity between operators
and does not depend on the choice of state. By commutation, the identity can be written as 
\begin{align*}
    P_j \prod_{i\in T\setminus \{j\}} P_i=I,
\end{align*}
and multiplying both sides by $P_j$ and using $P_j^2=I$ yields
\begin{align*}
    P_j = \prod_{i\in T\setminus \{j\}} P_i.
\end{align*}
Since every $P_i$ with $i\in T\setminus\{j\}$ belongs to
$\mathcal S_{\tau_{-j}}$ however, closure under multiplication gives
\[
    \prod_{i\in T\setminus\{j\}}P_i
    \in\mathcal S_{\tau_{-j}}.
\]
This contradicts $P_j\notin\mathcal S_{\tau_{-j}}$, which was
required by the second application of shattering. Thus the labels are linearly independent. 

Hence, $W:=\operatorname{span}\{[P_1],\ldots,[P_k]\}$ has dimension $k$ by linear independence, and is isotropic, because
\[
    \langle[P_i],[P_j]\rangle_{\mathrm{sp}}=0,
    \qquad i,j\in[k].
\]
Every isotropic subspace of $\mathbb F_2^{2M}$ has dimension at
most $M$, so $k\le M$. This proves the VC-dimension bound for
the class $\mathcal A_+$.

For the class $\mathcal A_-$, the same argument applies with
$P_i$ replaced by $-P_i$, using
\[
    f_\tau(P_i)=-1
    \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
    -P_i\in\mathcal S_\tau.
\]
Its VC dimension is therefore also at most $M$.

Finally, fix arbitrary $P_1,\ldots,P_q\in\mathcal P_M$ and set
$E:=\{P_1,\ldots,P_q\}$. Since $\mathcal A_+$ and $\mathcal A_-$
each have VC dimension at most $M$, Sauer's lemma
\cite[Lemma~6.10]{shalev2014understanding} gives
\[
    \#\{A\cap E:A\in\mathcal A_+\}
    \le \sum_{j=0}^M\binom qj,
    \qquad
    \#\{A\cap E:A\in\mathcal A_-\}
    \le \sum_{j=0}^M\binom qj,
\]
where we used $|E|\le q$.

For each $\tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_M$, define
\[
    E_\tau^+:=\{P\in E:f_\tau(P)=1\},
    \qquad
    E_\tau^-:=\{P\in E:f_\tau(P)=-1\}.
\]
Since $f_\tau$ takes values in $\{-1,0,1\}$,
\[
    f_\tau(P_i)
    =
    \mathbf 1_{E_\tau^+}(P_i)
    -
    \mathbf 1_{E_\tau^-}(P_i),
    \qquad i=1,\dots, q.
\]
Thus specifying $E_\tau^+$ and $E_\tau^-$ determines every
coordinate of the restricted profile. Moreover,
\[
    E_\tau^+\in\{A\cap E:A\in\mathcal A_+\},
    \qquad
    E_\tau^-\in\{A\cap E:A\in\mathcal A_-\}.
\]
Consequently,
\begin{align*}
    \#\left\{
        \bigl(f_\tau(P_1),\ldots,f_\tau(P_q)\bigr):
        \tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_M
    \right\}
    &\le
    \#\{A\cap E:A\in\mathcal A_+\}
    \#\{A\cap E:A\in\mathcal A_-\}\\
    &\le
    \bigg(\sum_{j=0}^M\binom qj\bigg)^2.
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Recall that ${\widehat M}=\min\{M,n2^D\}$.
For each circuit $Q$ of depth at most $D$ on ${\widehat M}$
qubits, define
\[
    \mathcal F_Q
    :=
    \left\{
        f_\rho:
        \rho=
        \operatorname{Tr}_{\{n+1,\ldots,{\widehat M}\}}(Q\tau Q^\dagger),~~
        \tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_{{\widehat M}}
    \right\}.
\]
Here $f_\rho(P)=\operatorname{Tr}(P\rho)$ for $P\in\mathcal P_{n,p}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:fixed-depth-active-cone-pruning}, $\mathcal F_{n,p}(\mathsf{mag}^{[D]}_{n,M-n})
    \subseteq
    \bigcup_Q\mathcal F_Q$. It therefore suffices to bound the metric entropy of
$\bigcup_Q\mathcal F_Q$.
To this end, we construct a finite circuit cover $\mathcal Q$ such that for any $Q$, there exists $\widetilde Q \in \mathcal Q$ such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:forward-profile-approximation}
    \sup_{f\in\mathcal F_Q}
    \inf_{g\in\mathcal F_{\widetilde Q}}
    \|f-g\|_{n,p}
    \le\varepsilon/4.
\end{equation}
Combining \eqref{eq:forward-profile-approximation} with an $\varepsilon/4$-cover
of each $\mathcal F_{\widetilde Q}$ then gives
\begin{align}
\label{eq:forward-cover-decomposition}
    \log N\bigg(
        \varepsilon,\bigcup_Q\mathcal F_Q,\|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \bigg)
    &\le
    \log\left(
        \sum_{\widetilde Q\in\mathcal Q}
        N\left(
            \varepsilon/4,\mathcal F_{\widetilde Q},\|\cdot\|_{n,p}
        \right)
    \right) \nonumber\\
    &\le
    \log\left(
        |\mathcal Q|\,
        \sup_{\widetilde Q\in\mathcal Q}
        N\left(
            \varepsilon/4,\mathcal F_{\widetilde Q},\|\cdot\|_{n,p}
        \right)
    \right)\nonumber\\
    &=
    \log|\mathcal Q|
    +
    \sup_{\widetilde Q\in\mathcal Q}
    \log N\left(
        \varepsilon/4,\mathcal F_{\widetilde Q},\|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \right).
\end{align}
We first bound the second term in the last line of
\eqref{eq:forward-cover-decomposition} uniformly over $Q$,
then construct $\mathcal Q$, verify
\eqref{eq:forward-profile-approximation},
and bound the first term $\log|\mathcal Q|$.


\textit{1. Covering profiles for fixed $Q$ and varying $\tau$: }
Fix $Q$. For every input $\tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_{{\widehat M}}$, let
$\rho=\operatorname{Tr}_{\{n+1,\ldots,{\widehat M}\}}(Q\tau Q^\dagger)$
be its reduced output. For every $P\in\mathcal P_{n,p}$,
\[
    \begin{aligned}
    f_\rho(P)
    &=\operatorname{Tr}(P\rho)
    =\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(
        P\,\operatorname{Tr}_{\{n+1,\ldots,{\widehat M}\}}
        (Q\tau Q^\dagger)
    \right)\\
    &=\operatorname{Tr}\bigl((P\otimes I)Q\tau Q^\dagger\bigr)
    =\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(Q^\dagger(P\otimes I)Q\,\tau\bigr).
    \end{aligned}
\]
The third equality is the defining identity for the partial trace,
where $I$ acts on the discarded qubits. We now show that the operator $Q^\dagger(P\otimes I)Q$ is supported on at most
\[
    s:=\min\{p2^D,{\widehat M}\}
\]
qubits, and use its Pauli expansion to express $f_\rho(P)$
in terms of input expectations.

Write $Q=Q_D\cdots Q_1$, where each $Q_t$ is a layer of gates
with disjoint supports of size at most two.
We first consider how conjugation by one layer changes the support
of an operator.

Fix a layer $Q_t=U_1\cdots U_r$, and let $E_j$ be the support
of $U_j$. Suppose $A$ is supported on $S$, meaning
$A=A_S\otimes I_{S^c}$, and define
\[
    J:=\{j\in[r]:E_j\cap S\ne\emptyset\}.
\]
For $j\notin J$, the gate $U_j$ acts outside $S$, so
$U_j^\dagger A U_j=A$.
Moreover, the $U_j$ commute with one another because their
supports are disjoint. We can therefore move every gate
with $j\notin J$ next to $A$ and cancel it with its adjoint,
obtaining
\[
    Q_t^\dagger A Q_t
    =
    \big(\prod_{j\in J}U_j\big)^\dagger
    A
    \big(\prod_{j\in J}U_j\big).
\]
Every factor on the right acts as the identity outside $S':=S\cup\bigcup_{j\in J}E_j$. Hence $\operatorname{supp}(Q_t^\dagger A Q_t)\subseteq S'$.

To bound $|S'|$, note that each $E_j$ with $j\in J$
contains at least one qubit of $S$ and has size at most two.
It therefore contains at most one qubit outside $S$.
Also, the sets $E_j\cap S$, $j\in J$, are nonempty and
pairwise disjoint, so $|J|\le|S|$. Consequently,
\[
    |S'|
    =
    |S|+\sum_{j\in J}|E_j\setminus S|
    \le
    |S|+|J|
    \le
    2|S|.
\]
Thus conjugation by one layer at most doubles the support size.

The operator $P\otimes I$ starts with support of size $p$.
In the expression
\[
    Q^\dagger(P\otimes I)Q
    =
    Q_1^\dagger\cdots Q_D^\dagger
    (P\otimes I)
    Q_D\cdots Q_1,
\]
we first conjugate by $Q_D$, then by $Q_{D-1}$, and continue
through $Q_1$. Applying the preceding bound at each step,
the support has size at most $2p$ after the first step,
$2^2p$ after the second, and $2^Dp$ after all $D$ steps.
Since the support is also a subset of the
${\widehat M}$ qubits, we obtain
\[
    \bigl|\operatorname{supp}(Q^\dagger(P\otimes I)Q)\bigr|
    \le
    \min\{p2^D,{\widehat M}\}
    =s.
\]

Now fix $P_1,\ldots,P_q\in\mathcal P_{n,p}$.
Each operator $Q^\dagger(P_\ell\otimes I)Q$ has a Pauli expansion
with at most $4^s$ terms, since there are four choices
$I,X,Y,Z$ on each qubit of its support and only $I$ elsewhere.
List the distinct Paulis appearing in these $q$ expansions
as $R_1,\ldots,R_N$, where $N\le q4^s$.
Then
\begin{align*}
    Q^\dagger(P_\ell\otimes I)Q
    &=\sum_{j=1}^N a_{\ell j}R_j,\\
    f_\rho(P_\ell)
    &=\sum_{j=1}^N a_{\ell j}f_\tau(R_j),
    \qquad \ell = 1,\dots,q,
\end{align*}
where the coefficients depend on $Q$ and the chosen output
Paulis, but not on $\tau$. If $\tau,\tau'\in\mathsf{mixstab}_{{\widehat M}}$ satisfy
\[
    f_\tau(R_j)=f_{\tau'}(R_j),
    \qquad j = 1,\dots, N,
\]
then their reduced outputs $\rho,\rho'$ under the same circuit $Q$
satisfy
\[
    f_\rho(P_\ell)
    =\sum_{j=1}^N a_{\ell j}f_\tau(R_j) =\sum_{j=1}^N a_{\ell j}f_{\tau'}(R_j)
    =f_{\rho'}(P_\ell),
    \qquad \ell =1,\dots, q.
\]
Thus the input expectations at $R_1,\ldots,R_N$ uniquely determine
the output expectations at $P_1,\ldots,P_q$, so the number of
distinct output vectors cannot exceed the number of distinct
input vectors.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:fixed-depth-mixed-stabilizer-growth},
\begin{align*}
    \#\left\{
        \bigl(f(P_1),\ldots,f(P_q)\bigr):f\in\mathcal F_Q
    \right\}
    &\le
    \#\left\{
        \bigl(f_\tau(R_1),\ldots,f_\tau(R_N)\bigr):
        \tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_{{\widehat M}}
    \right\}\\
    &\le
    \left(\sum_{j=0}^{{\widehat M}}\binom Nj\right)^2
    \le
    \left(\sum_{j=0}^{{\widehat M}}\binom{q4^s}{j}\right)^2.
\end{align*}
To apply Lemma~\ref{lem:growth-entropy} with
$d=2{\widehat M}$, we need a restriction-growth bound for
every $q\ge2{\widehat M}$.
For such $q$, we have $q4^s\ge {\widehat M}$, so the
standard binomial bound gives
\[
    \left(\sum_{j=0}^{{\widehat M}}\binom{q4^s}{j}\right)^2
    \le
    \left(\frac{eq4^s}{{\widehat M}}\right)^{2{\widehat M}}
    =
    \left(\frac{Aq}{d}\right)^d,
\]
with $d=2{\widehat M}$ and $A=2e4^s$. Thus $\mathcal F_Q$ satisfies the restriction-growth hypothesis
of the lemma with these parameters.

We use the uniform probability measure on $\mathcal P_{n,p}$.
For any function $h$ on this set, the corresponding $L_2$ norm satisfies
\[
    \|h\|_{L_2}^2
    =
    \frac{1}{3^p\binom np}
    \sum_{P\in\mathcal P_{n,p}}|h(P)|^2
    =
    3^{-p}\|h\|_{n,p}^2.
\]
Consequently, an $L_2$-cover of radius $\varepsilon/3^{p/2}$
is a cover of radius $\varepsilon$ in $\|\cdot\|_{n,p}$.
Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:growth-entropy} at this $L_2$ radius gives
\begin{align}
    \log N\left(\varepsilon,\mathcal F_Q,\|\cdot\|_{n,p}\right)
    &=
    \log N\left(
        \frac{\varepsilon}{3^{p/2}},\mathcal F_Q,L_2
    \right)\notag\\
    &\le
    Cd\log\left(\frac{eA3^{p/2}}{\varepsilon}\right)\notag\\
    &\le
    C{\widehat M}\left[
        s+\log\left(\frac{C3^{p/2}}{\varepsilon}\right)
    \right].
    \label{eq:forward-fixed-circuit-entropy}
\end{align}

The bound \eqref{eq:forward-fixed-circuit-entropy} holds uniformly over $Q$.

\textit{2. Covering the circuit class: }
An architecture specifies the gate locations in each layer.
For each qubit, there are three possibilities: it participates
in a two-qubit gate, in which case there are
${\widehat M}-1$ choices for the other qubit; it has a
one-qubit gate; or it has no gate.
Thus there are
\[
    ({\widehat M}-1)+1+1={\widehat M}+1
\]
possible labels per qubit.
Every valid layer determines such a labeling, so there are at most
$({\widehat M}+1)^{{\widehat M}}$ layer architectures
and therefore at most $({\widehat M}+1)^{D{\widehat M}}$ architectures for $D$ layers.
Finally, disjointness of the gate supports implies that each layer
has at most ${\widehat M}$ gates, giving at most
$D{\widehat M}$ gate locations in total.


As in Lemma~\ref{lem:gate-count-profile-entropy}, choose
operator-norm $\delta$-nets for $\mathsf U(2)$ and
$\mathsf U(4)$, with centers in the respective unitary groups
and cardinalities at most $(C/\delta)^C$.
For each architecture, approximate every gate by a point
in the corresponding net. Since there are at most
$D{\widehat M}$ gates, this gives at most
$(C/\delta)^{CD{\widehat M}}$ approximating circuits
per architecture. Taking the union over all architectures
gives a finite set $\mathcal Q$ of circuits satisfying
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:forward-circuit-cover-size}
    |\mathcal Q|\le
    ({\widehat M}+1)^{D{\widehat M}}
    (C/\delta)^{CD{\widehat M}}.
\end{equation}
For every circuit $Q$, the set $\mathcal Q$ contains
a circuit $\widetilde Q$ with the same architecture and
with corresponding gates differing by at most $\delta$.

To bound the covering radius, write $Q$ and $\widetilde Q$
in terms of their $L\le D{\widehat M}$ gates,
\[
    Q=U_L\cdots U_1,
    \qquad
    \widetilde Q=\widetilde U_L\cdots\widetilde U_1,
\]
using the same ordering of gate locations in both circuits.
Here each gate acts as the identity outside its designated
qubits, and
$\|U_j-\widetilde U_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta$.
Replacing the gates one at a time gives the telescoping identity
\[
    Q-\widetilde Q
    =
    \sum_{j=1}^L
        \widetilde U_L\cdots\widetilde U_{j+1}
        (U_j-\widetilde U_j)
        U_{j-1}\cdots U_1,
\]
where an empty product is interpreted as the identity.
All factors surrounding $U_j-\widetilde U_j$ are unitary,
so multiplication by these factors preserves its operator norm.
The triangle inequality therefore gives
\[
    \|Q-\widetilde Q\|_{\mathrm{op}}
    \le
    \sum_{j=1}^L\|U_j-\widetilde U_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}
    \le
    L\delta
    \le
    D{\widehat M}\delta.
\]
Thus this construction gives an operator-norm
$D{\widehat M}\delta$-cover of the circuit class.

\textit{3. Transferring the circuit approximation to profiles: }
Let $\rho$ and $\widetilde\rho$ be the reduced outputs of
$Q$ and $\widetilde Q$ applied to the same input
$\tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_{{\widehat M}}$.
Using contractivity under partial trace and $\|\tau\|_1=1$,
we obtain
\[
    \begin{aligned}
    \|\rho-\widetilde\rho\|_1
    &\le
    \|Q\tau Q^\dagger-\widetilde Q\tau\widetilde Q^\dagger\|_1
    \le
    \|(Q-\widetilde Q)\tau Q^\dagger\|_1
    +
    \|\widetilde Q\tau(Q^\dagger-\widetilde Q^\dagger)\|_1\\
    &\le
    2\|Q-\widetilde Q\|_{\mathrm{op}}
    \le 2D{\widehat M}\delta.
    \end{aligned}
\]
Since every Pauli has operator norm one and
$|\mathcal P_{n,p}|=3^p\binom np$, the definition of the
profile norm gives
\[
    \|f_\rho-f_{\widetilde\rho}\|_{n,p}
    \le
    3^{p/2}\|\rho-\widetilde\rho\|_1
    \le
    2\cdot3^{p/2}D{\widehat M}\delta.
\]
This bound is uniform over $\tau$. Taking $\delta
    =\varepsilon/
         ({8\cdot3^{p/2}D{\widehat M}})$ therefore ensures that every profile in $\mathcal F_Q$
lies within $\varepsilon/4$ of a profile in
$\mathcal F_{\widetilde Q}$, as required by
\eqref{eq:forward-profile-approximation}.

\textit{4. Combining the estimates:}
For each $\widetilde Q\in\mathcal Q$, choose an
$\varepsilon/4$-cover of $\mathcal F_{\widetilde Q}$
using \eqref{eq:forward-fixed-circuit-entropy}.

To verify that their union covers the target class, take any
target profile $f_\rho\in\mathcal F_Q$.
Approximate $Q$ by a circuit $\widetilde Q$ in the circuit cover
and apply it to the same input $\tau$.
For the chosen value of $\delta$, the resulting profile
$f_{\widetilde\rho}\in\mathcal F_{\widetilde Q}$ satisfies $\|f_\rho-f_{\widetilde\rho}\|_{n,p}
    \le\varepsilon/4$. The cover of $\mathcal F_{\widetilde Q}$ then contains a point
$h$ satisfying $\|f_{\widetilde\rho}-h\|_{n,p}
    \le\varepsilon/4$. Consequently,
\[
    \|f_\rho-h\|_{n,p}
    \le
    \|f_\rho-f_{\widetilde\rho}\|_{n,p}
    +
    \|f_{\widetilde\rho}-h\|_{n,p}
    \le\varepsilon/2.
\]
Thus the union of the profile covers is an
$\varepsilon/2$-cover, and hence an $\varepsilon$-cover,
of the target class.

There is one profile cover for each circuit in the circuit
cover. The total cardinality is therefore at most the
circuit-cover cardinality multiplied by the uniform bound
on the profile-cover cardinality for a fixed circuit.
Substituting \eqref{eq:forward-circuit-cover-size} and
\eqref{eq:forward-fixed-circuit-entropy} into the first and second
terms, respectively, in the last line of
\eqref{eq:forward-cover-decomposition} gives
\begin{align*}
    \log N\left(
        \varepsilon,
        \mathcal F_{n,p}(\mathsf{mag}^{[D]}_{n,M-n}),
        \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \right)
    &\le
    D{\widehat M}\log({\widehat M}+1)
    +CD{\widehat M}\log(C/\delta)\\
    &+
    C{\widehat M}\left[
        s+\log\left(\frac{C3^{p/2}}{\varepsilon}\right)
    \right].
\end{align*}

Here \eqref{eq:forward-fixed-circuit-entropy} is applied at
radius $\varepsilon/4$, with the factor $4$ absorbed into $C$.
Substituting
$\delta=\varepsilon/(8\cdot3^{p/2}D{\widehat M})$
and using $D\ge1$ yields
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:forward-combined-entropy}
    \log N\left(
        \varepsilon,
        \mathcal F_{n,p}(\mathsf{mag}^{[D]}_{n,M-n}),
        \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \right)
    \le
    C{\widehat M}\left[
        s+D\log\left(
            \frac{C3^{p/2}D{\widehat M}}{\varepsilon}
        \right)
    \right].
\end{equation}
Substituting $s=\min\{p2^D,{\widehat M}\}$ into
\eqref{eq:forward-combined-entropy} proves the first estimate.

\textit{5. Arbitrary discardable ancillas: }
For arbitrary discardable ancillas,
Lemma~\ref{lem:fixed-depth-active-cone-pruning} represents
every output using a depth-$D$ circuit on the common width
${\widehat M}=n2^D$, regardless of the original workspace.
The circuit cover counted in \eqref{eq:forward-circuit-cover-size}
and the profile covers obtained from
\eqref{eq:forward-fixed-circuit-entropy}
therefore cover the entire class, uniformly over the number
of ancillas.
Since $p\le n$, we have $s=p2^D$.
Substituting these values of ${\widehat M}$ and $s$
into \eqref{eq:forward-combined-entropy} proves the second estimate.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
\label{def:revmag-clean}
Fix $D\ge1$. Let $\mathsf{revmag}^{[D],\mathrm{clean}}_n$ be the class
of pure $n$-qubit states $\ket{\psi}$ for which there exist
$r\ge0$, a Clifford $C\in\mathsf{cliff}_{n+r}$, and a depth-$D$
matching circuit $Q$ on $n+r$ qubits such that
\[
    CQ\ket{0^{n+r}}
    =
    \ket{\psi}\ket{0^r}.
\]
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
\label{def:stabilizer-nullity}
For a pure $M$-qubit state $\ket{\xi}$, its Pauli
stabilizer space is
\[
    \mathsf S(\xi)
    :=
    \left\{
        [P]\in\mathbb F_2^{2M}:
        P\in\mathcal P_M^\pm,\;
        P\ket{\xi}=\ket{\xi}
    \right\},
\]
and its stabilizer nullity is
$\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\xi):=M-\dim\mathsf S(\xi)$.
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:revmag-local-recovery}
Let $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal P_M^\pm$ be a group of
commuting Pauli operators with $-I\notin\mathcal G$.
Let $S$ be its label space and $\mathcal K_S$ its common
$+1$ eigenspace, with $\dim S=M-t$ and $1\le t\le M$.
Suppose $V_{\mathrm{glob}}\in\mathsf{cliff}_M$ satisfies
\[
    V_{\mathrm{glob}}\mathcal K_S
    =\mathbb C^{2^t}
      \otimes\operatorname{span}\{\ket{0^{M-t}}\}.
\]
Let $E\subseteq[M]$ be such that every logical Pauli class
in $W_S=S^\perp/S$ has a representative supported on $E$.
Then there exist a Clifford $V_E$ on $E$ and an ordered set
$T=\{q_1,\ldots,q_t\}\subseteq E$ with the following property:
for every normalized $\ket{v}\in\mathcal K_S$, writing
$V_{\mathrm{glob}}\ket{v}=\ket{u}\otimes\ket{0^{M-t}}$, we have
\[
    \operatorname{Tr}_{E\setminus T}\left[
        V_E\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_{E^c}\ket{v}\bra{v}\bigr)V_E^\dagger
    \right]
    =\ket{u}\bra{u}.
\]
On the left, the qubits of $T$ are listed in the order
$q_1,\ldots,q_t$.
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
For $j\in[t]$, let $X_j,Z_j\in\mathcal P_t$ apply $X,Z$
to the $j$th logical qubit and the identity to the other
logical qubits. Define the physical operators
\[
    R_{X,j}:=V_{\mathrm{glob}}^\dagger
        (X_j\otimes I_{2^{M-t}})V_{\mathrm{glob}},
    \qquad
    R_{Z,j}:=V_{\mathrm{glob}}^\dagger
        (Z_j\otimes I_{2^{M-t}})V_{\mathrm{glob}}.
\]
Clifford conjugation preserves signed Hermitian Paulis,
so $R_{X,j},R_{Z,j}\in\mathcal P_M^\pm$; see
Appendix~\ref{app:PauliOpsandLabels}.
For any $\ket{v}\in\mathcal K_S$, write
$\ket{v}=V_{\mathrm{glob}}^\dagger
(\ket{u}\otimes\ket{0^{M-t}})$. Then
\[
    R_{X,j}\ket{v}
    =V_{\mathrm{glob}}^\dagger
      (X_j\ket{u}\otimes\ket{0^{M-t}})\in\mathcal K_S.
\]
The same identity holds with $X$ replaced by $Z$.
After decoding, these actions become $X_j\ket{u}$ and
$Z_j\ket{u}$, respectively. Thus $R_{X,j}$ and $R_{Z,j}$
implement $X$ and $Z$ on the $j$th logical qubit for
every vector in $\mathcal K_S$. In particular, they
preserve $\mathcal K_S$ and their labels belong to $S^\perp$.

By the hypothesis on $E$, there are stabilizers
$G_{X,j},G_{Z,j}\in\mathcal G$ such that
\[
    \overline X_j:=R_{X,j}G_{X,j},
    \qquad
    \overline Z_j:=R_{Z,j}G_{Z,j}
\]
are supported on $E$. To justify this choice, take a representative
on $E$ of $[R_{X,j}]+S$ and choose $G_{X,j}$ with label equal
to the difference of its label and $[R_{X,j}]$; the product
has the chosen label and hence the same support. The argument
for $Z$ is identical.
Since $R_{X,j}$ commutes with $G_{X,j}$, their product
$\overline X_j$ belongs to $\mathcal P_M^\pm$; the same
argument applies to $\overline Z_j$.
These operators agree exactly with $R_{X,j},R_{Z,j}$ on
$\mathcal K_S$, because every stabilizer acts as the
identity on this space.
Clifford conjugation preserves the commutation relations
of $X_j,Z_j$, and multiplication by stabilizers preserves
them because these stabilizers commute with every
$R_{X,j},R_{Z,j}$ and with one another. Consequently,
\[
    \overline X_j\overline Z_k
    =(-1)^{\delta_{jk}}\overline Z_k\overline X_j,
    \qquad
    [\overline X_j,\overline X_k]
    =[\overline Z_j,\overline Z_k]=0.
\]
Here $[A,B]=AB-BA$ and $\delta_{jk}$ is the Kronecker delta.

Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:app-local-symplectic} to these pairs
on the subsystem $E$. It gives distinct physical qubits
$q_1,\ldots,q_t\in E$ and a Clifford $V_E$ on $E$.
With $\widehat V_E:=V_E\otimes I_{E^c}$, we have
\[
    \widehat V_E\overline X_j\widehat V_E^\dagger=X_{q_j},
    \qquad
    \widehat V_E\overline Z_j\widehat V_E^\dagger=Z_{q_j}.
\]
Here $X_{q_j},Z_{q_j}$ act on physical qubit $q_j$ and
as the identity on the other $M-1$ qubits.
Set $T:=\{q_1,\ldots,q_t\}$, ordered by the pairs.

For any $P\in\mathcal P_t$, write
$P=\gamma\prod_{j=1}^t X_j^{a_j}Z_j^{b_j}$ with
$a_j,b_j\in\{0,1\}$ and $\gamma\in\{+1,-1,+i,-i\}$,
and define
$\overline P:=\gamma\prod_{j=1}^t
\overline X_j^{a_j}\overline Z_j^{b_j}$.
All factors preserve $\mathcal K_S$, so their matching actions
on that space give
\begin{align*}
    \overline P\ket{v}
    &=V_{\mathrm{glob}}^\dagger
      (P\ket{u}\otimes\ket{0^{M-t}}),\\
    \widehat V_E\overline P\widehat V_E^\dagger
    &=P_T\otimes I_{T^c}.
\end{align*}
Here $P_T$ denotes $P$ acting on the qubits of $T$ in
the chosen order. The second identity also shows that
$\overline P\in\mathcal P_M^\pm$.
Let $\rho_T$ denote the reduced state in the conclusion.
Since $V_E$ acts only on $E$, we also have
$\rho_T=\operatorname{Tr}_{T^c}[\widehat V_E\ket{v}\bra{v}\widehat V_E^\dagger]$.
The preceding identities yield
\[
    \operatorname{Tr}(P\rho_T)
    =\langle v|\overline P|v\rangle
    =\langle u|P|u\rangle,
    \qquad P\in\mathcal P_t.
\]
The phase-free Pauli operators form a basis of the space
of matrices on $t$ qubits by
Appendix~\ref{app:PauliOpsandLabels}, so
$\rho_T=\ket{u}\bra{u}$.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:revmag-clean-decomposition}
Suppose $CQ\ket{0^{n+r}}=\ket{\psi}\ket{0^r}$, where
$Q$ is a matching circuit of depth at most $D$ and
$C\in\mathsf{cliff}_{n+r}$.
Then there exist an integer $0\le t\le n$, a pure $t$-qubit
state $\ket{\phi}$, and a Clifford $U\in\mathsf{cliff}_n$ such that
\[
    \ket{\psi}=U\bigl(\ket{\phi}\ket{0^{n-t}}\bigr).
\]
Moreover, for some integer $m$ satisfying $t\le m\le2^{2D+1}t$,
there exist a matching circuit $Q'$ of depth at most $D$
on $m$ qubits and a Clifford $V\in\mathsf{cliff}_m$ such that
\[
    \ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}
    =\operatorname{Tr}_{\{t+1,\ldots,m\}}\left[
        VQ'\ket{0^m}\bra{0^m}Q'^\dagger V^\dagger
    \right].
\]
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
Set $M:=n+r$ and $\ket{\eta}:=Q\ket{0^M}$.
Clifford invariance of stabilizer nullity and its invariance
under appending zero-state qubits give
$t:=\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\eta)=\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\psi)\le n$.
If $t=0$, then $\psi$ is a stabilizer state, so
$\ket{\psi}=U\ket{0^n}$ for some $U\in\mathsf{cliff}_n$.
The second assertion holds with $m=0$, with the zero-qubit
state and identity represented by the scalar $1$.
Assume henceforth that $t\ge1$.

Set $S:=\mathsf S(\eta)$, and let
$\mathcal G_\eta=\{G\in\mathcal P_M^\pm:G\ket{\eta}=\ket{\eta}\}$
be the full signed Pauli stabilizer group of $\eta$.
Use $\mathcal K_S$ and $W_S$ for its code space and logical
Pauli space as defined above. We have $\dim S=M-t$ and
$\ket{\eta}\in\mathcal K_S$.
We first specify the logical state to recover, then find
a small set supporting its logical Pauli operations,
apply the recovery lemma, and prune the preparation circuit.

\medskip
\noindent
\textit{1. Choosing the logical state to recover.}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:app-stabilizer-nullity-decomposition},
there exist $V_{\mathrm{out}}\in\mathsf{cliff}_n$ and a pure
$t$-qubit state $\ket{\phi}$ with $\mathsf S(\phi)=\{0\}$ such that
\[
    V_{\mathrm{out}}\ket{\psi}
    =\ket{\phi}\otimes\ket{0^{n-t}}.
\]
Thus the first assertion already holds with
$U:=V_{\mathrm{out}}^\dagger$.
Define $V_{\mathrm{glob}}:=(V_{\mathrm{out}}\otimes I_{2^r})C$.
The clean-output identity gives
\[
    V_{\mathrm{glob}}\ket{\eta}
    =(V_{\mathrm{out}}\ket{\psi})\otimes\ket{0^r}
    =\ket{\phi}\otimes\ket{0^{M-t}}.
\]
For $j=t+1,\ldots,M$, the operators
$V_{\mathrm{glob}}^\dagger Z_jV_{\mathrm{glob}}$ stabilize $\eta$.
Their $M-t$ independent labels form a basis of $S$, so
they generate $\mathcal G_\eta$ by
Appendix~\ref{app:IsotropicSubspaces}. It follows that
\[
    V_{\mathrm{glob}}\mathcal K_S
    =\mathbb C^{2^t}
      \otimes\operatorname{span}\{\ket{0^{M-t}}\}.
\]
This specifies the logical state but does not locate it
on a small set of physical qubits, since $V_{\mathrm{glob}}$
may act on all $M$ qubits.

\medskip
\noindent
\textit{2. Finding a small set supporting the logical Pauli operations.}
Set $A_i:=QZ_iQ^\dagger$, $i\in[M]$.
Each $A_i$ is a Hermitian unitary fixing $\eta$.
Moreover, $\eta$ is their unique common $+1$ eigenstate
up to global phase. To see this, let $\ket{v}$ be a normalized
state satisfying $A_i\ket{v}=\ket{v}$ for every $i$.
Multiplication by $Q^\dagger$ gives
\[
    Z_iQ^\dagger\ket{v}=Q^\dagger\ket{v},
    \qquad i\in[M].
\]
These conditions force every qubit of $Q^\dagger\ket{v}$
to be in $\ket{0}$, so
$Q^\dagger\ket{v}=e^{i\theta}\ket{0^M}$ and hence
$\ket{v}=e^{i\theta}\ket{\eta}$.

Since each layer of $Q$ consists of disjoint one- and two-qubit
gates, $A_i$ is supported on at most $2^D$ qubits.
Every nonzero term in its Pauli expansion
$A_i=\sum_{R\in\mathcal P_M}a_i(R)R$ has support contained
in $\operatorname{supp}(A_i)$. Collect the logical classes of the terms
that commute with every stabilizer:
\[
    \mathcal L:=\left\{
        [R]+S:[R]\in S^\perp,\ R\in\mathcal P_M,\
        a_i(R)\ne0\text{ for some }i\in[M]
    \right\}.
\]
We claim that $\operatorname{span}\mathcal L=W_S$.
Otherwise, nondegeneracy of the symplectic form on $W_S$
provides a nonzero class $[P]+S$ orthogonal to this span.
Choose $P\in\mathcal P_M$ representing that class;
in particular, $P^\dagger=P$ and $P^2=I$.

For each term $R$ with $a_i(R)\ne0$, we compare its
expectations in $\eta$ and $P\eta$.
If $[R]\in S^\perp$, then $[R]+S\in\mathcal L$, so $P$
commutes with $R$ and the expectations agree.
If $[R]\notin S^\perp$, some $G\in\mathcal G_\eta$
anticommutes with $R$, giving
\[
    \langle\eta|R|\eta\rangle
    =\langle\eta|GRG|\eta\rangle
    =-\langle\eta|R|\eta\rangle=0.
\]
Since $PRP\in\{R,-R\}$, we also have
$\langle P\eta|R|P\eta\rangle=0$.
Thus every Pauli term has the same expectation
in the two states, and
$\langle P\eta|A_i|P\eta\rangle=1$ for every $i$.
As $A_i$ is a Hermitian unitary,
\[
    \|A_iP\ket{\eta}-P\ket{\eta}\|^2
    =2-2\operatorname{Re}\langle P\eta|A_i|P\eta\rangle=0.
\]
The uniqueness proved above shows that $\ket{\eta}$ is
an eigenvector of $P$. Since $P^2=I$, either $P$ or $-P$
fixes $\ket{\eta}$ and hence belongs to $\mathcal G_\eta$.
Both operators have label $[P]$, so $[P]\in S$,
contradicting the choice of a nonzero class.

Since $\dim W_S=2t$ by Appendix~\ref{app:stabilizer-nullity},
we can select $2t$ classes from $\mathcal L$ forming a basis
of $W_S$. Let $R_1,\ldots,R_{2t}$ be their corresponding
Pauli terms and set
\[
    E:=\bigcup_{j=1}^{2t}\operatorname{supp}(R_j),
    \qquad |E|\le2t\,2^D=2^{D+1}t.
\]
For every $R\in\mathcal P_M^\pm$ preserving $\mathcal K_S$, there are
$c_j\in\{0,1\}$ such that
\[
    [R]+S=\sum_{j=1}^{2t}c_j([R_j]+S).
\]
Thus $[R]=\sum_jc_j[R_j]+[G]$ for some
$G\in\mathcal G_\eta$, and
$R=\gamma R_1^{c_1}\cdots R_{2t}^{c_{2t}}G$
for some $\gamma\in\{+1,-1,+i,-i\}$.
Since $G$ acts as the identity on $\mathcal K_S$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:RepresentationofpreservingPauli}
    R\ket{v}=\gamma R_1^{c_1}\cdots R_{2t}^{c_{2t}}\ket{v},
    \qquad \ket{v}\in\mathcal K_S.
\end{equation}
The operator $\gamma R_1^{c_1}\cdots R_{2t}^{c_{2t}}=RG$
belongs to $\mathcal P_M^\pm$, because $R$ and $G$ commute.
It is supported on $E$, so every logical Pauli class has
a signed Hermitian representative supported on $E$.

\medskip
\noindent
\textit{3. Recovering the prescribed logical state from $E$.}
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:revmag-local-recovery} to this set $E$
and the decoder $V_{\mathrm{glob}}$ chosen in Step~1.
Because $V_{\mathrm{glob}}\ket{\eta}
=\ket{\phi}\otimes\ket{0^{M-t}}$, the lemma gives
a Clifford $V_E$ and an ordered set
$T=\{q_1,\ldots,q_t\}\subseteq E$ such that, with
$\eta_E:=\operatorname{Tr}_{E^c}\ket{\eta}\bra{\eta}$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:revmag-clean-local-recovery}
    \operatorname{Tr}_{E\setminus T}[V_E\eta_EV_E^\dagger]
    =\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}.
\end{equation}
The reduced state $\eta_E$ may be mixed; the identity shows
that applying $V_E$ and retaining $T$ recovers the same
pure state $\phi$ selected in Step~1.

\medskip
\noindent
\textit{4. Pruning the preparation circuit.}
Retain the gates in the backward lightcone of $E$ through $Q$.
They form a circuit $Q'$ of depth at most $D$ on $m$ qubits,
including all qubits in $E$.
Each backward layer increases the number of included qubits
by at most a factor of two. Therefore
\[
    t\le |E|\le m\le2^D|E|\le2^{2D+1}t.
\]
Index the retained qubits with $E$ first and, within $E$,
with $q_1,\ldots,q_t$ first in this order.
The pruning argument from the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:fixed-depth-active-cone-pruning} gives
\[
    \eta_E=\operatorname{Tr}_{\{|E|+1,\ldots,m\}}\left[
        Q'\ket{0^m}\bra{0^m}Q'^\dagger
    \right].
\]
The omitted gates do not affect expectations of operators
on $E$, and the retained input qubits are in $\ket{0^m}$.
Extend $V_E$ by setting
$V:=V_E\otimes I_{2^{m-|E|}}\in\mathsf{cliff}_m$.
Tracing out the remaining qubits and using
\eqref{eq:revmag-clean-local-recovery} yields
\begin{align*}
    \operatorname{Tr}_{\{t+1,\ldots,m\}}\left[
        VQ'\ket{0^m}\bra{0^m}Q'^\dagger V^\dagger
    \right]
    =\operatorname{Tr}_{E\setminus T}[V_E\eta_EV_E^\dagger]
    =\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}.
\end{align*}
Together with $U=V_{\mathrm{out}}^\dagger$ from Step~1,
this proves both assertions.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:revmag-clean-profile-entropy}
For every fixed $D\ge1$, there exists $C_D<\infty$ such that
\[
    \log N\left(
        \varepsilon,
        \mathcal F_{n,p}
        \left(
            \mathsf{revmag}^{[D],\mathrm{clean}}_n
        \right),
        \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \right)
    \le
    C_Dn^2
    +
    C_Dn
    \log\left(
        \frac{C_D3^{p/2}n}{\varepsilon}
    \right)
\]
for every $n\ge p\ge2$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
Fix $n\ge p\ge2$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$.
We first use Proposition~\ref{prop:revmag-clean-decomposition}
to represent every state in the class using circuits on a
common number of qubits. We then count the Clifford choices,
discretize the shallow preparation circuit, and bound the
resulting error in the profile norm.

\textit{1. Reducing to a common circuit width: }
Set $m_*:=2^{2D+1}n$.
By Proposition~\ref{prop:revmag-clean-decomposition}, every
$\ket{\psi}\in\mathsf{revmag}^{[D],\mathrm{clean}}_n$ can be written as
$\ket{\psi}=U(\ket{\phi}\ket{0^{n-t}})$, where
$0\le t\le n$, $U\in\mathsf{cliff}_n$, and $\ket{\phi}$ is obtained
by retaining the first $t$ qubits of a matching circuit of depth at most $D$ followed by a Clifford on at most
$2^{2D+1}t\le m_*$ qubits.
Append unused qubits in $\ket{0}$ and extend both circuits
by the identity to obtain a realization on exactly $m_*$
qubits. This preserves the depth and the reduced state on
the first $t$ qubits.

We now express the reduced logical state and the final
$n$-qubit state as density matrices. Set $\omega_*:=\ket{0^{m_*}}\bra{0^{m_*}}$ and, for
$U\in\mathsf{cliff}_n$, $V\in\mathsf{cliff}_{m_*}$, and a matching circuit
$Q$ of depth at most $D$ on $m_*$ qubits, define
\begin{align*}
    \sigma_t(V,Q)
    &:=\operatorname{Tr}_{\{t+1,\ldots,m_*\}}
        \left[VQ\omega_*Q^\dagger V^\dagger\right],\\
    \rho_t(U,V,Q)
    &:=U\left(
        \sigma_t(V,Q)\otimes
        \ket{0^{n-t}}\bra{0^{n-t}}
    \right)U^\dagger.
\end{align*}
Every target density matrix $\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}$ has this
form for some $t,U,V,Q$.
For $t=0$, the partial trace defining $\sigma_0(V,Q)$ is
the scalar $1$, so $\rho_0(U,V,Q)=U\ket{0^n}\bra{0^n}U^\dagger$.
Thus the same family also covers the zero-nullity case.
The full family may contain mixed states; we will account
for this when choosing the centers of the final cover.

For $k=n,m_*$, let $\mathcal C_k$ contain one unitary
representative of each $k$-qubit Clifford modulo global phase.
The Clifford count used in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:higher-magic-entropy} gives $|\mathcal C_k|\le\exp(Ck^2)$.

Global phases cancel in the density matrices above, so
we may restrict $U$ and $V$ to $\mathcal C_n$ and
$\mathcal C_{m_*}$, respectively, without changing the family.

\textit{2. Covering the preparation circuits: }
An architecture specifies the gate locations in each layer.
For each qubit in a layer, there are $m_*-1$ possible
partners for a two-qubit gate, one possibility for a
one-qubit gate, and one for no gate.
Every valid layer determines a labeling with $m_*+1$
choices per qubit. There are therefore at most
$(m_*+1)^{Dm_*}$ architectures with $D$ layers, including
circuits of smaller depth by allowing empty layers.
Since gate supports within a layer are disjoint, each
architecture has at most $Dm_*$ gate locations.

Fix $0<\delta<1$, to be chosen below.
As in Lemma~\ref{lem:gate-count-profile-entropy}, choose
operator-norm $\delta$-nets for $\mathsf U(2)$ and
$\mathsf U(4)$, with centers in the respective unitary
groups and cardinalities at most $(C/\delta)^C$.
For each architecture, replace each gate by a point in
the corresponding net. Taking the union over all
architectures gives a finite set $\mathcal Q$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:revmag-clean-circuit-cover-size}
    |\mathcal Q|
    \le
    (m_*+1)^{Dm_*}(C/\delta)^{CDm_*}.
\end{equation}
For every $Q$, there is $\widetilde Q\in\mathcal Q$ with
the same architecture and with corresponding gates
differing by at most $\delta$ in operator norm.

To bound the accumulated error, write
$Q=U_L\cdots U_1$ and
$\widetilde Q=\widetilde U_L\cdots\widetilde U_1$,
where $L\le Dm_*$ and the same ordering of gate locations
is used in both circuits. Each gate is extended by the
identity outside its support. Replacing the gates one
at a time gives
\[
    Q-\widetilde Q
    =\sum_{j=1}^L
        \widetilde U_L\cdots\widetilde U_{j+1}
        (U_j-\widetilde U_j)
        U_{j-1}\cdots U_1,
\]
where empty products are identities.
The factors surrounding $U_j-\widetilde U_j$ are unitary,
so the triangle inequality gives
\[
    \|Q-\widetilde Q\|_{\mathrm{op}}
    \le\sum_{j=1}^L
        \|U_j-\widetilde U_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}
    \le L\delta\le Dm_*\delta.
\]

\textit{3. Transferring the circuit approximation to profiles: }
Fix $t,U,V,Q$ and choose $\widetilde Q$ as above.
Set $\rho:=\rho_t(U,V,Q)$ and
$\widetilde\rho:=\rho_t(U,V,\widetilde Q)$.
Conjugation by a unitary and tensoring with a fixed pure
state preserve the trace norm. Partial trace contracts
the trace norm of the difference of two states.
Keeping $U$ and $V$ unchanged therefore gives
\begin{align*}
    \|\rho-\widetilde\rho\|_1
    &=\|\sigma_t(V,Q)-\sigma_t(V,\widetilde Q)\|_1\\
    &\le\|Q\omega_*Q^\dagger
          -\widetilde Q\omega_*\widetilde Q^\dagger\|_1\\
    &\le\|(Q-\widetilde Q)\omega_*Q^\dagger\|_1
       +\|\widetilde Q\omega_*
           (Q^\dagger-\widetilde Q^\dagger)\|_1\\
    &\le 2\|Q-\widetilde Q\|_{\mathrm{op}}
     \le 2Dm_*\delta,
\end{align*}
where the penultimate inequality uses $\|\omega_*\|_1=1$
and the operator norm one of the unitary factors.

For each $P\in\mathcal P_{n,p}$, we have
$|\operatorname{Tr}(P(\rho-\widetilde\rho))|
\le\|\rho-\widetilde\rho\|_1$, since
$\|P\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1$.
Using $|\mathcal P_{n,p}|=3^p\binom np$ in the definition
of the profile norm gives
\begin{align*}
    \|f_\rho-f_{\widetilde\rho}\|_{n,p}^2
    =\binom np^{-1}
      \sum_{P\in\mathcal P_{n,p}}
        |\operatorname{Tr}(P(\rho-\widetilde\rho))|^2
    \le 3^p\|\rho-\widetilde\rho\|_1^2.
\end{align*}
Consequently, taking
$\delta:=\varepsilon/(8\cdot3^{p/2}Dm_*)$ ensures that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:revmag-clean-profile-approximation}
    \|f_\rho-f_{\widetilde\rho}\|_{n,p}
    \le 2\cdot3^{p/2}Dm_*\delta
    =\frac{\varepsilon}{4}.
\end{equation}
This estimate holds uniformly over $t,U,V,Q$.

\textit{4. Combining the estimates: }
Let $\mathcal F:=
\mathcal F_{n,p}(\mathsf{revmag}^{[D],\mathrm{clean}}_n)$ and form
the finite set
\[
    \mathcal H:=\left\{
        f_{\rho_t(U,V,\widetilde Q)}:
        0\le t\le n,\quad
        U\in\mathcal C_n,\quad
        V\in\mathcal C_{m_*},\quad
        \widetilde Q\in\mathcal Q
    \right\}.
\]
Every profile in $\mathcal F$ lies within $\varepsilon/4$
of some $h\in\mathcal H$, by the representation above
and \eqref{eq:revmag-clean-profile-approximation}.
The points of $\mathcal H$ need not belong to $\mathcal F$,
because discretizing $Q$ may produce a mixed reduced state.
For each $h\in\mathcal H$ whose closed
$\varepsilon/4$-ball meets $\mathcal F$, choose a profile
$g_h$ in that intersection; discard the other centers.
If $f\in\mathcal F$ satisfies
$\|f-h\|_{n,p}\le\varepsilon/4$, then
\[
    \|f-g_h\|_{n,p}
    \le\|f-h\|_{n,p}+\|h-g_h\|_{n,p}
    \le\frac{\varepsilon}{2}.
\]
Thus the chosen $g_h$ form an $\varepsilon$-cover with
centers in $\mathcal F$ and cardinality at most
\[
    |\mathcal H|
    \le(n+1)|\mathcal C_n|\,|\mathcal C_{m_*}|\,|\mathcal Q|.
\]
Combining the Clifford counts with
\eqref{eq:revmag-clean-circuit-cover-size} gives
\begin{align*}
    \log N(\varepsilon,\mathcal F,\|\cdot\|_{n,p})
    &\le\log(n+1)+C(n^2+m_*^2)
       +Dm_*\log(m_*+1)
       +CDm_*\log(C/\delta)\\
    &\le\log(n+1)+C(n^2+m_*^2)
       +Dm_*\log(m_*+1)
       +CDm_*\log\left(
           \frac{C3^{p/2}Dm_*}{\varepsilon}
       \right).
\end{align*}
Since $m_*=2^{2D+1}n$, increasing a constant $C_D$
depending only on $D$ yields
\[
    \log N(\varepsilon,\mathcal F,\|\cdot\|_{n,p})
    \le C_Dn^2
       +C_Dn\log\left(
           \frac{C_D3^{p/2}n}{\varepsilon}
       \right).
\]
Here the architecture count and the factor $n+1$ have
been absorbed into the right-hand side.
The representation and the cover apply to every original
ancillary width, so the bound is uniform over the number
of clean ancillas.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:revmag-clean-ground-gap}
Fix an integer $D\ge1$.  There exists $p_0=p_0(D)<\infty$ such that,
for every fixed $p\ge p_0$, there is $c_{p,D}>0$ for which
\[
    \mathbb P\left(
        \Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n,p}
        \left(
            \mathsf{revmag}^{[D],\mathrm{clean}}_n
        \right)
        \ge
        c_{p,D}\sqrt n
    \right)
    \longrightarrow1.
\]
The conclusion is uniform over the number of clean ancillas.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Fix $D\ge1$ and choose $C_D\ge1$ so that the bound in
Lemma~\ref{lem:revmag-clean-profile-entropy} holds for all
$n\ge p\ge2$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$.
To apply Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}
to the class $\mathsf{revmag}^{[D],\mathrm{clean}}_n$, take
\[
    a_{n,p}:=C_Dn^2,
    \qquad
    b_{n,p}:=C_Dn,
    \qquad
    B_{n,p}:=C_D3^{p/2}n.
\]
These parameters satisfy $a_{n,p},b_{n,p}\ge0$ and
$B_{n,p}\ge1$, and the entropy lemma gives precisely
the required bound
$a_{n,p}+b_{n,p}\log(B_{n,p}/\varepsilon)$.
The corresponding effective profile complexity is
\[
    \Gamma_{n,p}
    :=a_{n,p}+b_{n,p}\log(eB_{n,p}n)
    =C_Dn^2+C_Dn\log\left(eC_D3^{p/2}n^2\right).
\]
For every fixed $p$, we therefore have
\[
    \frac{\Gamma_{n,p}}{n^2}
    =C_D+\frac{C_D}{n}
        \left(2\log n+\log(eC_D)+\frac p2\log3\right)
    \longrightarrow C_D.
\]
In particular, the limiting bound is independent of $p$.
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(i)},
applied with $L=C_D$, supplies a threshold $p_0=p_0(D)$
such that, for every fixed $p\ge p_0$, there is
$c_{p,D}>0$ with
\[
    \mathbb P\left(
        \Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n,p}
        \left(\mathsf{revmag}^{[D],\mathrm{clean}}_n\right)
        \ge c_{p,D}\sqrt n
    \right)\longrightarrow1.
\]
The entropy bound was proved for the full class allowing
every number of clean ancillas. Hence this event gives
the same lower bound simultaneously for every subclass
with a prescribed ancillary width, proving the asserted
uniformity.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
For item~\textup{(i)}, the linear-width ground-state conclusion follows
from Proposition~\ref{prop:dense-magic}\textup{(i)}.  The comparison with
$\mathsf{prod}_n$ in the presence of arbitrary discardable ancillas follows
from Proposition~\ref{prop:dense-magic}\textup{(ii)} under the stated
logarithmic-depth assumption.

For item~\textup{(ii)}, the linear-width conclusion follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:higher-magic-ground-gap} with $k=1$, and the fixed-depth conclusion with arbitrary clean ancillas is
Theorem~\ref{thm:revmag-clean-ground-gap}.  Item~\textup{(iii)} is
Proposition~\ref{prop:higher-magic-ground-gap}, which covers both
orientations for every fixed number of shallow blocks.  In each
linear-width application, choose a fixed $K$ such that $M_n\le Kn$
for all sufficiently large $n$.

Although the proofs assume $D\ge1$, the results also cover
circuits of depth zero. To see this, replace any nonnegative
depth sequence by $\widehat D_n:=\max\{D_n,1\}$. This enlarges the preparation
class while preserving the stated depth bounds for all sufficiently
large $n$, provided the corresponding prefactors $L$ or $c$ are
positive.

If $L=0$, every shallow block is eventually the identity.
The resulting classes are therefore contained in the corresponding
depth-one classes, to which we may apply the theorem with $L=1$.
Similarly, the clean-ancilla class at depth zero is contained in
the class at depth one.

The ground-state gap lower bounds pass to these subclasses.
The product-state comparison also passes to them by monotonicity
of $\Delta^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,p}(\,\cdot\,;\mathsf{prod}_n)$.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lem:nullity-preserving-conditioning}
Let $n\ge p\ge2$ and $t\ge0$ be integers, and suppose $\rho=\operatorname{Tr}_E|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|$ with $\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\Psi)\le t$, where $|\Psi\rangle$ is a pure state on the $n$ qubits and finitely many additional qubits $E$.
For every integer $0\le m_\star\le n-p$, there are
$J\subseteq[n]$ and $\sigma\in\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal B_{n,t})$
such that $|J|\ge n-m_\star$ and 
\[
    \|\mathsf M_J(f_\rho-f_\sigma)\|_{n,p}
    \le c\frac{2^{p/2}p^{3/2}}{\sqrt{m_\star+1}},
\]
where $c>0$ is a universal constant.
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
We first construct a mixture of product states approximating
the local marginals of $\rho$. We then show that each product
state in the mixture can be chosen with at most $t$ factors
that are not one-qubit stabilizer states.

\textit{1. Construct the conditioning approximation.}
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:measurement-parametrized-definetti}
to $\rho$ with measurement budget $m_\star$ and the Pauli POVM in \eqref{eq:pauli-conditioning-measurement}.
This gives a set $S$ of measured qubits with $|S|\le m_\star$.
Let $J=[n]\setminus S$ denote the unmeasured qubits.

Let $q(z)$ and $\rho_{J\mid z}$ be the outcome probabilities
and conditional states defined in
\eqref{eq:conditioning-state-convention}.
For each $z$ with $q(z)>0$, define
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:t-count-conditional-products}
    \rho_{i\mid z}
    :=\operatorname{Tr}_{J\setminus\{i\}}(\rho_{J\mid z}),
    \qquad
    \theta_{J,z}
    :=\bigotimes_{i\in J}\rho_{i\mid z}.
\end{equation}
Thus $\theta_{J,z}$ is the product of the one-qubit marginals
of $\rho_{J\mid z}$. Averaging these products gives
\[
    \eta_J:=\sum_{z:q(z)>0}q(z)\theta_{J,z}.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:measurement-parametrized-definetti} then guarantees
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:t-count-conditioned-marginal-error}
    \frac1{\binom{|J|}{p}}
    \sum_{\substack{I\subseteq J\\|I|=p}}
        \|\rho_I-(\eta_J)_I\|_1^2
    \le C\frac{p^3}{m_\star+1}.
\end{equation}

\textit{2. Identify the exceptional factors.}
We now perform the same measurements on $S$ in the full pure state
$|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|$, retaining the extra qubits $E$.
By Corollary~\ref{cor:conditioning-extensions}, the outcome
probabilities are again $q(z)$. Since the Pauli POVM has
rank-one effects, the joint conditional state is pure.
Writing it as
$\widehat\rho_{JE\mid z}=|\Psi_z\rangle\langle\Psi_z|$, we have
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:t-count-conditional-marginals}
\begin{aligned}
    \rho_{J\mid z}
    &=\operatorname{Tr}_E\widehat\rho_{JE\mid z},\\
    \rho_{i\mid z}
    &=\operatorname{Tr}_{J\setminus\{i\}}(\rho_{J\mid z})
      =\operatorname{Tr}_{(J\setminus\{i\})\cup E}
          \widehat\rho_{JE\mid z},
    \qquad i\in J.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:app-nullity-conditioning}\textup{(ii)}, conditioning on Pauli measurement outcomes does not increase
nullity, so
\[
    \nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\Psi_z)
    \le\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\Psi)\le t.
\]
Applying part~\textup{(iii)} of that lemma to $|\Psi_z\rangle$
and using \eqref{eq:t-count-conditional-marginals} gives
\[
    F_z:=\left\{
        i\in J:
        \rho_{i\mid z}\notin\operatorname{conv}(\mathsf{pstab}_{\{i\}})
    \right\},
    \qquad
    |F_z|\le\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\Psi_z)\le t.
\]
Here $F_z$ is the set of sites $i\in J$ whose conditional
marginals $\rho_{i\mid z}$ cannot be written as mixtures of
pure one-qubit stabilizer states. These are the sites at
which the decomposition below requires non-stabilizer factors.

Fix an outcome $z$ with $q(z)>0$. For $i\in J\setminus F_z$,
decompose $\rho_{i\mid z}$ into pure one-qubit stabilizer states.
For $i\in F_z$, use its spectral decomposition into arbitrary
pure states. In both cases, write
\[
    \rho_{i\mid z}
    =\sum_\ell\lambda_{i,z,\ell}
        |\phi_{i,z,\ell}\rangle\langle\phi_{i,z,\ell}|,
    \qquad
    \lambda_{i,z,\ell}\ge0,\quad
    \sum_\ell\lambda_{i,z,\ell}=1.
\]
Expanding the tensor product in
\eqref{eq:t-count-conditional-products} gives
\[
    \theta_{J,z}
    =
    \sum_{(\ell_i)_{i\in J}}
        \left(\prod_{i\in J}\lambda_{i,z,\ell_i}\right)
        \bigotimes_{i\in J}
        |\phi_{i,z,\ell_i}\rangle\langle\phi_{i,z,\ell_i}|.
\]
For every pure product state $\tau$ appearing in this sum,
\[
    E_J(\tau)\subseteq F_z,
    \qquad
    |E_J(\tau)|\le t,
    \qquad
    \tau\in\mathcal B_{J,t}.
\]
The coefficients are nonnegative and sum to one. Consequently,
\[
    \theta_{J,z}\in\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal B_{J,t}),
    \qquad
    \eta_J=\sum_{z:q(z)>0}q(z)\theta_{J,z}
    \in\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal B_{J,t}).
\]

\textit{3. Extend the approximation and bound the profile error.}
Append $|0\rangle\langle0|$ at every site in $S$, defining
\[
    \sigma
    :=\eta_J\otimes\bigotimes_{i\in S}|0\rangle\langle0|_i.
\]
These additional factors are one-qubit stabilizer states, so
\[
    \sigma\in\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal B_{n,t}),
    \qquad
    \sigma_I=(\eta_J)_I
    \quad\text{for }I\subseteq J.
\]
Pauli orthogonality and
\eqref{eq:t-count-conditioned-marginal-error} therefore give
\begin{align*}
    \|\mathsf M_J(f_\rho-f_\sigma)\|_{n,p}^2
    &\le\frac{2^p}{\binom np}
        \sum_{\substack{I\subseteq J\\|I|=p}}
        \|\rho_I-(\eta_J)_I\|_1^2
    \le c\frac{2^pp^3}{m_\star+1}
        \frac{\binom{|J|}{p}}{\binom np}
    \le c\frac{2^pp^3}{m_\star+1}.
\end{align*}
Taking square roots proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- corollary-10: body_md -->
\label{cor:t-count-conditioning-benchmark}
For every sequence $(t_n)_{n\ge1}$ of nonnegative integers,
$(\mathcal B_{n,t_n})_{n\ge1}$ is a conditioning benchmark for
$(\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,t_n})_{n\ge1}$ in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:conditioning-benchmark}.
<!-- end corollary-10 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
Fix $p\ge2$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$.
Let $\rho\in\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,t_n}$, and let
$|\Psi\rangle$ be its full circuit output before the
additional qubits $E$ are discarded.
The initial state has nullity zero, Clifford gates preserve
nullity, and each $T$-gate increases it by at most one,
by Lemma~\ref{lem:app-nullity-conditioning}\textup{(i)}.
Consequently,
\[
    \rho=\operatorname{Tr}_E|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|,
    \qquad
    \nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\Psi)\le t_n.
\]

We may therefore apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:nullity-preserving-conditioning}
with $t=t_n$ and $m_\star=\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor$.
For all sufficiently large $n$, this budget satisfies
$m_\star\le n-p$. The lemma gives $J\subseteq[n]$ and
$\sigma\in\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal B_{n,t_n})$ such that
\[
    |J|\ge n-\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor\ge(1-\alpha)n
\]
and
\[
    \|\mathsf M_J(f_\rho-f_\sigma)\|_{n,p}^2
    \le
    C\frac{2^pp^3}{\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor+1}
    \le
    C\frac{2^pp^3}{\alpha n}
    =O_{p,\alpha}(n^{-1}).
\]
The bound is uniform over $\rho$ and independent of $t_n$,
which verifies the conditioning-benchmark property.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{lem:t-count-fixed-projection}
Set
\[
    |a\rangle:=\frac{|0\rangle+e^{-i\pi/4}|1\rangle}{\sqrt2},
    \qquad \Pi_a:=|a\rangle\langle a|.
\]
For every $\rho\in\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,t}$, there exists
$\tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_{n+t}$ such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:t-count-fixed-projection}
    \rho
    =2^t\bigl(I_{2^n}\otimes\langle a|^{\otimes t}\bigr)
      \tau\bigl(I_{2^n}\otimes|a\rangle^{\otimes t}\bigr).
\end{equation}
In particular,
$\operatorname{Tr}[(I_{2^n}\otimes\Pi_a^{\otimes t})\tau]=2^{-t}$.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
We first express a single $T$-gate using an extra qubit, a CNOT,
and a fixed contraction. We then apply this construction throughout
the circuit and trace out the original ancillary qubits.

\textit{1. Replacing a single $T$-gate.}
Let $|\psi\rangle_i=\alpha|0\rangle_i+\beta|1\rangle_i$ be an arbitrary
one-qubit state. By definition,
\[
    T_i|\psi\rangle_i
    =
    \alpha|0\rangle_i+e^{i\pi/4}\beta|1\rangle_i.
\]

Appending an extra qubit $j$ in the state $|0\rangle_j$ gives
\[
    (I\otimes|0\rangle_j)|\psi\rangle_i
    =
    |\psi\rangle_i\otimes|0\rangle_j
    =
    \alpha|0\rangle_i|0\rangle_j
    +\beta|1\rangle_i|0\rangle_j.
\]
The controlled-NOT gate with control qubit $i$ and target qubit $j$
is defined by
\[
    \operatorname{CNOT}_{i\to j}
    (|x\rangle_i\otimes|y\rangle_j)
    =
    |x\rangle_i\otimes|x\oplus y\rangle_j,
    \qquad x,y\in\{0,1\},
\]
where $\oplus$ denotes addition modulo $2$. Applying it gives
\[
    \operatorname{CNOT}_{i\to j}
    (|\psi\rangle_i\otimes|0\rangle_j)
    =
    \alpha|0\rangle_i|0\rangle_j
    +\beta|1\rangle_i|1\rangle_j.
\]

We next apply $I\otimes\langle a|_j$, which takes the inner product
on qubit $j$ and leaves a vector on qubit $i$. We obtain
\begin{align*}
    (I\otimes\langle a|_j)
    \bigl(
        \alpha|0\rangle_i|0\rangle_j
        +\beta|1\rangle_i|1\rangle_j
    \bigr) 
    &=
    \alpha\langle a|0\rangle\,|0\rangle_i
    +\beta\langle a|1\rangle\,|1\rangle_i \\
    &=
    \frac1{\sqrt2}
    \bigl(
        \alpha|0\rangle_i
        +e^{i\pi/4}\beta|1\rangle_i
    \bigr)
    =
    \frac1{\sqrt2}\,T_i|\psi\rangle_i.
\end{align*}
We have therefore shown that
\[
    \sqrt2\,
    (I\otimes\langle a|_j)
    \operatorname{CNOT}_{i\to j}
    (I\otimes|0\rangle_j)|\psi\rangle_i
    =
    T_i|\psi\rangle_i.
\]
Since $|\psi\rangle_i$ was arbitrary, this proves the operator identity
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:t-gate-contraction}
    T_i
    =
    \sqrt2\,
    (I\otimes\langle a|_j)
    \operatorname{CNOT}_{i\to j}
    (I\otimes|0\rangle_j).
\end{equation}
If qubit $i$ belongs to an $M$-qubit system, tensoring
\eqref{eq:t-gate-contraction} with the identity on the other
$M-1$ qubits gives
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:t-gate-contraction-extended}
    T_i
    =
    \sqrt2\,
    (I^{\otimes M}\otimes\langle a|_j)
    \operatorname{CNOT}_{i\to j}
    (I^{\otimes M}\otimes|0\rangle_j),
\end{equation}
where $T_i=I^{\otimes(i-1)}\otimes T\otimes I^{\otimes(M-i)}$.


\textit{2. Replacing all $T$-gates.}
Choose $M\ge n$ and a Clifford+$T$ circuit $U$ on $M$ qubits,
containing $s\le t$ $T$-gates, such that
\[
    |\Psi\rangle:=U|0^M\rangle,
    \qquad
    \rho=\operatorname{Tr}_{n+1,\ldots,M}(|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|).
\]

First consider a circuit with one $T$-gate, $U=C_1T_iC_0$.
Since $C_0$ and $C_1$ act only on the original $M$ qubits,
the extra qubit can be appended before $C_0$ is applied and contracted
after $C_1$ is applied. Specifically, by \eqref{eq:t-gate-contraction-extended} 
\begin{align*}
    C_1T_iC_0
    &=
    \sqrt2\,C_1
    (I^{\otimes M}\otimes\langle a|_j)
    \operatorname{CNOT}_{i\to j}
    (I^{\otimes M}\otimes|0\rangle_j)C_0 \\
    &=
    \sqrt2\,
    (I^{\otimes M}\otimes\langle a|_j)
    (C_1\otimes I)
    \operatorname{CNOT}_{i\to j}
    (I^{\otimes M}\otimes|0\rangle_j)C_0 \\
    &=
    \sqrt2\,
    (I^{\otimes M}\otimes\langle a|_j)
    (C_1\otimes I)
    \operatorname{CNOT}_{i\to j}
    (C_0\otimes I)
    (I^{\otimes M}\otimes|0\rangle_j).
\end{align*}

For the general circuit, write
\[
    U=C_sT_{i_s}C_{s-1}\cdots T_{i_1}C_0,
    \qquad C_0,\ldots,C_s\in\mathsf{cliff}_M.
\]
We introduce $t$ extra qubits, labelled $M+1,\ldots,M+t$,
all initialized in $|0\rangle$ and replace the $k$-th $T$-gate
by $\operatorname{CNOT}_{i_k\to M+k}$. Each occurrence uses
a different extra qubit, even if some of the indices $i_k$
coincide. This gives the Clifford circuit
\[
    \widetilde U
    :=
    (C_s\otimes I^{\otimes t})
    \operatorname{CNOT}_{i_s\to M+s}
    (C_{s-1}\otimes I^{\otimes t})
    \cdots
    \operatorname{CNOT}_{i_1\to M+1}
    (C_0\otimes I^{\otimes t}).
\]
The last $t-s$ extra qubits are untouched. For $s=0$, take
$\widetilde U=C_0\otimes I^{\otimes t}$.

No later gate acts on an extra qubit after its CNOT.
Consequently, as in the one-gate example, all extra qubits
can be appended at the beginning and all contractions
postponed until the end. Each used extra qubit implements
its $T$-gate with a factor $2^{-1/2}$, while each unused
extra qubit contributes $\langle a|0\rangle=2^{-1/2}$.
Therefore,
\[
    U
    =
    2^{t/2}
    (I^{\otimes M}\otimes\langle a|^{\otimes t})
    \widetilde U
    (I^{\otimes M}\otimes|0^t\rangle).
\]

\textit{3. Tracing out the original ancillary qubits.}
Using the representation of $U$ from Step~2, we obtain
\begin{align*}
    |\Psi\rangle
    &=U|0^M\rangle \\
    &=
    2^{t/2}
    (I^{\otimes M}\otimes\langle a|^{\otimes t})
    \widetilde U
    (I^{\otimes M}\otimes|0^t\rangle)|0^M\rangle \\
    &=
    2^{t/2}
    (I^{\otimes M}\otimes\langle a|^{\otimes t})
    \widetilde U
    (|0^M\rangle\otimes|0^t\rangle) \\
    &=
    2^{t/2}
    (I^{\otimes M}\otimes\langle a|^{\otimes t})
    \widetilde U|0^{M+t}\rangle.
\end{align*}
Set $|\Phi\rangle:=\widetilde U|0^{M+t}\rangle$.
Since $\widetilde U$ is Clifford, $|\Phi\rangle$ is a pure
stabilizer state. Taking outer products gives
\[
    |\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|
    =
    2^t
    (I^{\otimes M}\otimes\langle a|^{\otimes t})
    |\Phi\rangle\langle\Phi|
    (I^{\otimes M}\otimes|a\rangle^{\otimes t}).
\]
Substituting into the definition of $\rho$, we have
\begin{align*}
    \rho
    &=
    \operatorname{Tr}_{n+1,\ldots,M}(|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|) \\
    &=
    2^t\operatorname{Tr}_{n+1,\ldots,M}\!\left[
        (I^{\otimes M}\otimes\langle a|^{\otimes t})
        |\Phi\rangle\langle\Phi|
        (I^{\otimes M}\otimes|a\rangle^{\otimes t})
    \right] \\
    &=
    2^t
    (I^{\otimes n}\otimes\langle a|^{\otimes t})
    \operatorname{Tr}_{n+1,\ldots,M}(|\Phi\rangle\langle\Phi|)
    (I^{\otimes n}\otimes|a\rangle^{\otimes t}).
\end{align*}
The last equality holds because the partial trace acts on
the original ancillary qubits $n+1,\ldots,M$, whereas the
contractions act on the extra qubits $M+1,\ldots,M+t$.

Now define $\tau
    :=
    \operatorname{Tr}_{n+1,\ldots,M}(|\Phi\rangle\langle\Phi|)$. This state retains the first $n$ original qubits and all $t$
extra qubits. Since it is a reduction of the pure stabilizer
state $|\Phi\rangle$, we have
$\tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_{n+t}$. The preceding calculation gives
\[
    \rho
    =
    2^t
    (I^{\otimes n}\otimes\langle a|^{\otimes t})
    \tau
    (I^{\otimes n}\otimes|a\rangle^{\otimes t}),
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:t-count-fixed-projection}.
Taking traces yields
\[
    1=\operatorname{Tr}\rho
    =
    2^t\operatorname{Tr}\bigl[
        (I^{\otimes n}\otimes\Pi_a^{\otimes t})\tau
    \bigr],
\]
and hence the stated probability $2^{-t}$.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{lem:t-count-profile-entropy}
There is a universal constant $C<\infty$ such that, for every
$n\ge p\ge2$, integer $t\ge0$, and $0<\varepsilon<1$,
\[
    \log N\left(
        \varepsilon,
        \mathcal F_{n,p}(\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,t}),
        \|\cdot\|_{n,p}
    \right)
    \le
    C(n+t)\left[
        t+\log\left(\frac{C3^{p/2}}{\varepsilon}\right)
    \right].
\]
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
Fix $n\ge p\ge2$, $t\ge0$, and $0<\varepsilon<1$, and set
$m:=n+t$ and
$\mathcal F:=\mathcal F_{n,p}(\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,t})$.

\textit{1. Expressing output expectations through stabilizer profiles.}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:t-count-fixed-projection}, every
$\rho\in\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,t}$ has a representing
state $\tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_m$ satisfying
\eqref{eq:t-count-fixed-projection}.
For any $Q\in\mathcal P_{n,p}$, 
\begin{align*}
    f_\rho(Q)
    &=
    2^t\operatorname{Tr}\left[
        Q(I^{\otimes n}\otimes\langle a|^{\otimes t})
        \tau(I^{\otimes n}\otimes|a\rangle^{\otimes t})
    \right] \\
    &=
    2^t\operatorname{Tr}\left[
        (I^{\otimes n}\otimes|a\rangle^{\otimes t})
        Q(I^{\otimes n}\otimes\langle a|^{\otimes t})\tau
    \right] \\
    &=
    2^t\operatorname{Tr}\left[
        (Q\otimes\Pi_a^{\otimes t})\tau
    \right] \\
    &=
    \operatorname{Tr}\left[
        \bigl(Q\otimes(2\Pi_a)^{\otimes t}\bigr)\tau
    \right],
\end{align*}
where $\Pi_a = \ket{a}\bra{a}$.

By definition of $|a\rangle$, we have
\[
    2\Pi_a
    =I+\frac{X-Y}{\sqrt2}
    =\sum_{P\in\mathcal P_1}b_PP,
\]
where $b_I:=1$, $b_X:=1/\sqrt2$, $b_Y:=-1/\sqrt2$,
and $b_Z:=0$.
Expanding the tensor product amounts to choosing a Pauli operator
at each position and multiplying its coefficients. Thus
\[
    (2\Pi_a)^{\otimes t}
    =
    \sum_{R\in\mathcal P_t}
        \left(\prod_{k=1}^t b_{R_k}\right)R.
\]
Since $b_Z=0$, only the $3^t$ strings with factors in
$\{I,X,Y\}$ have nonzero coefficients.
For $t=0$, the expansion consists of the scalar $1$,
with the empty product interpreted as $1$.

Now fix $Q_1,\ldots,Q_q\in\mathcal P_{n,p}$.
Each operator $Q_i\otimes(2\Pi_a)^{\otimes t}$ is a linear
combination of $3^t$ Pauli strings of the form $Q_i\otimes R$,
where $R\in\mathcal P_t$ contains no $Z$ factors.
Collect the distinct Pauli strings appearing across these
$q$ expansions into a single list $P_1,\ldots,P_N$.
Each acts on $m=n+t$ qubits, and $N\le q3^t$. Write
\[
    Q_i\otimes(2\Pi_a)^{\otimes t}
    =
    \sum_{j=1}^N a_{ij}P_j,
    \qquad i=1,\ldots,q,
\]
with $a_{ij}=0$ whenever $P_j$ does not appear in the $i$-th
expansion. Taking expectations against $\tau$ gives
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:t-count-profile-linear-map}
    f_\rho(Q_i)
    =
    \operatorname{Tr}\left[
        \bigl(Q_i\otimes(2\Pi_a)^{\otimes t}\bigr)\tau
    \right] 
    =
    \sum_{j=1}^N a_{ij}\operatorname{Tr}(P_j\tau)
    =
    \sum_{j=1}^N a_{ij}f_\tau(P_j),
    \qquad i=1,\ldots,q.
\end{equation}
The collection $P_1,\ldots,P_N$ and the coefficients $a_{ij}$ are
fixed once $t$ and $Q_1,\ldots,Q_q$ are chosen and they do not
depend on $\rho$ or $\tau$.

\textit{2. Counting the possible response vectors.}
Equation~\eqref{eq:t-count-profile-linear-map} shows that
the values $f_\tau(P_j)$, $1\le j\le N$, determine all
the queried output expectations $f_\rho(Q_i)$, $1\le i\le q$. Counting every $\tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_m$ can only enlarge
the set of possible input response vectors. Hence
Lemma~\ref{lem:fixed-depth-mixed-stabilizer-growth} gives
\begin{align*}
    \#\left\{
        (f(Q_1),\ldots,f(Q_q)):f\in\mathcal F
    \right\}
    &\le
    \#\left\{
        (f_\tau(P_1),\ldots,f_\tau(P_N)):
        \tau\in\mathsf{mixstab}_m
    \right\}\\
    &\le\left(\sum_{j=0}^m\binom Nj\right)^2
     \le\left(\sum_{j=0}^m\binom{q3^t}{j}\right)^2.
\end{align*}
For every $q\ge2m$, we have $q3^t\ge m$, and so a binomial
bound yields
\[
    \left(\sum_{j=0}^m\binom{q3^t}{j}\right)^2
    \le\left(\frac{eq3^t}{m}\right)^{2m}
    =\left(\frac{Aq}{d}\right)^d,
\]
where $d:=2m$, $A:=2e3^t$. This verifies the restriction-growth hypothesis of
Lemma~\ref{lem:growth-entropy} for every required $q$.

\textit{3. Converting the growth bound to profile entropy.}
Every $f\in\mathcal F$ takes values in $[-1,1]$, since it
is the profile of a normalized output state and every
Pauli has operator norm one.
