Let $\mu_{n,p}$ be the uniform probability measure on
$\mathcal P_{n,p}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:growth-entropy} then gives, for
$0<\delta<1$,
\begin{align*}
    \log N(\delta,\mathcal F,L_2(\mu_{n,p}))
    &\le Cd\log\left(\frac{eA}{\delta}\right)
    \le Cm\left[t+\log\left(\frac C\delta\right)\right].
\end{align*}
For any function $h$ on the retained output Paulis,
\[
    \|h\|_{L_2(\mu_{n,p})}^2
    =\frac1{3^p\binom np}
       \sum_{Q\in\mathcal P_{n,p}}|h(Q)|^2
    =3^{-p}\|h\|_{n,p}^2.
\]
An $L_2(\mu_{n,p})$-cover of radius
$\delta:=\varepsilon/3^{p/2}$ is therefore an
$\varepsilon$-cover in $\|\cdot\|_{n,p}$.
Substituting this value and $m=n+t$ gives the stated bound.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Suppose $t_n\le\kappa n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:t-count-profile-entropy}, we may take
\[
    a_{n,p}:=C(n+t_n)t_n,
    \qquad b_{n,p}:=C(n+t_n),
    \qquad B_{n,p}:=C3^{p/2}
\]
in Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle},
where $C\ge1$ is universal.
The effective complexity
$\Gamma_{n,p}:=a_{n,p}+b_{n,p}\log(eB_{n,p}n)$ therefore satisfies
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:t-count-effective-complexity}
    \frac{\Gamma_{n,p}}{n^2}
    =C\left(1+\frac{t_n}{n}\right)
       \left[
           \frac{t_n}{n}
           +\frac{\log(eC3^{p/2}n)}{n}
       \right].
\end{equation}
For every fixed $p$, it follows that
\[
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{\Gamma_{n,p}}{n^2}
    \le C\kappa(1+\kappa).
\]
Since this bound is independent of $p$,
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(i)}
implies that, for every sufficiently large fixed $p$
depending on $\kappa$, there is $c_{p,\kappa}>0$ such that
\[
    \mathbb P\left(
        \Delta^{\mathrm{opt}}_{n,p}
        (\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,t_n})
        \ge c_{p,\kappa}\sqrt n
    \right)\longrightarrow1.
\]
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{lem:pstab-exceptional-site-cost}
For integers $n\ge p\ge2$ and $0\le t\le n-p$,
\[
    0\le
    \mathbb E\left[M_{n,p}(\mathcal B_{n,t})-M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)\right]
    \le C3^{p/2}\sqrt{pt},
\]
where $C>0$ is a universal constant.
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Let $\omega\in\mathcal B_{n,t}$.
Let $F:=E_{[n]}(\omega)$, so $|F|\le t$, and define
\[
    \omega'
    :=\bigotimes_{i=1}^n\omega_i',
    \qquad
    \omega_i':=
    \begin{cases}
        |0\rangle\langle0|_i, & i\in F,\\
        \omega_i, & i\notin F,
    \end{cases}
\]
where $\omega_i$ is the one-qubit marginal of $\omega$.
Every factor of $\omega'$ is a pure one-qubit stabilizer
state, so $\omega'\in\mathsf{pstab}_n$.

The states $\omega$ and $\omega'$ have identical marginals
on $F^c$. Write
\[
    H_{\mathrm{hit}(F)}
    :=
    \frac{1}{\sqrt{\binom np}}
    \sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{n,p}\\
                    \operatorname{supp}(P)\cap F\ne\emptyset}}
        g_P P,
\]
where $g_P$ are the same Gaussian coefficients as in $H_{n,p}$.
Thus $H_{\mathrm{hit}(F)}$ contains the interactions
involving at least one qubit in $F$.

We then have
\begin{align*}
    \left|\operatorname{Tr}[H_{n,p}(\omega-\omega')]\right|
    &=\left|\operatorname{Tr}[H_{\mathrm{hit}(F)}(\omega-\omega')]\right|
    \le \|H_{\mathrm{hit}(F)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
        \|\omega-\omega'\|_1
    \le 2\|H_{\mathrm{hit}(F)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\end{align*}
The first inequality uses
$|\operatorname{Tr}(AB)|\le\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|B\|_1$. The second follows from
$\|\omega-\omega'\|_1\le\|\omega\|_1+\|\omega'\|_1=2$.
Since $\mathsf{pstab}_n\subseteq\mathcal B_{n,t}$, taking the supremum
over $\omega$ yields
\[
    0\le M_{n,p}(\mathcal B_{n,t})-M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)
    \le2\max_{\substack{F\subseteq[n]\\|F|\le t}}
        \|H_{\mathrm{hit}(F)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Taking expectations and applying
Lemma~\ref{lem:revmag-hit-bound} with budget $t$
proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
Suppose $t_n=o(n)$ and fix $p\ge2$.
Set $\mathcal C_n=\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,t_n}$ and
$\mathcal B_n=\mathcal B_{n,t_n}$.
We have shown that $\mathcal B_n$ is a conditioning benchmark
for $\mathcal C_n$, and
\eqref{eq:t-count-effective-complexity} gives
$\Gamma_{n,p}=o(n^2)$.
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(ii)}
therefore implies
\[
    \frac{[M_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n)-M_{n,p}(\mathcal B_n)]_+}
         {\sqrt n}
    \longrightarrow0
\]
in $L^1$.
For sufficiently large $n$, we also have $t_n\le n-p$, so
Lemma~\ref{lem:pstab-exceptional-site-cost} gives
\[
    0\le
    \frac{\mathbb E[M_{n,p}(\mathcal B_n)-M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)]}{\sqrt n}
    \le C3^{p/2}\sqrt{\frac{pt_n}{n}}
    \longrightarrow0.
\]
Product Pauli eigenstates belong to both $\mathcal B_n$ and
$\mathcal C_n$. Hence
\begin{align*}
    0
    &\le M_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n)-M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)\\
    &\le[M_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n)-M_{n,p}(\mathcal B_n)]_+
       +M_{n,p}(\mathcal B_n)-M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n).
\end{align*}
After division by $\sqrt n$, both terms on the right are
nonnegative and have expectations tending to zero. Thus
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:t-count-product-stabilizer-comparison}
    \frac{M_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n)-M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)}{\sqrt n}
    \longrightarrow0
\end{equation}
in $L^1$ and in probability.
The large-$p$ assertion follows from the benchmark calculation
in Subsection~\ref{subsec:product-stabilizer-value}.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- corollary-11: body_md -->
\label{thm:clifford-product-stabilizer}
For every fixed $p\ge2$,
\[
    \frac{
        M_{n,p}(\mathsf{stab}_n)-M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)
    }{\sqrt n}
    \longrightarrow0
\]
in $L^1$ and in probability.
<!-- end corollary-11 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
With no $T$ gates, the output is a reduced state of a pure stabilizer
state, so $\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,0}=\mathsf{mixstab}_n$.
Such reduced states are mixtures of pure stabilizer states; see
Appendix~\ref{app:IsotropicSubspaces}. Consequently,
\[
    \mathsf{stab}_n
    \subseteq\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,0}
    \subseteq\operatorname{conv}(\mathsf{stab}_n).
\]
Linearity of the energy gives
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:t-count-zero-energy}
    M_{n,p}(\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,0})
    =M_{n,p}(\mathsf{stab}_n).
\end{equation}
The claim follows by setting $t_n=0$ in
\eqref{eq:t-count-product-stabilizer-comparison}.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{lem:pstab-thermodynamic-limit}
For every fixed $p\ge2$, the limit
\[
    \lim_{n\to\infty}
    \frac{\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)}{\sqrt n}
\]
exists.
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
Set $G_n(u):=\sqrt n\,X_u$. For $\beta>0$, define the
normalized expected free energy
\[
    F_{n,\beta}
    :=
    \frac1{\beta n}\mathbb E\log
    \sum_{u\in\mathcal A^n}\exp\bigl(\beta G_n(u)\bigr).
\]
The elementary bounds
\[
    \max_u G_n(u)
    \le
    \frac1\beta\log\sum_u e^{\beta G_n(u)}
    \le
    \max_u G_n(u)+\frac{n\log6}{\beta}
\]
give
\[
    0\le
    F_{n,\beta}
    -\frac{\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)}{\sqrt n}
    \le\frac{\log6}{\beta}.
\]
Thus, it suffices to prove that $F_{n,\beta}$ converges
as $n\to\infty$ for every fixed $\beta>0$.

We first compare the original process with an auxiliary
process that allows repeated site indices.
For $u,v\in\mathcal A^n$, define $q_n(u,v):=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n u_i\cdot v_i$. Expanding its $p$th power gives
\[
    q_n(u,v)^p
    =
    \frac1{n^p}
    \sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_p\in[n]}
        \prod_{k=1}^p(u_{i_k}\cdot v_{i_k}).
\]
On the other hand, writing
$(n)_p:=n(n-1)\cdots(n-p+1)$,
\eqref{eq:pstab-covariance} gives
\[
    \frac1n\mathbb E G_n(u)G_n(v)
    =
    \frac1{(n)_p}
    \sum_{\substack{i_1,\ldots,i_p\in[n]\\
                    \text{all distinct}}}
        \prod_{k=1}^p(u_{i_k}\cdot v_{i_k}).
\]
The first expression averages over all ordered tuples,
whereas the second averages only over tuples with
distinct indices. These correspond to sampling with
and without replacement, respectively.

Extend $q_n$ to $(\mathbb R^3)^n$ by the same formula, and let $\widetilde G_n$ be a centered Gaussian process on this space with
covariance $\mathbb E\widetilde G_n(u)\widetilde G_n(v)
    =
    nq_n(u,v)^p$. Note that for any finite collection of configurations, the overlap matrix $(q_n(u,v))_{u,v}$
is positive semidefinite, and its entrywise $p$th power
is positive semidefinite by the Schur product theorem \cite[Section~7.5]{horn2012matrix}.

To compare the two processes, fix $u,v\in\mathcal A^n$
and let $J_1,\ldots,J_p$ be independent uniform indices
in $[n]$, with $\mathcal D$ denoting the event that they
are all distinct. Setting
$W:=\prod_{k=1}^p(u_{J_k}\cdot v_{J_k})$,
the two covariance formulas above give
\[
    \frac1n\mathbb E\widetilde G_n(u)\widetilde G_n(v)
    =q_n(u,v)^p=\mathbb E W,
    \qquad
    \frac1n\mathbb E G_n(u)G_n(v)
    =\mathbb E[W\mid\mathcal D].
\]
By conditioning on $\mathcal D$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
    \frac1n\mathbb E G_n(u)G_n(v)-q_n(u,v)^p
    &=
    \mathbb P(\mathcal D^c)
    \left(
        \mathbb E[W\mid\mathcal D]
        -
        \mathbb E[W\mid\mathcal D^c]
    \right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Since $|W|\le1$, and since a union bound gives
\[
    \mathbb P(\mathcal D^c)
    \le
    \sum_{1\le k<\ell\le p}\mathbb P(J_k=J_\ell)
    =
    \binom p2\frac1n,
\]
we obtain
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:pstab-with-replacement}
    \left|
        \frac1n\mathbb E G_n(u)G_n(v)-q_n(u,v)^p
    \right|
    \le
    \frac{p(p-1)}n.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
    \sup_{u,v\in\mathcal A^n}
    \left|
        \mathbb E G_n(u)G_n(v)
        -
        \mathbb E\widetilde G_n(u)\widetilde G_n(v)
    \right|
    \le p(p-1).
\]

Define the corresponding auxiliary free energy by
\[
    \widetilde F_{n,\beta}
    :=
    \frac1{\beta n}\mathbb E\log
    \sum_{u\in\mathcal A^n}
        \exp\bigl(\beta\widetilde G_n(u)\bigr).
\]
Both Gaussian processes have variance $n$ at every
configuration $u\in\mathcal A^n$. Gaussian interpolation, as in the proof
of \cite[Lemma~3.2]{bhattacharya2026parisi}, together
with the preceding covariance bound, gives
\begin{align}
\label{eq:interpolation-bd}
    |F_{n,\beta}-\widetilde F_{n,\beta}|
    \le \frac{\beta p(p-1)}{2n}.
\end{align}
For fixed $p$ and $\beta$, this difference tends to zero.
It remains to prove convergence of
$\widetilde F_{n,\beta}$.

We now use \cite[Proposition~8.4]{chen2025free},
following the approach of
\cite[Lemma~3.4]{bhattacharya2026parisi}.
We state explicitly the consequence we need.
The result concerns centered Gaussian processes $Y_n$
with covariance
\[
    \mathbb E Y_n(u)Y_n(v)
    =
    n\xi\bigl(R_n(u,v)\bigr),
    \qquad
    R_n(u,v):=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n u_iv_i^\top.
\]
It averages $e^{Y_n(u)}$ over configurations
$u=(u_1,\ldots,u_n)$ by integrating each $u_i$
independently against the same fixed compactly supported probability measure
on $\mathbb R^3$. We use the uniform measure on the finite set $\mathcal A$,
so this condition holds and the configuration average is $6^{-n}\sum_{u\in\mathcal A^n}e^{Y_n(u)}$.

In the polynomial case used here, the remaining
conditions are that $\xi(0)=0$ and that $\xi$ is convex
on the cone of positive semidefinite $3\times3$ matrices.
Under these conditions, the cited result guarantees
that
\[
    \frac1n\mathbb E\log\left(
        6^{-n}\sum_{u\in\mathcal A^n}e^{Y_n(u)}
    \right)
\]
converges as $n\to\infty$.

We apply this result with $Y_n=\beta\widetilde G_n$.
Since $q_n(u,v)=\operatorname{Tr} R_n(u,v)$, its covariance has
the required form with $\xi_\beta(A):=\beta^2(\operatorname{Tr} A)^p$.

This is a polynomial that vanishes at zero.
On the positive semidefinite cone, the trace is
nonnegative, so convexity of $x\mapsto x^p$ on
$[0,\infty)$ implies convexity of $\xi_\beta$.
Thus all the conditions hold for every integer $p\ge2$.

Proposition~8.4 of \cite{chen2025free} therefore implies
that
\[
    \frac1n\mathbb E\log\left(
        6^{-n}\sum_{u\in\mathcal A^n}
            e^{\beta\widetilde G_n(u)}
    \right)
    =
    \beta\widetilde F_{n,\beta}-\log6
\]
converges. Hence $\widetilde F_{n,\beta}$ converges
for every fixed $\beta>0$, and
\eqref{eq:interpolation-bd} gives the same conclusion
for $F_{n,\beta}$.

Since $F_{n,\beta}$ converges for every fixed $\beta>0$,
the preceding inequality implies
\[
    0\le
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}
        \frac{\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)}{\sqrt n}
    -
    \liminf_{n\to\infty}
        \frac{\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)}{\sqrt n}
    \le \frac{\log6}{\beta}.
\]
Letting $\beta\to\infty$ shows that the limit superior
and limit inferior coincide, proving the claim.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:pstab-value}
There exist universal constants $C>0$ and $p_0\ge2$ such that, for
every integer $p\ge p_0$,
\[
    \sqrt{2\log6}
    -
    C\frac{(\log p)^2}{p}
    \le
    \lim_{n\to\infty}
    \frac{\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)}{\sqrt n}
    \le
    \sqrt{2\log6}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
   \lim_{p\to\infty}
   \lim_{n\to\infty}
    \frac{\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)}{\sqrt n}
    =
    \sqrt{2\log6}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
The existence of the limit follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:pstab-thermodynamic-limit}.

The upper bound follows immediately from the Gaussian maximal
inequality. Since $|\mathcal A^n|=6^n$ and every $X_u$ has variance
one, we have
\[
    \mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)
    \le
    \sqrt{2\log(6^n)}
    =
    \sqrt{2n\log6}.
\]
Therefore
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:pstab-upper}
    \frac{\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)}{\sqrt n}
    \le
    \sqrt{2\log6}.
\end{equation}

For the lower bound, we construct a packing in the canonical
metric of the Gaussian process, $d_X(u,v)
    :=
    (\mathbb E(X_u-X_v)^2)^{1/2}$. Since $\mathbb E X_u^2=1$ for every $u$,
\[
    d_X(u,v)^2
    =
    2\bigl(1-\mathbb E X_uX_v\bigr).
\]
Thus, constructing an $\varepsilon$-packing amounts to finding a set
whose distinct elements satisfy
\[
    \mathbb E X_uX_v
    \le
    1-\frac{\varepsilon^2}{2}.
\]

Recall the overlaps $q_n(u,v)$ from the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:pstab-thermodynamic-limit}.
Fix $\delta\in(0,1/2)$. We will construct a set
$\mathcal C_{n,\delta}\subseteq\mathcal A^n$ such that for all distinct
$u,v\in\mathcal C_{n,\delta}$, $|q_n(u,v)|\le1-\delta$.
For every integer $p\ge2$,
\[
    q_n(u,v)^p
    \le |q_n(u,v)|^p
    \le (1-\delta)^p.
\]
Together with \eqref{eq:pstab-with-replacement} and
$G_n(u)=\sqrt n\,X_u$, this gives
\[
    \mathbb E X_uX_v
    \le
    (1-\delta)^p+\frac{p(p-1)}n
    =:
    \beta_n.
\]
Consequently, for all sufficiently large $n$,
$\mathcal C_{n,\delta}$ is a
$\sqrt{2(1-\beta_n)}$-packing in the canonical metric.

To construct this set, note that the quantity $q_n(u,v)$ can be close to
$1$ when $u$ and $v$ are close, and close to $-1$ when $u$ and $-v$
are close. We must therefore keep each pair separated. Accordingly, for
$u,v\in\mathcal A^n$ define
\[
    d_{\pm}(u,v)
    :=
    \min\{d_H(u,v),d_H(u,-v)\},
\]
where $d_H$ denotes Hamming distance. Let $r=\lfloor\delta n\rfloor$.

For $w\in\mathcal A^n$, write the radius-$r$ Hamming ball
\[
    B_H(w,r)
    :=
    \{v\in\mathcal A^n:d_H(w,v)\le r\}.
\]
Since $d_H(u,-v)=d_H(-u,v)$,
\[
    \{v\in\mathcal A^n:d_{\pm}(u,v)\le r\}
    =
    B_H(u,r)\cup B_H(-u,r).
\]
To construct a vector at Hamming distance exactly $k$ from $w$, one
chooses the $k$ coordinates to be changed and, at each such coordinate,
one of the five elements of $\mathcal A$ different from the original
entry. Hence
\[
    |B_H(w,r)|
    =
    \sum_{k=0}^r\binom nk5^k
    :=V_6(n,r).
\]
The standard $6$-ary Hamming-volume estimate gives
\[
    V_6(n,r)
    \le
    \exp\left\{
        n\bigl(h(\delta)+\delta\log5\bigr)
    \right\},
\]
where $h(\delta) := -\delta\log\delta-(1-\delta)\log(1-\delta)$; see \cite[Proposition~3.3.3]{guruswami2025essential}.

We now construct $\mathcal C_{n,\delta}$ greedily by adapting the argument in \cite[Sec.~4.2.1]{guruswami2025essential}. Initialize
$\mathcal C_{n,\delta}=\emptyset$ and let
$\mathcal R=\mathcal A^n$ be the set of available points. While
$\mathcal R$ is nonempty, choose any $u\in\mathcal R$, add $u$ to
$\mathcal C_{n,\delta}$, and remove from $\mathcal R$ every $v$
satisfying $d_{\pm}(u,v)\le r$. Continue until $\mathcal R$ is empty. Each selected
point removes at most $2V_6(n,r)$ points. Since all $6^n$ points of
$\mathcal A^n$ have been removed when the procedure terminates,
\[
    |\mathcal C_{n,\delta}|
    \ge
    \frac{6^n}{2V_6(n,r)}.
\]
Moreover, any two distinct selected points satisfy
$d_{\pm}(u,v)>r$. Since $d_{\pm}(u,v)$ is integer-valued and
$r=\lfloor\delta n\rfloor$, this implies $d_{\pm}(u,v)>\delta n$.

The Hamming-volume bound therefore gives
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:pstab-code-rate}
    \frac1n\log|\mathcal C_{n,\delta}|
    \ge
    \log6-h(\delta)-\delta\log5-\frac{\log2}{n}.
\end{equation}
It remains to verify that the Hamming separation gives the desired separation in the canonical metric. Fix distinct $u,v\in\mathcal C_{n,\delta}$ and define
\[
N_+(u,v) := \bigl|\{i:u_i=v_i\}\bigr|,
\qquad N_-(u,v) := \bigl|\{i:u_i=-v_i\}\bigr|.
\]
Since
\[
d_H(u,v)=n-N_+(u,v), \qquad d_H(u,-v)=n-N_-(u,v),
\]
the inequality $d_{\pm}(u,v)>\delta n$ implies
\[
N_+(u,v)<(1-\delta)n, \qquad N_-(u,v)<(1-\delta)n.
\]
Moreover, $u_i\cdot v_i$ equals $1$, $-1$, or $0$ as $u_i=v_i$, $u_i=-v_i$, or neither. Hence
\[
|q_n(u,v)|
= \frac{|N_+(u,v)-N_-(u,v)|}{n}
\le
\frac{\max\{N_+(u,v),N_-(u,v)\}}{n} < 1-\delta.
\]
Thus $\mathcal C_{n,\delta}$ has the covariance separation claimed above, i.e. $\mathbb E X_uX_v\le\beta_n$ for all distinct $u,v\in\mathcal C_{n,\delta}$.

Let $K_n:=|\mathcal C_{n,\delta}|$, and let $Z_0$ and $(Z_u)_{u\in\mathcal C_{n,\delta}}$ be independent standard Gaussian variables. For all sufficiently large $n$, we have $0\le\beta_n<1$, so define the comparison process
\[
Y_u := \sqrt{\beta_n}\,Z_0 + \sqrt{1-\beta_n}\,Z_u, \qquad u\in\mathcal C_{n,\delta}.
\]
The process $(Y_u)$ has variance one and pairwise covariance $\beta_n$. Consequently, for distinct $u,v\in\mathcal C_{n,\delta}$,
\[
\mathbb E(X_u-X_v)^2 = 2\bigl(1-\mathbb E X_uX_v\bigr) \ge 2(1-\beta_n) = \mathbb E(Y_u-Y_v)^2.
\]
Sudakov--Fernique \cite[Theorem~7.2.11]{vershynin2018high} therefore gives
\begin{align*}
\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n) &\ge \mathbb E\max_{u\in\mathcal C_{n,\delta}}X_u \\
&\ge \mathbb E\max_{u\in\mathcal C_{n,\delta}}Y_u \\
&= \sqrt{1-\beta_n}\, \mathbb E\max_{1\le j\le K_n}Z_j.
\end{align*}
The final equality holds because the term $\sqrt{\beta_n}Z_0$ is common to every $Y_u$ and has mean zero. The standard asymptotic for the maximum of independent standard Gaussian variables gives
\[
\mathbb E\max_{1\le j\le K_n}Z_j = (1+o_n(1))\sqrt{2\log K_n}.
\]
Since $\beta_n\to(1-\delta)^p$ as $n\to\infty$, it follows from \eqref{eq:pstab-code-rate} that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:pstab-lower-delta}
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\frac{\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)}{\sqrt n}
\ge \sqrt{ 2\bigl(1-(1-\delta)^p\bigr) \bigl( \log6-h(\delta)-\delta\log5 \bigr) }.
\end{equation}
For sufficiently large $p$, take $\delta=\frac{2\log p}{p}$. Then $\delta\in(0,1/2)$ and
\[
(1-\delta)^p \le e^{-p\delta} = p^{-2}.
\]
Moreover, using $h(\delta)\le\delta\log(e/\delta)$,
\[
h(\delta)+\delta\log5 \le \frac{2\log p}{p} \log\left(\frac{5ep}{2\log p}\right) \le C\frac{(\log p)^2}{p}.
\]
Substituting these estimates into \eqref{eq:pstab-lower-delta} gives
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\frac{\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)}{\sqrt n}
\ge \sqrt{2\log6} - C\frac{(\log p)^2}{p}.
\]
Taking $n\to\infty$ in \eqref{eq:pstab-upper} gives
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\frac{\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)}{\sqrt n}\le\sqrt{2\log6}.
\]
Combining the two estimates proves the claimed bounds. Letting $p\to\infty$ gives the result.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
Let $t_n=o(n)$ and set
$\mathcal C_n:=\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,t_n}$.
Corollary~\ref{cor:t-count-conditioning-benchmark} provides
the conditioning benchmark $\mathcal B_{n,t_n}$, while
Lemma~\ref{lem:t-count-profile-entropy} gives
$\Gamma_{n,p}=o(n^2)$ for every fixed $p$.
Applying
Theorem~\ref{thm:local-profile-complexity-principle}\textup{(ii)}
and then Lemma~\ref{lem:pstab-exceptional-site-cost}
gives \eqref{eq:t-count-product-stabilizer-comparison}.

It remains to prove the large-$p$ assertion. Fix $\varepsilon>0$.
By Proposition~\ref{prop:pstab-value}, for every sufficiently
large fixed integer $p$ and all sufficiently large $n$,
\[
    \left|
        \frac{\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)}{\sqrt n}
        -\sqrt{2\log6}
    \right|
    \le\frac{\varepsilon}{3}.
\]
Each product-stabilizer energy is a linear functional of the
Gaussian disorder with coefficient vector of norm one.
Their supremum is therefore $1$-Lipschitz, so Gaussian
concentration gives
\[
    \mathbb P\left(
        |M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)-\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)|>u
    \right)\le2e^{-u^2/2},
    \qquad u>0.
\]
Taking $u=(\varepsilon/3)\sqrt n$ and using
\eqref{eq:t-count-product-stabilizer-comparison}, we obtain,
with probability tending to one,
\begin{align*}
    \left|
        \frac{M_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n)}{\sqrt n}
        -\sqrt{2\log6}
    \right|
    &\le
    \frac{M_{n,p}(\mathcal C_n)-M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)}{\sqrt n}\\
    &+
    \frac{|M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)-\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)|}{\sqrt n}\\
    &+
    \left|
        \frac{\mathbb E M_{n,p}(\mathsf{pstab}_n)}{\sqrt n}
        -\sqrt{2\log6}
    \right|
    \le\varepsilon.
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- corollary-12: body_md -->
\label{cor:sharp-clifford-energy}
For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $p_\varepsilon\ge2$ such that,
for every fixed integer $p\ge p_\varepsilon$,
\[
    \mathbb P\left(
        \left|
            \frac{M_{n,p}(\mathsf{stab}_n)}{\sqrt n}
            -
            \sqrt{2\log6}
        \right|
        \le\varepsilon
    \right)
    \longrightarrow1
\]
as $n\to\infty$.
<!-- end corollary-12 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
Apply the large-$p$ assertion of
Corollary~\ref{cor:intro-t-count}\textup{(ii)} with $t_n=0$
and use \eqref{eq:t-count-zero-energy}.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
The constant $\sqrt{2\log6}$ reflects the six possible one-qubit
stabilizer states.  It does not conflict with the unrestricted
product-state value \cite{anschuetz2025bounds}, which grows with $p$, because arbitrary product
states may choose continuously many Bloch-sphere directions whereas
product stabilizer states have only six local choices.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{lem:growth-entropy}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$,
and let $\mathcal F\subseteq[-1,1]^\Omega$. Suppose that there exist a positive integer $d$ and
$A\ge1$ such that, for every $m\ge d$ and every
$\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_m\in\Omega$,
\[
  \#\{
    (f(\omega_1),\ldots,f(\omega_m)):
    f\in\mathcal F
  \}
  \le
  \left(\frac{Am}{d}\right)^d.
\]
Then, for every $0<\varepsilon<1$,
\[
  \log N(\varepsilon,\mathcal F,L_2(\mu))
  \le
  C d\log\left(\frac{eA}{\varepsilon}\right),
\]
where $C>0$ is a universal constant.
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
This is the standard approximation argument for classes with polynomial
restriction growth; see, for example,
\cite[Chapter~II, Lemma~25]{poll}.

If $\mathcal F=\emptyset$, there is nothing to prove, so
assume $\mathcal F\ne\emptyset$.  For completeness, apply the restriction-growth hypothesis to
a finite list containing every point of $\Omega$, with repetitions if
needed to make its length at least $d$.  It follows that $\mathcal F$
contains only finitely many distinct profiles, so we may choose a maximal
$\varepsilon$-separated family $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F$ in $L_2(\mu)$,
and write $M=|\mathcal G|$. Since
$\mathcal F\subseteq[-1,1]^\Omega$, any distinct $f,g\in\mathcal G$ satisfy
\[
    \mu\{f\ne g\}
    \ge \frac{1}{4}\|f-g\|_{L_2(\mu)}^2
    > \frac{\varepsilon^2}{4}.
\]
Take
$m:=d+\lceil8\varepsilon^{-2}\log(\max\{M,2\})\rceil$.  A union bound shows
that $m$ independent points sampled from $\mu$ distinguish every pair
in $\mathcal G$ with positive probability. For such a sample, the restriction-growth assumption
gives $M\le (Am/d )^d$.

Writing $x=(\log M)/d$, the last inequality implies
$x\le\log(CA(1+x/\varepsilon^2))$.  If $x\le2$ there is nothing to prove;
if $x>2$, using $\log x\le x/2$ and rearranging gives
$x\le C\log(eA/\varepsilon)$.  Thus $\log M
    \le
    C d\log (eA/\varepsilon)$. Since a maximal $\varepsilon$-separated family is an $\varepsilon$-net, the result follows.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-stabilizer-nullity-decomposition}
Let $|\eta\rangle$ be a pure $M$-qubit state with
$\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\eta)=t$.
There exists $V\in\mathsf{cliff}_M$ such that
\[
    V\mathcal G_\eta V^\dagger
    =\langle Z_{t+1},\ldots,Z_M\rangle.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
    V\mathcal K_\eta
    &=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes t}
      \otimes\operatorname{span}\{|0^{M-t}\rangle\},\\
    V\Pi_\eta V^\dagger
    &=I_{2^t}\otimes|0^{M-t}\rangle\langle0^{M-t}|.
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, there is a pure $t$-qubit state $|\chi\rangle$
such that
\[
    V|\eta\rangle=|\chi\rangle\otimes|0^{M-t}\rangle,
    \qquad \mathsf S(\chi)=\{0\}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
Choose generators $G_1,\ldots,G_{M-t}$ whose labels form a
basis of $\mathsf S(\eta)$. Since this subspace is
isotropic, we can complete these labels to a symplectic
basis. Mapping this basis to the standard symplectic
basis, with a suitable ordering, gives an invertible
linear map $F$ preserving the symplectic inner product
and satisfying
\[
    F([G_j])=[Z_{t+j}],
    \qquad j=1,\ldots,M-t.
\]
By \eqref{eq:app-clifford-symplectic-action}, there is
$V_0\in\mathsf{cliff}_M$ implementing this map on Pauli labels.
Consequently,
\[
    V_0G_jV_0^\dagger=\varepsilon_jZ_{t+j},
    \qquad \varepsilon_j\in\{\pm1\}.
\]
Since $XZX=-Z$, the Clifford
\[
    V:=\left(\prod_{j:\,\varepsilon_j=-1}X_{t+j}\right)V_0
\]
corrects all signs, so that
$VG_jV^\dagger=Z_{t+j}$ for every $j$.
Because the $G_j$ generate $\mathcal G_\eta$, this proves
the claimed group identity.

The common $+1$ eigenspace of $Z_{t+1},\ldots,Z_M$
consists of arbitrary states on the first $t$ qubits
tensored with $|0^{M-t}\rangle$.
This gives the stated eigenspace and projector formulas.
Since $|\eta\rangle\in\mathcal K_\eta$, it also gives
the factorization of $V|\eta\rangle$.

Finally, suppose that a nonidentity Pauli $P$ satisfies
$P|\chi\rangle=\varepsilon|\chi\rangle$ for some
$\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}$. Then
\[
    V^\dagger(\varepsilon P\otimes I)V
    \in\mathcal G_\eta.
\]
This contradicts the group identity, since
$\varepsilon P\otimes I$ acts nontrivially on the first
$t$ qubits, whereas every element of
$\langle Z_{t+1},\ldots,Z_M\rangle$ acts trivially there.
Thus $\mathsf S(\chi)=\{0\}$. If $t=M$, then $\mathsf S(\eta)=\{0\}$, and we may
simply take $V=I$ and $|\chi\rangle=|\eta\rangle$.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-stabilizer-pauli-action}
Let $\mathcal G$, $S$, $t$, and $V$ be as above, and let
$R\in\mathcal P_M^\pm$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
    \item If $[R]\notin S^\perp$, then
    $\Pi_{\mathcal G}R\Pi_{\mathcal G}=0$.

    \item If $[R]\in S^\perp$, then $R$ preserves
    $\mathcal K_S$ and
    \[
        VRV^\dagger=\varepsilon_RP_R\otimes B_R,
        \qquad
        P_R\in\mathcal P_t,\quad
        \varepsilon_R\in\{\pm1\},\quad
        B_R\in\{I,Z\}^{\otimes(M-t)}.
    \]
    Its action after decoding is therefore
    \[
        VRV^\dagger
        \bigl(|u\rangle\otimes|0^{M-t}\rangle\bigr)
        =(\varepsilon_RP_R|u\rangle)
          \otimes|0^{M-t}\rangle.
    \]
    The map $[R]+S\mapsto[P_R]$ is a linear symplectic
    bijection from $W_S$ to $\mathbb F_2^{2t}$.
    Thus two preserving Paulis have the same action on
    $\mathcal K_S$ up to sign if and only if their labels
    belong to the same coset of $S$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
For \textup{(i)}, choose $G\in\mathcal G$ anticommuting
with $R$. Since $G\Pi_{\mathcal G}=\Pi_{\mathcal G}$,
\[
    \Pi_{\mathcal G}R\Pi_{\mathcal G}
    =\Pi_{\mathcal G}GR\Pi_{\mathcal G}
    =-\Pi_{\mathcal G}RG\Pi_{\mathcal G}
    =-\Pi_{\mathcal G}R\Pi_{\mathcal G}.
\]
For \textup{(ii)}, the signed Pauli $VRV^\dagger$ commutes
with $Z_{t+1},\ldots,Z_M$, so its last $M-t$ factors are
$I$ or $Z$. These factors fix $|0^{M-t}\rangle$, giving
the stated logical action. Conjugation by $V$, followed by
restriction of binary labels to the first $t$ qubits, defines
a linear map $S^\perp\to\mathbb F_2^{2t}$ with kernel $S$.
It is surjective, since
$V^\dagger(P\otimes I)V$ realizes every $P\in\mathcal P_t$.
It preserves the symplectic form because the discarded
$I,Z$ factors commute pairwise. This proves the quotient
identification and the final assertion.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-local-symplectic}
Let $t\ge0$ be an integer, and let
$\overline X_1,\overline Z_1,\ldots,
\overline X_t,\overline Z_t\in\mathcal P_M^\pm$
be $t$ pairs of signed Pauli operators supported on
$\Lambda\subseteq[M]$, satisfying
\[
\begin{aligned}
    \langle[\overline X_i],[\overline X_j]\rangle_{\mathrm{sp}}
    &=\langle[\overline Z_i],[\overline Z_j]\rangle_{\mathrm{sp}}=0,\\
    \langle[\overline X_i],[\overline Z_j]\rangle_{\mathrm{sp}}
    &=\delta_{ij},\qquad i,j\in[t].
\end{aligned}
\]
Then $t\le|\Lambda|$. For any distinct designated qubits
$\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_t\in\Lambda$, there is a Clifford $C$
supported on $\Lambda$ such that
\[
    C\overline X_jC^\dagger=X_{\ell_j},
    \qquad C\overline Z_jC^\dagger=Z_{\ell_j},
    \qquad j\in[t].
\]
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Restrict the labels to $\mathbb F_2^{2|\Lambda|}$.
The displayed pairings show that these $2t$ vectors are
independent and span a nondegenerate symplectic subspace
$U$. Hence $t\le|\Lambda|$, and a symplectic basis of
$U^\perp$ completes them to one of the full label space.
The Clifford--symplectic correspondence gives a Clifford
$C_0$ supported on $\Lambda$ with
\[
    C_0\overline X_jC_0^\dagger=(-1)^{a_j}X_{\ell_j},
    \qquad
    C_0\overline Z_jC_0^\dagger=(-1)^{b_j}Z_{\ell_j},
    \qquad a_j,b_j\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Set $Q:=\prod_{j=1}^tX_{\ell_j}^{b_j}Z_{\ell_j}^{a_j}$
and $C:=QC_0$. Conjugation by $Q$ corrects both signs
independently for each $j$, giving the required identities.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-nullity-conditioning}
Let $|\psi\rangle$ be a pure $M$-qubit state.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
    \item For every $P\in\mathcal P_M^\pm$ and
    $\theta\in\mathbb R$,
    \[
        \nu_{\mathrm{st}}(e^{-i\theta P}\psi)
        \le\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\psi)+1.
    \]
    In particular, a $T$-gate increases nullity by at most one.

    \item Measure one qubit in a Pauli basis, as in the
    Pauli POVM defined in
    Section~\ref{subsubsec:pauli-povm}.
    Condition on any outcome of positive probability
    and discard the measured qubit. The remaining qubits
    are then in a pure state $|\psi'\rangle$ satisfying
    \[
        \nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\psi')
        \le\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\psi).
    \]

    \item For the one-qubit reduced density matrices
    $\psi_i:=\operatorname{Tr}_{[M]\setminus\{i\}}|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$,
    \[
        \#\{i\in[M]:\psi_i\notin\operatorname{conv}(\mathsf{pstab}_1)\}
        \le\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\psi).
    \]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
Let $S:=\mathsf S(\psi)$ and $k:=\dim S$.
For \textup{(i)}, every $G\in\mathcal G_\psi$ commuting
with $P$ also stabilizes $e^{-i\theta P}|\psi\rangle$,
since
\[
    Ge^{-i\theta P}|\psi\rangle
    =e^{-i\theta P}G|\psi\rangle
    =e^{-i\theta P}|\psi\rangle.
\]
The labels of these operators form $S\cap[P]^\perp$,
whose dimension is at least $k-1$, because commutation
with $P$ imposes at most one linear constraint.
Thus the output nullity is at most
$M-(k-1)=\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\psi)+1$.
The $T$-gate claim follows from
$T_i=e^{i\pi/8}e^{-i\pi Z_i/8}$.

For \textup{(ii)}, the normalized state conditional on
the measurement outcome $s$, before discarding the
measured qubit, is
\[
    |\phi\rangle
    :=\frac{(I+sP)|\psi\rangle}
            {\|(I+sP)|\psi\rangle\|},
    \qquad P=a_i,\quad a\in\{X,Y,Z\},\quad s\in\{\pm1\}.
\]
If $[P]\in S$, then $|\psi\rangle$ is an eigenvector
of $P$, and the only positive-probability outcome
leaves the state unchanged.

If $[P]\notin S$, every $G\in\mathcal G_\psi$ commuting
with $P$ also stabilizes $|\phi\rangle$, since $G$
commutes with $I+sP$. The labels of these operators
form $S\cap[P]^\perp$, whose dimension is at least $k-1$.
Moreover, $P|\phi\rangle=s|\phi\rangle$, so $sP$ is
a stabilizer of $|\phi\rangle$. Its label $[P]$ lies
outside $S$ and therefore gives an additional
independent stabilizer.

In either case, $\dim\mathsf S(\phi)\ge k$, so
$\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\phi)\le\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\psi)$; see
~\cite[Proposition~2.3]{beverland2020lower}.
The conditional state is the tensor product of the
measured qubit's pure Pauli eigenstate and the pure
state $|\psi'\rangle$ on the remaining qubits.
The Pauli eigenstate has nullity zero, so tensor
additivity gives
$\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\psi')=\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\phi)$.

For \textup{(iii)}, let $F$ be the sites on which every
element of $\mathcal G_\psi$ acts trivially. If $i\notin F$,
choose $G\in\mathcal G_\psi$ with a nonidentity factor
$a\in\{X,Y,Z\}$ at $i$. For each $b \in \{X,Y,Z\} \setminus \{a\}$, the operator $b_i$ anitcommutes with $G$, so
\[
    \langle\psi|b_i|\psi\rangle
    =\langle\psi|Gb_iG|\psi\rangle
    =-\langle\psi|b_i|\psi\rangle=0.
\]
Hence, for some $\alpha\in[-1,1]$,
\[
    \psi_i
    =\frac{I+\alpha a}{2}
    =\frac{1+\alpha}{2}\frac{I+a}{2}
     +\frac{1-\alpha}{2}\frac{I-a}{2}.
\]
Since $(I+a)/2$ and $(I-a)/2$ are pure one-qubit
stabilizer states, $\psi_i\in\operatorname{conv}(\mathsf{pstab}_1)$.
All exceptional sites therefore lie in $F$. Restricting
$S$ to $F^c$ identifies it with an isotropic subspace on
$M-|F|$ qubits, so $k\le M-|F|$. Consequently,
\[
    \#\{i:\psi_i\notin\operatorname{conv}(\mathsf{pstab}_1)\}
    \le|F|\le M-k=\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\psi).
\]
This is the support-counting argument of
\cite[Lemma~9]{coble2023hamiltonians}, expressed in terms
of nullity.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- lemma-28: body_md -->
\label{lem:t-count-nullity-cost}
A projector $|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|$ belongs to
$\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{pure}}_{M,t}$ if and only if, up to
global phase,
\[
    |\Psi\rangle=R(P_s)\cdots R(P_1)|\phi\rangle,
    \qquad 0\le s\le t,
\]
where $|\phi\rangle$ is a pure stabilizer state and
$P_j\in\mathcal P_M^\pm\setminus\{\pm I\}$.
The empty product is the identity. Every such state has
$\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\Psi)\le t$.
<!-- end lemma-28 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
Replace each $T_i$ by $R(Z_i)$ up to phase and move
Clifford factors to the right using
$CR(P)=R(CPC^\dagger)C$; see
\cite[Proposition~1]{gosset2013algorithm}.
Conversely, every signed nonidentity Hermitian Pauli is
$P=VZ_1V^\dagger$ for a Clifford $V$, so
$R(P)=e^{-i\pi/8}VT_1V^\dagger$ uses one $T$-gate.
The nullity bound follows by iterating
Lemma~\ref{lem:app-nullity-conditioning}\textup{(i)}
from $\nu_{\mathrm{st}}(\phi)=0$.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- lemma-29: body_md -->
\label{lem:t-count-workspace-compression}
For integers $n\ge1$ and $t\ge0$, every state in
$\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,t}$ can be prepared using at most
$t$ $T$-gates on at most $2n+t$ total qubits. Equivalently,
\[
    \mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,t}
    =\left\{
        \operatorname{Tr}_{\{n+1,\ldots,2n+t\}}\omega:
        \omega\in\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{pure}}_{2n+t,t}
      \right\}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-29 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
Let $A=[n]$ index the retained qubits, and let $E$ index
the $r$ ancillary qubits discarded at the output.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:t-count-nullity-cost}, a preparation on
$M=n+r$ qubits has the form
\[
    \rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_E|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|,
    \qquad
    |\Psi\rangle=R(P_s)\cdots R(P_1)|\phi\rangle,
    \qquad s\le t,
\]
with $\phi$ a pure stabilizer state. Consider the stabilizers of $\phi$ supported on $E$
that commute with each $P_j$. Their labels form the
subspace
\[
    L:=\{(x,z)\in\mathsf S(\phi):x_A=z_A=0\}
       \cap\bigcap_{j=1}^s[P_j]^\perp.
\]
Since $\dim\mathsf S(\phi)=M$, the $2n$ support constraints
and $s$ commutation constraints give
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:t-count-environment-stabilizers}
    d:=\dim L\ge M-2n-s=r-n-s.
\end{equation}
Choose signed stabilizers $G_1,\ldots,G_d$ with labels
forming a basis of $L$. Apply the stabilizer-group
version of Lemma~\ref{lem:app-stabilizer-nullity-decomposition}
within $E$ to obtain a Clifford $V=I_A\otimes V_E$
acting only on the qubits in $E$ and sending these
generators to $Z_{e_1},\ldots,Z_{e_d}$.
Writing $E_0:=\{e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$ and $E':=E\setminus E_0$,
we have
\[
    V|\phi\rangle=|\phi'\rangle_{AE'}\otimes|0^d\rangle_{E_0},
    \qquad
    VP_jV^\dagger=P'_j\otimes Z^{z_j},
\]
where $\phi'$ is a pure stabilizer state,
$P'_j$ is a signed Hermitian Pauli on $AE'$, and
$Z^{z_j}\in\{I,Z\}^{\otimes d}$.
The first assertion follows from the $+1$ constraints
and nullity additivity. The second follows because each
$P_j$ commutes with all $G_\ell$.

Since $Z^{z_j}|0^d\rangle=|0^d\rangle$, for every vector
$|\xi\rangle$ on $AE'$,
\[
    R(VP_jV^\dagger)(|\xi\rangle\otimes|0^d\rangle)
    =R(P'_j)|\xi\rangle\otimes|0^d\rangle.
\]
Applying this successively gives
\[
    V|\Psi\rangle=|\Psi'\rangle_{AE'}\otimes|0^d\rangle_{E_0},
    \qquad
    |\Psi'\rangle:=R(P'_s)\cdots R(P'_1)|\phi'\rangle.
\]
As $V$ acts only on the discarded qubits,
$\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_{E'}|\Psi'\rangle\langle\Psi'|$.
The remaining width satisfies
\[
    M-d\le2n+s\le2n+t.
\]
Since $\phi'$ is a pure stabilizer state, it can be
prepared using only Clifford gates. Rotations with
$P'_j=\pm I$ change only the global phase and can be
omitted. By Lemma~\ref{lem:t-count-nullity-cost}, each
remaining rotation can be implemented using one $T$-gate
and Clifford gates. This prepares $\rho_A$ on at most
$2n+t$ qubits using at most $s\le t$ $T$-gates.

Adding unused ancillary qubits initialized in $|0\rangle$
gives a preparation on exactly $2n+t$ qubits without
changing $\rho_A$ or the $T$-count. Conversely, every
$n$-qubit state obtained from such a preparation by
discarding the ancillary qubits belongs to
$\mathsf{cliffT}^{\mathrm{anc}}_{n,t}$ by definition.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
